item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
MWCD and MSDE to jointly launch NAVYA 2.0 in Haridwar on 28 November 2026
Joint initiative to empower adolescent girls and young women through skills, confidence-building and livelihood opportunities across 100 districts in 24 States/UTs
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) will jointly launch the second phase of NAVYA – Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls (NAVYA 2.0) on 28 November 2026 at 3:30 PM at the Uttarakhand Sanskrit Academy Auditorium, Haridwar. Building on the learnings of its pilot phase, NAVYA 2.0 aims to advance women-led development by nurturing the aspirations of adolescent girls and young women, strengthening their capabilities and enabling them to achieve greater confidence, self-reliance and economic independence.

The programme will be graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon’ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development; Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; Smt. Rekha Arya, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister for Women Empowerment and Child Development, Food and Civil Supplies, Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Madan Kaushik, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister of Panchayati Raj, Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, Ayush and Ayush Education, Reorganization and Census, Government of Uttarakhand; and Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Uttarakhand.

The launch programme will feature the formal launch of NAVYA 2.0 by the Hon’ble Union Ministers. It will also include the inauguration of Saksham Anganwadi Centres and new Anganwadi Centres constructed under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand, and distribution of certificates to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

NAVYA: Nurturing aspirations and enabling empowerment

NAVYA is a collaborative initiative of MWCD and MSDE that brings together the strengths of the women and child development and skill development ecosystems to empower adolescent girls and young women. The initiative recognises that empowerment goes beyond training and entails nurturing aspirations, building confidence, developing capabilities and enabling informed choices about the future.

The pilot phase was launched on 24 June 2025 in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh, with an envisaged coverage of 27 Aspirational Districts across 19 States. Approximately 1,200 adolescent girls were trained in industry-relevant job roles such as Drone Manufacturing and Assembly Technician, Solar PV Installation Helper and Fashion Designer. The initiative also emphasised digital and financial literacy, career readiness and entrepreneurship to strengthen their confidence and socio-economic independence.

NAVYA 2.0: Expanding the horizons of empowerment

Building on the pilot experience, NAVYA 2.0 will expand its reach to 100 districts across 24 States/UTs, with a particular focus on aspirational and hard-to-reach areas. The eligible age group has also been widened from 16–18 years to 16–25 years, bringing a larger cohort of adolescent girls and young women within its ambit.

The expanded initiative will provide greater access to vocational training in industry-relevant, new-age and non-traditional job roles, while strengthening pathways to employment, apprenticeships and entrepreneurship. It places emphasis on institutional convergence, coordinated district-level implementation and outcome-oriented support. A structured Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has also been introduced to facilitate effective coordination and implementation at the district level.

Technology-enabled implementation

The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) will serve as the digital platform for facilitating access to skilling opportunities and supporting candidates throughout their journey from enrolment to training and certification. It will also enable real-time tracking of beneficiary registration, attendance, training progress and certification, strengthening transparency and accountability. Digitally verifiable credentials will further help candidates demonstrate their skills and competencies.

Advancing women-led development

Through the convergence of MWCD and MSDE, NAVYA 2.0 seeks to create an enabling ecosystem where adolescent girls and young women, particularly from aspirational and underserved regions, can realise their potential, pursue their aspirations and participate meaningfully in economic and social development.

NAVYA 2.0 is a step towards transforming aspirations into opportunities and opportunities into empowerment, enabling every young woman to shape her own future and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

*****

RC/SM

item.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported continuous rise in TB cases in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh amidst Tuberculosis Free India campaign
item.dc:creator: National Human Rights Commission
item.description: National Human Rights Commission NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported continuous rise in TB cases in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh amidst Tuberculosis Free India campaign Reportedly, only 1.43 lakh out of 1.77 lakh registered patients in 2024 received a single instalment of financial assistance of Rs. 1,000 per month under a government nutrition scheme The Commission issues a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 8:06PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported continuous rise in TB cases in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh amidst Tuberculosis Free India campaign
Reportedly, only 1.43 lakh out of 1.77 lakh registered patients in 2024 received a single instalment of financial assistance of Rs. 1,000 per month under a government nutrition scheme
The Commission issues a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report regarding the continuous rise in the number of registered tuberculosis (TB) patients in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Reportedly, registered TB patients in Bhopal have increased by about 19 per cent from 10,773 in 2022 to 12,850 in 2024. According to the media report, these figures have emerged even as there is a Tuberculosis Free India campaign going on in the country. Further, only 1.43 lakh out of 1.77 lakh registered patients in 2024 reportedly received a single instalment financial assistance of Rs. 1,000 per month under a government nutrition scheme, as per Madhya Pradesh Economic Survey. The remaining did not receive a single instalment.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violations. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

According to the media report, carried on 26th November 2026, about 1.72 lakh cases of TB and 4,733 deaths were reported across the State in 2025.

*****

item.title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported suicide of two prisoners within a span of seven days at two jails in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
item.dc:creator: National Human Rights Commission

item.content:encoded:
National Human Rights Commission
NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported suicide of two prisoners within a span of seven days at two jails in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh
Issues notices to the Director General of Prisons, Uttar Pradesh and District Magistrate, Lucknow, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 8:05PM by PIB Delhi

The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken suo motu cognizance of a media report of 26th November 2026 that within a span of seven days, two prisoners died by suicide at two jails in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Reportedly, an undertrial prisoner and another serving life imprisonment were found hanging at District Jail and Model Jail on 19th and 25th November 2026, respectively.

The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued notices to the Director General of Prisons, Uttar Pradesh and District Magistrate, Lucknow, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.

The Commission also noted that the custodial deaths had not been reported to it within 24 hours as per its guidelines. Therefore, it has sought an explanation from the concerned authorities within 24 hours as to why no intimation was sent about these custodial deaths to the NHRC.

*****

NSK

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
Prime Minister meets Foreign Ministers and Heads of Delegation of IORA Member-States in New Delhi
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi

The Prime Minister today met the Foreign Ministers and Heads of Delegation of the 23 Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA) Member-States, who are in New Delhi to participate in the 25th Meeting of the IORA Council of Ministers.

Highlighting the millennia-old historical and cultural ties fostered by the Indian Ocean, the Prime Minister reaffirmed India’s commitment as the Chair of IORA to working closely with all member partners. He emphasised that India looks forward to advancing its vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) to further strengthen peace, security, stability, and shared prosperity across the Indian Ocean Region.

The Prime Minister posted on X:

"Delighted to meet the Foreign Ministers and Heads of Delegation of the 23 Indian Ocean Rim Association Member-States participating in the 25th Meeting of the IORA Council of Ministers in New Delhi.

The Indian Ocean has connected our people for millennia. As Chair of IORA, India looks forward to working closely with all partners to advance its vision of MAHASAGAR (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and to strengthen peace, security, stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region.

@IORAofficial"

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Inaugurates Advanced Spectral CT Facility at NIMHANS, Bengaluru; Reviews Key Mental Healthcare and Brain Health Initiatives
Smt. Srivastava Reviews NIMHANS’ Suicide Prevention Programmes and Capacity-Building Initiatives to Strengthen the Mental Health Workforce Across Four Professional Disciplines
Tele-MANAS Crosses 50 Lakh Calls; Expansion of Helpline Integration, Counsellor Training, Quality Assurance and Technology-Enabled Mental Health Services Reviewed
NIMHANS Centre for Addiction Medicine Treats 25,913 Individuals Between January and October 2026; Strengthens Telemedicine Follow-ups, Specialised Treatment and Nationwide Outreach
NIMHANS suicide prevention initiatives reach 37 government hospitals across Karnataka; 31,557 survivors receive interventions under Urban Self-Harm Study
Karnataka Brain Health Initiative (KaBHI), Developed by NIMHANS and State Government with NITI Aayog's Consultation, Conducts 2.61 Lakh Screenings and Treats 32,630 Patients; MoHFW task Force Proposes National- Level Replication
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi

Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava inaugurated and dedicated an advanced Spectral CT facility at the Emergency Block of the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, today. During her visit, the Secretary reviewed the Institute's major initiatives and its contributions to national efforts in mental healthcare, suicide prevention, addiction treatment, capacity building and brain health.

The newly commissioned facility is equipped with the Revolution Apex Elite CT scanner from GE, a 256-detector-row system featuring advanced spectral imaging and AI-based image reconstruction. Designed to support comprehensive neurological, cardiac, vascular and whole-body imaging for both adults and children, the scanner will operate round the clock to cater to the substantial patient load at the Emergency Department.

The advanced imaging system is expected to strengthen emergency diagnostics, particularly in stroke and neurovascular care, where timely and accurate diagnosis is critical. It enables rapid identification of brain haemorrhage, arterial blockages and other life-threatening conditions, while also supporting the evaluation of cardiac and vascular disorders, post-interventional complications, polytrauma and other complex medical conditions.

Review of National Mental Healthcare Initiatives

During the visit, the Secretary reviewed the progress of Tele-MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States), which has crossed the milestone of 50 lakh calls. The programme has steadily expanded its reach through integration with other helplines, nationwide awareness initiatives, counsellor training and accreditation, quality assurance measures and technology-enabled services. Its five-year vision for 2027–32 focuses on expanding access, enhancing service quality and integrating Tele-MANAS more closely with the broader healthcare system.

The Secretary also reviewed the activities of the Centre for Addiction Medicine (CAM), NIMHANS, one of the six centres supported under the Ministry's Tobacco Control and Drug De-addiction Programme. Between January and October 2026, the Centre provided treatment to 25,913 individuals with addictive disorders, with more than 7,000 receiving telemedicine follow-ups.

Its specialised services include opioid substitution treatment, neuromodulation, counselling and tele-aftercare. The Centre also reaches healthcare professionals across the country through digital training and e-learning programmes. Its Addiction Rx mobile application has recorded approximately 19,600 downloads across 145 countries. Community outreach activities include initiatives under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan and the Tobacco Quitline, which has received over 36,000 calls. The Centre is working towards expanding its training programmes and digital consultation services, alongside developing AI-enabled tools to facilitate early identification of addiction, particularly among young people.

Strengthening Professional Capacities and Suicide Prevention

The review also covered the NIMHANS–CIP–LGBRIMH Capacity Building Programme, undertaken in collaboration with the Central Institute of Psychiatry (CIP), Ranchi, and Lokopriya Gopinath Bordoloi Regional Institute of Mental Health (LGBRIMH), Tezpur. The programme aims to strengthen professional capacities in Psychiatry, Clinical Psychology, Psychiatric Social Work and Psychiatric Nursing.

Another key area of review was the work of the NIMHANS Suicide Prevention, Research, Implementation, Training and Engagement (N-SPRITE) Centre, aligned with the four pillars of the National Suicide Prevention Strategy (2022).

The Centre's Urban Self-Harm Study (USHAS) has recorded 42,382 cases since 2022, with 31,557 survivors receiving interventions and a reported re-attempt rate of 1.3%. The Centre is now operational in 37 government hospitals across Karnataka. It also implements SURAKSHA, YASHAS and EMPOWER, focusing on community, youth and workplace suicide prevention.

Smt. Srivastava was also apprised of the recently launched Wellness Centre, NIMHANS Student Mental Health Services. The Centre provides dedicated counselling, psychotherapy and psychiatric support to students through a multidisciplinary team. Its services include structured short-term therapy, referrals for long-term care wherever needed and psychiatric consultations twice a week.

Advancing Brain Health and Emergency Neurological Care

The discussions also covered NIMHANS' efforts to strengthen brain health and neurological care across Karnataka. The Karnataka Brain Health Initiative (KaBHI), of NIMHANS and the State government, developed with NITI Aayog’s consultation, focuses on the early detection, prevention and treatment of neurological disorders. The initiative has conducted 2.61 lakh screenings and provided treatment to 32,630 patients.

The National Task Force on Brain Health, constituted by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, has proposed KaBHI as a model for national-level initiatives. Complementing these efforts, the proposed Hub and Spoke Model for Head Trauma and Stroke Care in Karnataka aims to improve access to timely emergency neurological care through regional hubs and coordinated referral networks. The proposed model includes a Neurohub at KMCRI, Hubballi, and an Acute Stroke Emergency and Assessment Centre at NIMHANS.

The Government of India remains committed to strengthening comprehensive and accessible healthcare, with mental health forming an integral part of this effort. Through initiatives spanning early diagnosis, treatment, suicide prevention, addiction care, professional capacity building and brain health, the Ministry continues to support efforts towards improving access to quality healthcare services and strengthening the mental healthcare ecosystem across the country.

*****

SR
HFW/Union Health Secretary Inaugurates Advanced Spectral CT Facility at NIMHANS/27th November 2026/1

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
At 57th IFFI, a Story of How the Entire Crew of ‘The River Train’ Stepped into a Child’s World
The Argentine Feature Brings Together Childhood Dreams and the Spirit of Collaboration
‘The River Train’ captures the universal desire to explore the unknown and find one’s own path in life
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:40PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

The cast and crew of the Spanish language film The River Train (El Tren Fluvial), - producer Valentine Torre and actor Rita Pauls - spoke about how trust, friendship and sensitivity shaped the making of the film at a press conference organized today on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Directed by Lorenzo Ferro and Lucas A. Vignale, the 75-minute Spanish-language feature from Argentina had its India premiere in the International Competition section of IFFI 2026.

Set in the Argentine Pampas, the film follows nine year old Milo, who trains in Malambo, a traditional Argentine folk dance, but dreams of travelling by train to Buenos Aires, a city he knows only through films. As he ventures out on his own, unfamiliar encounters and moments of loneliness lead him to discover a world beyond the expectations placed upon him. His journey explores childhood, freedom and the challenges of pursuing one’s dreams.

Recalling the origins of the project, Mr. Torre said it began as an informal invitation among friends to make a small film. What started as a modest undertaking gradually grew into a feature through mutual trust and collective effort, eventually reaching international audiences at film festivals in Berlin, San Sebastián and Buenos Aires.

Ms. Pauls, who plays the Professor in the film, spoke about working with Milo Barría, a young Malambo dancer with no previous acting experience. Rather than expecting the child to adapt to the demands of a conventional film set, the crew adjusted its working methods to his needs and moods, she said. She explained that this flexibility allowed the young actor to remain at the centre of the creative process.

Speaking about the film’s visual style, the producer explained that the 4:3 aspect ratio was inspired from the directors’ admiration for classic cinema while also helping the team work within its production budget. The use of black-and-white imagery in parts of the film evokes the atmosphere of older cinema and lends a dreamlike quality to the narrative.

Looking ahead, Mr.Torre shared that the team plans to begin shooting Plan de fuga, a road film about two brothers, in 2027. He also spoke about the recent theatrical release of The River Train in Spain and expressed hope for future filmmaking collaborations in India.

Through Milo’s journey, The River Train captures the universal desire to explore the unknown and find one’s own path in life. Its making also offers a reminder that meaningful cinema can emerge from modest beginnings when creative ambition is matched by empathy and collective effort.

The session was moderated by Anushka Sarkar.

item.title: ‘I Came as a Jury Member, but Became a Student of Cinema’: Aanand L Rai on the Golden Peacock Jury Experience at 57th IFFI
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting ‘I Came as a Jury Member, but Became a Student of Cinema’: Aanand L Rai on the Golden Peacock Jury Experience at 57th IFFI Filmmakers must remain responsive to changes in cinematic grammar, irrespective of the language in which they work: Aanand L Rai, Jury Chairperson, International Competition, at 57th IFFI Deliberations on Award Selection Were Organic, Decisions Unanimous: IFFI International Competition Jury Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:26PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 27 November 2026 International Jury Chairperson and…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
‘I Came as a Jury Member, but Became a Student of Cinema’: Aanand L Rai on the Golden Peacock Jury Experience at 57th IFFI
Filmmakers must remain responsive to changes in cinematic grammar, irrespective of the language in which they work: Aanand L Rai, Jury Chairperson, International Competition, at 57th IFFI
Deliberations on Award Selection Were Organic, Decisions Unanimous: IFFI International Competition Jury
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:26PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

International Jury Chairperson and Indian filmmaker Aanand L Rai, along with fellow jury members, addressed a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in Goa today on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI). Reflecting on their experience of evaluating 15 feature films competing for the Golden Peacock Award, the jury members spoke about the diversity of cinematic voices, the exchange of cultural perspectives and the evolving language of cinema.

Describing the experience as an opportunity to learn, Rai said that watching films from different countries and cultures, followed by discussions among jury members, offered insights into the creative choices and cultural contexts behind each work. “I came as a jury member, but while watching the films I became a student of cinema,” he said.

Explaining the jury's deliberations, Rai said the selection process was shaped by open and candid discussions, without any predetermined approach or consideration of the countries of origin of the films. He described the process as organic, with members freely sharing their responses and perspectives. “Actually, it went very organic for me. I really don't know how to put it, but we just spoke our hearts out, that's it,” he said. He added that the discussions were healthy and enriching, with members often finding common ground while bringing different perspectives to the same cinematic moments.

Emphasising that cinema is a constantly evolving art form, Rai said filmmakers must remain responsive to changes in cinematic grammar, irrespective of the language in which they work. “A film is an experience, an experience of an emotion or expression of it. Each film should do something to you. You would not be the same after watching it; it should change something within you.” he said. He added that cinematic grammar was ultimately shaped by filmmakers rather than languages.

Thai filmmaker Ratchapoom Boonbunchachoke, who returned to IFFI after his film was screened as the closing film at the previous edition, highlighted how the diverse backgrounds of jury members enriched their discussions. He said the emotional impact of a film mattered more than technical brilliance alone. “It matters how the filmmaker used the technique to emotionally impact the audience,” he observed.

Colombian sound designer María Alejandra Rojas described the experience as particularly meaningful from the perspective of a professional working in post-production. She said the deliberations were intellectually stimulating, with even the moments of silence following screenings adding depth to the discussions.

Argentinian filmmaker and screenwriter Sol Berruezo Pichon-Rivière appreciated the plurality of voices represented in the festival's selection. She noted that IFFI offered a platform to films from diverse countries, cultures and production scales, including works that may not have featured prominently in major international festival circuits.

Romanian writer-director and producer Bogdan Mureșanu described the overall selection as unusually strong and noted the remarkable convergence of tastes among jury members from different parts of the world. Recalling their discussions after screenings, he said, “We talked immediately after each film about what we liked or what we disliked. We were still immersed in the stories and we had this pleasure to be there a bit more till we jumped to another journey.” He also highlighted the value of listening to fellow jury members and discovering different perspectives on the films.

The jury members' reflections underscored the role of international film festivals in bringing diverse cinematic traditions into conversation and creating opportunities for shared learning and appreciation.

The press conference was moderated by Shri Rajith Chandran.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Ministry of Women and Child Development marks two years of 'Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' Campaign
National level event reinforces collective resolve towards a Child Marriage Free India
States/UTs and stakeholders join the programme at Vigyan Bhawan and through webcast
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Women and Child Development today marked two years of the 'Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' Abhiyaan through a national-level programme at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, in the august presence of the Hon'ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon'ble Chief Minister of Delhi, Smt. Rekha Gupta, and Hon'ble Minister of State for Women and Child Development, Smt. Savitri Thakur.

The programme brought together representatives of States/UTs, Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs), Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), Ministries and Departments, legal services institutions, international organisations and civil society organisations. It was also webcast to enable officials, frontline functionaries and stakeholders across the country to join the national event. During the programme, participants also took a collective pledge, reaffirming their resolve to work towards making India free from child marriage.

Speaking on the occasion, the Hon'ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi,​ “Our goal is to ensure that every child in the country gets a safe childhood, every daughter gets the opportunity for education, and they become capable of making their own life decisions—and we have pledged that child marriage will not happen in our home, our neighborhood, or anywhere in the country.” She reiterated that ending child marriage requires sustained action through a 'whole-of-government' and 'whole-of-society' approach and emphasised the importance of education, skilling and empowerment of girls in realising the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047.

Smt. Savitri Thakur, Hon’ble Minister of State for Women and Child Development, emphasised the importance of grassroots participation and community-led efforts, highlighting the role of Panchayats, frontline functionaries and community leaders in preventing child marriage. “A Child Marriage Free India is not just a target for 2030; it is an essential step toward realizing the vision of a Developed India (Viksit Bharat) by 2047 under the leadership of the Honorable Prime Minister.”

Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Delhi, called for coordinated efforts by the Government and communities to eliminate child marriage, promote girls’ education and safeguard the rights of children. “A daughter will only progress when we give her the blessing that we will not snatch the book from her hand, we will not marry her off early, and we will give her respect and equal opportunities to move forward.”

The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Campaign was launched on 27 November 2024 with the objective of making Child Marriage Free Bharat. The Campaign focuses on awareness generation, community participation, strengthening the role of CMPOs, timely reporting and intervention, and supporting adolescent girls who are school dropouts or at risk of child marriage through education, skilling and empowerment.

Over the past two years, the Campaign has developed into a sustained nationwide effort. The awareness programmes had reached over 12 crore citizens, while more than 42 lakh pledges had been registered across the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal, MyGov and MY Bharat platforms. The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal had also emerged as a centralised repository of more than 72,000 Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs) across States and Union Territories. The observance is also being held during the ongoing 100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Awareness Module 2.0, from 21 October to 21 December 2026, aimed at intensifying awareness, mobilisation and coordinated action against child marriage across the country.

Around 700 persons participated in the programme at Vigyan Bhawan. Wider participation was facilitated through webcast, enabling stakeholders across States and Union Territories to join the programme and the nationwide pledge against child marriage. Around 47000 people watched the event via webcast.

The Campaign complements implementation of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 by strengthening the capacity of CMPOs and other duty-bearers and encouraging timely reporting and intervention. Citizens can report incidents, take the pledge and access information and resources through the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal at https://stopchildmarriage.wcd.gov.in/ .  Child Helpline 1098, Emergency Response Support System 112 and Women Helpline 181 are also available for assistance and timely intervention.

As Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat completes two years, the Ministry called upon citizens, communities, institutions and all stakeholders to make prevention of child marriage a shared national responsibility and ensure that every child is able to pursue education and realise their full potential.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) wins Bronze Medal for display at India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026
More than 1 lakh people visit the CBIC Pavillion across age groups, professions and sectors, reflecting strong public interest in CBIC’s reform and facilitation initiatives
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

In recognition of its sustained outreach efforts, engaging public-facing formats and citizen-centric communication, the GST & Customs Pavilion of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has been awarded the Bronze Medal for Display at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today.

CBIC showcased its flagship ‘GST & Customs Pavilion’ at IITF 2026 from 14th–27th November 2026. The Pavilion was inaugurated on 16th November 2026 by Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, in the presence of Members of the Board and senior officers.

Aligned with the fair’s theme “Vikas aur Virasat”, the Pavilion focused on creating awareness about the Next-Gen GST Process Reforms, the updated Baggage Rules, 2026 and CBIC’s digital initiatives. Designed as an interactive and educational space, it served as a single-point public interface where taxpayers, traders, exporters and importers, students, travellers and citizens could understand recent changes in tax and customs procedures and the benefits available to them.

More than 1 lakh people visit the CBIC Pavillion across age groups, professions and sectors, reflecting strong public interest in CBIC’s reform and facilitation initiatives.

Key highlights of the CBIC Pavilion

1. Expert helpdesks for on-the-spot assistance 8 dedicated helpdesks covering GST, Customs, GSTN, Invoice Registration Portal (IRP), ICEGATE and CPGRAMS, manned by officers and domain experts, assisted visitors with GST registration, return filing, refunds, e-invoicing, customs procedures, baggage provisions, import-export facilitation and grievance redressal.

2. Awareness on Next-Gen GST Process Reforms and Baggage Rules, 2026 Special emphasis was placed on explaining the Next-Gen GST Process Reforms and the updated Baggage Rules, 2026, helping taxpayers and international travellers understand the simplified procedures and their entitlements.

3. Interactive digital exhibits Digital displays and educational material showcased CBIC’s technology-driven transformation, highlighting greater transparency, efficiency and ease of compliance. [Educational videos and tutorials were available in X regional languages besides Hindi and English.]

4. Engaging Awareness Activities Virtual Reality (VR) games, mechanical games like catch the baton and gold bar, ventriloquist and puppet shows, coloring competition for kids and interactive quizzes, magic shows, Augmented Reality (AR) selfie zones, regional dances, Nukkad Nataks (street plays) made tax and customs awareness fun and accessible for visitors of all ages, especially children and youth.

CBIC expresses its gratitude to all visitors, stakeholders and partners for their enthusiastic participation and reaffirms its commitment to simplifying taxes, enhancing transparency and building a more citizen-friendly indirect taxation and customs ecosystem.

item.title: Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme Provides Financial Assistance of up to ₹ 3.50 Lakh to SC and ST Patients for Treatment of Life-Threatening Diseases
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme Provides Financial Assistance of up to ₹ 3.50 Lakh to SC and ST Patients for Treatment of Life-Threatening Diseases SC and ST Patients with Annual Family Income of up to ₹5 Lakh Eligible for Medical Assistance under the Revised Scheme Scheme Covers Heart Surgery, Kidney Surgery, Dialysis, Cancer Treatment, Brain Surgery, Organ Transplantation, Spinal Surgery and Other Life-Threatening Diseases Eligible Beneficiaries To Log In https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme Provides Financial Assistance of up to ₹ 3.50 Lakh to SC and ST Patients for Treatment of Life-Threatening Diseases
SC and ST Patients with Annual Family Income of up to ₹5 Lakh Eligible for Medical Assistance under the Revised Scheme
Scheme Covers Heart Surgery, Kidney Surgery, Dialysis, Cancer Treatment, Brain Surgery, Organ Transplantation, Spinal Surgery and Other Life-Threatening Diseases
Eligible Beneficiaries To Log In https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi

The Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is implementing the revised ‘Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme’, providing financial assistance of up to ₹3.50 lakh to eligible patients belonging to the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) suffering from serious and life-threatening diseases.

Director DAF Shri Vinesh Pachnanda said the revised scheme, notified on June 2, 2026, aims to improve access to specialised healthcare services and reduce the financial burden of medical treatment on economically vulnerable families. It seeks to ensure that financial constraints do not become a barrier to accessing essential medical treatment and surgical interventions, he said.

Shri Pachnanda said under the revised provisions, individuals belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes whose annual family income does not exceed ₹5 lakh are eligible to apply for financial assistance.

The scheme covers serious ailments related to the kidney, heart, liver, brain and cancer, besides organ transplantation, spinal surgery and other life-threatening diseases requiring medical or surgical intervention, he added.

Under the scheme, 100% of the estimated cost of surgery or covered treatment, subject to the prescribed financial ceiling, is released directly to the concerned hospital, Shri Pachnanda added.

The Director said the maximum financial assistance admissible is ₹1.50 lakh for heart surgery, ₹3.50 lakh for kidney surgery or dialysis, ₹2.50 lakh for cancer surgery, chemotherapy or radiotherapy, ₹2 lakh for brain surgery, ₹3.50 lakh for kidney or organ transplantation, ₹1.50 lakh for spinal surgery and ₹2 lakh for other life-threatening diseases.

The financial assistance may be released in a single instalment before surgery directly to the concerned hospital through RTGS, NEFT or Demand Draft, thereby reducing the immediate financial burden on patients and their families, the Director added.

Recognising the financial challenges associated with prolonged medical treatment, the revised scheme also enables patients suffering from chronic ailments to seek a second renewal grant in the subsequent financial year, subject to the applicable provisions, he said.

Shri Pachnanda further said a significant provision of the revised scheme is the inclusion of beneficiaries covered under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) who are suffering from renal diseases or require kidney or organ transplantation.

Such beneficiaries are also eligible to seek medical assistance under the Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme while other patients covered under PM-JAY are not eligible for assistance under the scheme, he clarified.

To facilitate access to specialised medical treatment across the country, the scheme is implemented through a wide network of recognised healthcare institutions, including the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, and AIIMS in other States, all Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)-approved hospitals, hospitals attached to State Government medical colleges, State Government hospitals, hospitals recognised by State Governments and hospitals fully funded by the Central or State Governments, Shri Pachnanda informed.

The scheme also covers Government hospitals located at district headquarters and major towns where facilities for the treatment of serious and life-threatening diseases, including organ transplantation and spinal surgery, are available, he added.

Shri Pachnanda informed several specialised healthcare institutions, including Sanjay Gandhi Post Graduate Institute, Lucknow; Patna Medical College Hospital, Patna; Jabalpur Hospital and Research Centre, Jabalpur; B. Barua Cancer Institute, Guwahati; Birla Heart Foundation, Kolkata; Kalinga Hospital, Bhubaneswar; Tata Cancer Research Institute, Mumbai; Nizam Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad; and the Voluntary Health Services, Chennai, are also covered under the scheme.

In exceptional circumstances, treatment at other hospitals may be considered, subject to the satisfaction of the Chairman of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation regarding the merits of the case, he said.

He clarified that applications seeking reimbursement of expenditure already incurred on surgery or medical treatment are ordinarily not entertained. However, reimbursement may be considered on the merits of the case if the application was received by the Foundation at least 15 days before the scheduled date of surgery, he added.

Shri Pachnanda said to ensure transparency and accountability in the utilisation of financial assistance, the concerned hospital is required to submit a Utilisation Certificate along with the final medical bills at the time of discharge of the patient.

The medical aid released to the hospital must be utilised within one month of its release, and any unutilised or balance amount must be returned to the Foundation at the earliest, but not later than one month after the date of discharge of the patient, he said.

The Director DAF informed that eligible beneficiaries may apply for medical assistance through the prescribed application form available on the official website of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF) https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/

or submit an application on plain paper containing the requisite details as specified in the prescribed format.

The application must be accompanied by self-attested copies of the latest income certificate, caste certificate and ration card or Aadhaar card of the patient, along with a self-attested passport-size photograph. Applicants are also required to submit the original Estimated Cost Certificate, duly signed by the Medical Superintendent of the concerned hospital, indicating the estimated cost of treatment and the scheduled date of surgery.

In cases involving kidney transplantation, applicants are required to furnish additional documents relating to the relationship between the donor and the beneficiary, the prescribed Form 14 pertaining to the decision of the Authorisation Committee and relevant particulars of the kidney donor. The bank account details of the concerned hospital, including the account number, name of the account holder and IFSC code, may also be provided to facilitate the timely processing and direct transfer of financial assistance.

The duly completed application, along with the requisite documents, must reach the Director, Dr. Ambedkar Foundation, 15, Janpath, New Delhi – 110001, at least 15 days before the scheduled date of surgery, dialysis or chemotherapy.

The Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme serves as an important intervention in addressing the financial barriers faced by economically vulnerable families belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in accessing specialised healthcare services. By extending financial assistance for critical medical interventions, the scheme seeks to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure and facilitate timely access to essential healthcare.

Eligible beneficiaries and their family members are encouraged to avail themselves of the benefits under the scheme. Healthcare institutions, State Government departments, social welfare organisations and other stakeholders are also encouraged to disseminate information about the scheme to ensure wider awareness among eligible beneficiaries.

For detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria, recognised hospitals and prescribed application forms, interested applicants may visit the official website of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation.

https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/

The implementation of the revised Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme reinforces the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to promoting social justice, equitable access to healthcare, financial security and the dignity and well-being of disadvantaged communities, towards the realisation of an inclusive Viksit Bharat@2047.

item.title: ‘The Villain Is Not Always an Individual, but a Reflection of Society’: Karthik Subbaraj at 57th IFFI
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting ‘The Villain Is Not Always an Individual, but a Reflection of Society’: Karthik Subbaraj at 57th IFFI Filmmaker explores morality, patriarchy and cinema’s potential to challenge social prejudices Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:11PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 27 November 2026 Renowned filmmaker Karthik Subbaraj explored the complexities of morality, the societal roots of villainy and cinema’s potential to challenge prejudice during an interview session titled “ What If the Villain Is Right?” at the 57th International Film…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
‘The Villain Is Not Always an Individual, but a Reflection of Society’: Karthik Subbaraj at 57th IFFI
Filmmaker explores morality, patriarchy and cinema’s potential to challenge social prejudices
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 7:11PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

Renowned filmmaker Karthik Subbaraj explored the complexities of morality, the societal roots of villainy and cinema’s potential to challenge prejudice during an interview session titled “What If the Villain Is Right?” at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Moderated by film critic Sudhir Srinivasan, the session examined how his films challenge conventional distinctions between good and evil.

Observing that human behaviour is shaped by circumstances and social experiences, Subbaraj said, “The base is grey for everyone.” He explained that the people individuals encounter and the situations they experience influence how they are perceived as good or bad.

Discussing his film Dorothy, Subbaraj distinguished between characters who consciously commit evil and those whose harmful behaviour stems from deeply ingrained social conditioning. While Whistle Veeraiya represents an overtly evil character, he suggested that figures such as the parotta shop owner could be more dangerous because they fail to recognise their own prejudices and wrongdoing.

Subbaraj said Dorothy portrays masculinity and patriarchal attitudes as the forces behind the protagonist’s death, positioning an oppressive mindset, rather than a single individual, as the real antagonist. Drawing a parallel with Mercury, he explained how the collective mentality of a village is portrayed negatively, showing how individual acts of villainy can emerge from wider social attitudes.

Reflecting on humiliation and accountability, the filmmaker observed that ridicule and laughter directed at someone's inability can be more hurtful than reprimand. He also spoke about remorse and guilt as forms of punishment, noting that the consequences of one's actions need not always take the form of physical harm or death.

On cinema's ability to influence society, Subbaraj recalled audience responses to Dorothy, including moments when viewers embraced transgender people and men were moved to tears. Such reactions, he said, reinforced his belief that films can go beyond entertainment to foster empathy and encourage social change. He added that the idea of bringing about change through storytelling had also informed his approach to Jigarthanda.

Throughout the conversation, Subbaraj emphasised his reluctance to portray characters as entirely virtuous heroes or irredeemably evil villains. By leaving moral judgments open to interpretation, he invites audiences to examine characters and their motivations from their own perspectives.

The session offered insights into Subbaraj’s cinematic approach, in which villainy is often rooted not merely in individuals, but in the social attitudes and structures that shape them.

Subbaraj’s reflections underscored cinema’s ability to look beyond conventional notions of good and evil, encouraging audiences to question ingrained prejudices and engage with complex social realities. Resonating with the theme of the 57th International Film Festival of India, ‘Stories Without Borders’, his approach to storytelling highlights how narratives rooted in specific social and cultural contexts can raise universal questions about morality, empathy and human behaviour.

Director Kamakhya Narayan Singh and producer Ravindra Sanghavi shared…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Filmmakers Share the Creative Journeys behind The Kerala Story 2 : Goes Beyond and Demography Is Destiny at IFFI 2026
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:50PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

The importance of character-driven narratives, research-based filmmaking and the power of cinema to bring diverse stories to audiences came into focus at a press conference held on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) today. Director Kamakhya Narayan Singh and producer Ravindra Sanghavi shared insights into the making of The Kerala Story 2 : Goes Beyond and the documentary Demography Is Destiny, discussing research, character development and the challenges of presenting complex subjects through cinema.

Sharing his experience of directing The Kerala Story 2, Kamakhya Narayan described the film as a character-driven narrative, noting that bringing together multiple stories while maintaining a common emotional thread was both a challenge and a rewarding experience. He highlighted the role of music in connecting the different narratives, explaining that despite the film exploring three separate stories, a shared emotional core helped bind them together.

Narayan also said that the film draws upon case studies and factual references, with the intention of presenting its narrative through the experiences and emotions of its characters.

Speaking about Demography Is Destiny, producer Ravindra Sanghavi and director Kamakhya Narayan highlighted the challenges of translating empirical data into an engaging cinematic narrative. Kamakhya explained that finding relatable characters is essential to making complex information accessible to audiences. Drawing on his experience as a documentary filmmaker, Kamakhya said his process generally begins with data collection and interviews, followed by identifying individuals whose experiences can help shape the narrative.

He also spoke about the importance of visual authenticity in filmmaking, including selecting locations that lend credibility to the story. His travel experiences and familiarity with different places helped him identify suitable locations, to recreate the desired visual setting.

The speakers also reflected on the role of social media in helping films reach wider audiences, while emphasising that their respective creative journeys were driven by the desire to tell stories they considered meaningful.

The discussion also turned to the role of IFFI in providing a platform for films from different regions, languages and production backgrounds. Singh observed that the festival enables filmmakers working with varied budgets and resources to present their work on the same platform. He recalled how IFFI had introduced him to international cinema and filmmakers early in his career, well before digital streaming platforms became widely available.

Singh described the festival's theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, as closely aligned with its long-standing role in bringing diverse cinematic voices together. The platform, he said, allows films from smaller regions and lesser-known languages to reach wider audiences.

The Press Conference was moderated by Kuldeep Meena.

item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Portuguese Film ‘Come With Me’ Explores Friendship and the Shared Experience of Cinema at 57th IFFI Filmmakers discuss the enduring appeal of theatrical viewing, universal themes and the evolving relationship between art-house and mainstream cinema Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:41PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 27 November 2026 Director João Lameira, actor António Simão and producer Daniel Pereira addressed a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in Goa today on the sidelines of the 57th…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Portuguese Film ‘Come With Me’ Explores Friendship and the Shared Experience of Cinema at 57th IFFI
Filmmakers discuss the enduring appeal of theatrical viewing, universal themes and the evolving relationship between art-house and mainstream cinema
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:41PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

Director João Lameira, actor António Simão and producer Daniel Pereira addressed a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) in Goa today on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), following the World Premiere of their Portuguese film Come with Me (Anda daí), featured in the Cinema of the World section. The filmmakers discussed the film’s themes of friendship, its art-house sensibility and the continuing relevance of the theatrical experience amid the growth of streaming platforms.

Emphasising the importance of watching films together, actor António Simão expressed concern over declining cinema audiences in Portugal and the growing preference for watching films at home. He said cinema-going was also about meeting people and sharing a collective cultural experience. “People need to be together and talk and see each other,” he said, adding, “Long live cinema.”

Producer Daniel Pereira reaffirmed his commitment to theatrical exhibition, noting that his production and distribution company continues to prioritise cinema releases. While acknowledging the influence of streaming platforms, he viewed them as complementary to, rather than a replacement for, the theatrical experience.

Speaking about the film, director João Lameira said that although its story is rooted in Lisbon and its cultural setting, its central theme of male friendship is intended to resonate with audiences across geographical and cultural boundaries. “I hope the story and the characters are universal enough to be understood by everyone,” he said, adding that the specificity of the setting and characters could itself help audiences connect with the story.

Lameira also clarified that he had not approached the film with a particular classification, such as art-house or mainstream cinema, in mind. His intention was to make the film he wanted to make while hoping that audiences would appreciate it. Pereira observed that the distinction between art-house and mainstream cinema had evolved over time, noting that films with distinctive directorial perspectives and compelling stories were once more accessible to wider audiences.

Reflecting on his approach to acting, Simão spoke about how personal experiences, observation and imagination shape a performance. Drawing on his extensive theatre background, he said the character initially felt close to his own life, making him conscious of the personal experiences he might bring to the role. He eventually moved beyond these concerns to focus on the character’s circumstances and actions.

The filmmakers also expressed their appreciation for presenting the film’s World Premiere at IFFI. Acknowledging the historical and architectural connections between Portugal and Goa, they said that while some aspects of the region felt familiar, the overall experience remained culturally distinct. They welcomed the opportunity to explore Goa and share their work with Indian audiences.

The press conference was moderated by Smt. Vishali P.

item.title: Virtual Bharat Explores India’s Diverse Storytelling Traditions and the Global Power of Indian Cinema at IFFI 2026
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Virtual Bharat Explores India’s Diverse Storytelling Traditions and the Global Power of Indian Cinema at IFFI 2026 Bharat Bala and Dhiraj Singh underline the importance of authentic narratives, creative freedom and technology in taking Indian stories to the world Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:27PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 27 November 2026 A panel discussion on Virtual Bharat explored India’s diverse storytelling traditions, creative freedom and the evolving landscape of cinema on the sidelines of the 57th International…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Virtual Bharat Explores India’s Diverse Storytelling Traditions and the Global Power of Indian Cinema at IFFI 2026
Bharat Bala and Dhiraj Singh underline the importance of authentic narratives, creative freedom and technology in taking Indian stories to the world
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:27PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

A panel discussion on Virtual Bharat explored India’s diverse storytelling traditions, creative freedom and the evolving landscape of cinema on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) today. The session featured Bharat Bala, acclaimed filmmaker and Dhiraj Singh, an Indian Information Service (IIS) officer currently serving as Vice Chancellor of the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune and Managing Director (Additional Charge), National Film Development Corporation (NFDC). Vani Tripathi Tikoo, actor, producer, theatre practitioner and cultural leader, conceptualised and moderated the session.

The engaging discussion explored the importance of authentic grassroots narratives and India's growing presence in international cinema, with Vani Tripathi Tikoo sharing her perspectives and bringing depth and direction to the conversation.

‘Filmmakers must first recognise and bring forth the stories within their own country’

Speaking about his creative philosophy, Bala said he did not differentiate between music videos, short films, feature films, fiction and non-fiction, emphasising that storytelling and creative expression must remain central to every format.

Reflecting on his work over the past five years, he spoke about taking cameras to the remotest corners of the country, engaging with real people, building their trust and providing them with a platform to share their own stories. He emphasised that the essence of filmmaking lies in capturing authentic human experiences rather than imposing preconceived narratives.

Highlighting the Virtual Bharat initiative, which brings together 143 films on a cloud-based platform, Bala underscored India’s extraordinary cultural and geographical diversity as an immense source of untold stories. He observed that filmmakers must first recognise and bring forth the stories within their own country to establish a meaningful global presence. “Bharat is the new global,” he remarked, emphasising that authentic narratives rooted in India’s lived experiences can resonate with audiences across the world.

‘Artistic expression draws its strength from human experiences’

Noting that the country possesses a vast audience base and an extraordinary reservoir of stories, Dhiraj Singh reflected on India’s potential to emerge as a stronger voice in global storytelling. He stressed the need for Indian cinema to draw from its own cultural ethos rather than remain confined by external perceptions and influences. Reflecting on the relationship between cinema, art and reality, he observed that artistic expression draws its strength from human experiences and eventually creates its own world.

Singh said the purpose of Film Festivals extends beyond screening films. Festivals, he noted, introduce audiences to the wider world of cinema, nurture cinematic appreciation and provide emerging filmmakers with opportunities to learn, interact and showcase their work. He also highlighted IFFI’s initiatives to engage young talent, including students from the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, and the Film and Television Institute (FTI), Arunachal Pradesh. Providing students with exposure, creative opportunities and a platform to engage with the cinematic community, he said, was an important aspect of film education.

The discussion also addressed the growing influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) on the creative industries. Responding to concerns about AI replacing creative professionals, Singh said that rather than being apprehensive, creators must remain alert to technological developments and undertake timely course corrections. He emphasised that human creativity and artistic expression cannot be replaced, as art ultimately emerges from human imagination and experience.

Bala welcomed AI as an evolving technology that could expand creative possibilities and open new avenues for filmmakers. However, he maintained that storytelling remains fundamentally rooted in human creativity and originality. He said technological advancements should encourage creators to become more innovative and push the boundaries of original storytelling.

The discussion highlighted the growing importance of platforms such as Virtual Bharat in bringing India’s diverse and authentic stories to the forefront, while reaffirming the role of film festivals in nurturing talent, encouraging creative exchange and strengthening India’s presence on the global cinematic stage.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
MoSJE Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Records Sales of Approximately ₹2.07 Crore As on November 26; Strong Public Response Boosts Artisans’ Livelihoods
Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase India’s Rich Cultural Heritage , Traditional Craftsmanship, Strengthens Market Linkages, Entrepreneurship and Economic Empowerment
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹2.07 crore up to November 26, 2026, reflecting an encouraging response from visitors and strong consumer appreciation for indigenous products, traditional craftsmanship and the entrepreneurial talent of artisans from across the country.

Located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, the Ministry’s pavilion has emerged as a vibrant platform for showcasing India’s diverse cultural heritage, traditional skills and indigenous craftsmanship. The enthusiastic participation of visitors and their purchases have provided direct market access to artisans and contributed to strengthening their livelihood opportunities.

The Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 reinforces its commitment to promoting inclusive economic development, preserving traditional craftsmanship, strengthening grassroots entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities towards the realisation of the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

The participation of these Apex Corporations reflects the Ministry’s continued commitment to strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs), he said.

The Official said the pavilion features an extensive collection of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products.

He said representing the distinctive artistic identities and cultural diversity of different regions, these products provide visitors an opportunity to experience and appreciate India's rich traditions of craftsmanship.

The encouraging sales performance underscores the importance of national-level exhibitions in enabling traditional artisans to enhance the visibility of their products, interact directly with customers, understand evolving consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore new market opportunities, the Official said.

He added participation in such prestigious platforms also help artisans strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities, expand their customer base and build sustainable business prospects.

A significant highlight of the Ministry’s participation is the promotion of TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), which aims to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among consumers, the Official added.

Through this initiative, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation and create sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, he said.

The Official said the Ministry’s efforts are aligned with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi under the guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’, fostering inclusive growth, economic empowerment and equitable development.

The Official remarked the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, brought together producers, entrepreneurs, traders and consumers from across the country and abroad, providing a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange.

The Ministry’s pavilion has provided participating artisans with valuable exposure, enhanced market access and opportunities to connect with consumers.

The encouraging response and sales achieved during the fair reaffirm the importance of providing traditional artisans with platforms to showcase their skills, promote their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Second Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 concludes at Agra, Emphasising Sustainability, Community Ownership and Gram Panchayat-led Water Governance
Senior Officials Visit Water Supply Infrastructure and Participate In Jal Arpan Diwas Celebrations Across Five Villages in Uttar Pradesh
Participating States/UTs reaffirm their commitment towards accelerating implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:09PM by PIB Delhi

The second regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0, organised by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, concluded today at Agra, Uttar Pradesh. The conference brought together representatives of seven northern States and Union Territories to deliberate on key strategies for accelerating implementation, strengthening sustainability and ensuring long-term functionality of rural drinking water supply systems

As part of the two-day regional conference, Shri Ashok K. K. Meena, Secretary, Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, today visited rural drinking water supply infrastructure and participated in the Jal Arpan Diwas celebration at Badhera (Bhadaira) W/S Scheme and 456 MLD WTP, Etah.

In the valedictory session, Secretary, DDWS emphasised that the Regional Conference had provided an important platform for States/UT to develop a common understanding of the reforms envisaged under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and to learn from one another's experiences. Referring to the field visits undertaken during the day, he highlighted innovative practices observed in Uttar Pradesh, including the use of solar energy for rural water supply schemes and command-and-control systems for monitoring and operation of water supply infrastructure, and encouraged States to examine such practices for wider replication.

Highlighting that rural drinking water service delivery is fundamentally a local service, Shri Meena stressed the importance of strengthening ownership of water supply assets by Gram Panchayats and local communities. He noted that Jal Arpan represents an important step towards transferring responsibility and ownership of drinking water infrastructure to communities and underscored the need to build the financial, technical and institutional capacities of Gram Panchayats for sustained service delivery.

He said that infrastructure creation must be complemented by effective management, regular water quality surveillance and community participation. He reiterated the need for convergence among Departments of Panchayati Raj, Rural Development, Skill Development and Drinking Water to strengthen operation and maintenance, build local capacities and promote source sustainability through initiatives such as Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari. He called upon States to move towards sustainable, community-owned and efficiently managed rural drinking water systems while strengthening Gram Panchayats as the foundation of Viksit Villages and Viksit Bharat.

Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM called for digital mapping of all drinking water supply infrastructure and highlighted the importance of leveraging existing institutional platforms for capacity building and strengthening Gram Panchayat-led water governance. He informed that a joint initiative has been undertaken by DDWS and the Ministry of Panchayati Raj to align training programmes under SBM-G with the existing capacity-building framework under Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA).

He emphasised that integrating water and sanitation-related training modules into ongoing Panchayati Raj training programmes would help strengthen the capacities of Sarpanches, Panchayat Secretaries and other grassroots functionaries. He urged States to enhance coordination with Panchayati Raj institutions and utilise existing training ecosystems to build awareness, strengthen community ownership and improve long-term management of rural drinking water supply systems.

 

 

Summarising the key outcomes of the two-day deliberations, Shri D. Senthil Pandiyan, Joint Secretary, DDWS, noted that ensuring sustainable rural drinking water services requires a whole-of-government approach and cannot be achieved by a single department alone. He highlighted the importance of convergence among departments dealing with drinking water, Panchayati Raj, Rural Development, Tribal Affairs and Skill Development for effective implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 reforms.

Shri Pandiyan called for working towards strengthened Gram Panchayat ownership of water supply infrastructure, capacity building of VWSCs and Sujalam Shakti, digital monitoring through the Sujalam framework, water quality surveillance, source sustainability, Jal Arpan, and institutional mechanisms for long-term operation and maintenance. He also appreciated the exchange of best practices by participating States and called upon them to undertake timely implementation of the agreed reform measures and action plans.

During the concluding day of the conference, Shri Vijay Kumar, Director, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, highlighted the opportunities available under the 16th Finance Commission framework for strengthening rural drinking water service delivery and sustainability. He emphasised the importance of mapping water supply infrastructure on the e-GramSwaraj portal, integrating drinking water priorities into Gram Panchayat Development Plans and effectively utilising Finance Commission grants for operation, maintenance and management of rural water supply assets. He also encouraged States to strengthen Panchayat planning processes and maximise the benefits of performance-linked grants through improved local governance and service delivery outcomes.

Field Visits and Jal Arpan Diwas Celebrations

Five teams comprising senior officials from the Government of India, participating States and Union Territories, partner Ministries and technical institutions visited rural drinking water supply schemes and participated in Jal Arpan ceremonies across Uttar Pradesh. The visits covered the Badhera (Bhadaira) Water Supply Scheme in Etah district, Nagla Babu Water Supply Scheme in Hathras district, Simrau Water Supply Scheme in Mainpuri district, Shahpur Qutub Water Supply Scheme in Aligarh district and Sultanpur Water Supply Scheme in Hathras district.

The field visits were led by senior officials, including Ashok K K Meena, Secretary, DDWS, Shri. Kamal Kishore Soan, AS & MD, NJJM, D Senthil Paniyan, Joint Secretary, NJJM, Director and Deputy Secretary, NJJM along with representatives from SPM NIWAS and participating States/UTs. The teams observed water treatment and distribution systems, interactions with PRIs, Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), water quality testing with FTK by trained women and community participation in operation and maintenance of drinking water infrastructure.

During the field visit to villages on the occasion of Jal Arpan Diwas, Shri Ashok K.K.Meena, Secretary, DDWS and Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM drank water directly from household taps, reinforcing community confidence in the quality and safety of the drinking water being supplied. They encouraged officials to adopt similar practices during field visits to build public trust in rural drinking water services and emphasised that Jal Arpan should be communicated as a step towards shared responsibility for sustainable water service delivery, rather than merely the handover of infrastructure. He also underscored the need to reassure Gram Panchayats of continued technical support from implementing departments, particularly for major repairs and infrastructure breakdowns, to strengthen their confidence in managing village water supply systems.

During the Jal Arpan ceremonies, Gram Panchayats, VWSC members, Self Help groups, school children and community representatives participated in activities promoting water conservation, responsible water use and community ownership of drinking water assets. The events highlighted the importance of shared responsibility among communities, Gram Panchayats and implementing agencies for ensuring sustainable rural drinking water services.

Over the two days, discussions focused on implementation of reforms, source sustainability, operation and maintenance, skilling of local human resources, inter-ministerial convergence, financial sustainability and strengthening community ownership of rural drinking water infrastructure.

The Conference concluded with participating States/UTs reaffirming their commitment towards accelerating implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 and advancing the transition towards sustainable, community-owned and service-oriented rural drinking water systems. The insights emerging from the deliberations and field visits are expected to strengthen interstate learning, improve programme implementation and contribute to long-term water security in rural areas.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
DELIVERY OF VINDHYAGIRI DESIG (Y3024) (PROJECT 17A INDIGENOUS ADVANCED STEALTH FRIGATE)
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi

Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024), the seventh and final ship of Nilgiri class (Project 17A) and the third of the class built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd (GRSE), was delivered to the Indian Navy on 27 Nov 26 at GRSE, Kolkata, marking the successful culmination of Project 17A ship deliveries and a major milestone in achieving self-reliance in warship design and construction.

Project 17A frigates are versatile multi-mission platforms, designed to address current and future challenges in the maritime domain. Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the ship is a reincarnation of the erstwhile INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate, that was part of the Indian Navy fleet from 08 Jul 1981 to 11 Jun 2012, rendering 31 years of glorious service to the nation. This state-of-the-art frigate reflects a quantum leap in naval design, stealth, firepower, automation and survivability and is an admirable symbol of Aatmanirbharta in warship building.

Designed by the Warship Design Bureau (WDB) and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team (Kolkata), P17A frigates reflect a generational leap in indigenous ship design, stealth, survivability and combat capability. These ships feature an advanced suite of weapons and sensors compared to the P17 (Shivalik) class. The ships are configured with Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) propulsion plants, comprising a diesel engine and a gas turbine that drive a Controllable Pitch Propeller (CPP) on each shaft, and a state-of-the-art Integrated Platform Management System (IPMS). The potent and technologically advanced weapons and sensors suite significantly enhances the ships’ multi-dimensional warfare capabilities across anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine domains.

Delivery of Vindhyagiri marks a historic milestone wherein all seven P17A frigates have been delivered to the Indian Navy within a span of 23 months from the delivery of the first-of-class (INS Nilgiri) on 20 Dec 24 (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2086668). Furthermore, the institutional experience gained from the construction of preceding six P17A ships enabled a significant compression of the build period of Vindhyagiri to 68 months, in comparison to 84 months taken for the first-of-class (INS Nilgiri). Delivery of Vindhyagiri showcases the design, ship construction and engineering prowess of the nation and reflects Indian Navy’s unrelenting focus of Aatmanirbharta in both ship design and ship building. With an indigenisation content of 75%, the project has involved over 200 MSMEs and has enabled employment generation of approx. 4000 personnel directly and more than 10000 personnel indirectly.
