Three friends…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Revisiting 2001: Filmmakers Who Took Hindi Cinema in New Directions Reunite 25 Years Later
“Cinema Is a Mirror to Society; I Believe in Exploring Real Life Rather Than Reel Life”: Madhur Bhandarkar
“How an actor listens and reacts to a cue is very important”: Ashutosh Gowariker
“Be Fearless, Leave Your Ego Behind and Tell Your Own Story”: Farhan Akhtar on the Art of Filmmaking
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 6:01PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 27 November 2026

 

A village takes on an empire with a game of cricket. Three friends navigate friendship, heartbreak and the uncertainties of growing up. And a filmmaker turns the camera towards women and realities society often chooses to ignore. Three films with unconventional stories, 2001 was one of the most remarkable years in Hindi cinema.

Lagaan, Dil Chahta Hai and Chandni Bar didn't just entertain; they challenged conventions, broke new ground and changed the cinematic conversation. While Lagaan celebrated the spirit of rebellion, Dil Chahta Hai captured the mood of a generation, and Chandni Bar brought attention to women and lives often left unseen.

Twenty-five years later, the creative mavericks behind these iconic films—Ashutosh Gowariker, Farhan Akhtar and Madhur Bhandarkar reunited at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Goa, for ‘The Legendary 25s’, a session that celebrated films that dared to break the mould and creators who chose to follow their own path.

“AI May Change Filmmaking, But It Cannot Replace the Human Soul”

Championing cinema as a reflection of society, filmmaker Madhur Bhandarkar reiterated his commitment to telling stories drawn from real life, particularly those that bring untold narratives and overlooked realities to the forefront. Recalling the challenges of advocating for female-centric subjects at a time when the industry was hesitant to embrace unconventional portrayals of women, he spoke about how films like Chandni Bar, Corporate and Fashion emerged from his conviction to portray women in all their complexities, vulnerabilities and strengths. “I have always wanted to make films about subjects that people hesitate to talk about or even explore. I am drawn to the stories behind the scenes, the realities that often remain hidden from the public eye. For me, cinema has always been a mirror to society. I would rather explore real life than create an idealised reel life,” he said.

Emphasising the importance of creative courage and conviction, Bhandarkar urged filmmakers to remain true to the stories they believe in rather than be influenced by prevailing industry trends or audience expectations. He also reflected on the growing role of technology in filmmaking, acknowledging that AI and visual effects could open up exciting new dimensions in visual storytelling. However, he firmly maintained that technology could never replace the human element that gives cinema its emotional depth.

“AI and VFX can certainly enhance the visual experience and expand the possibilities of filmmaking, but they can never replace the human touch. Technology can create images, but it cannot replicate human emotions, sensitivity and the emotional connect that breathe life into a character,” he added.

 

“Every Film Is a Reset to Zero. The Magic of Acting Lies in the Silence Between Words.”

Reflecting on his creative journey, Ashutosh Gowariker described every new film as a “reset to zero”, requiring a fresh perspective, an open mind and the willingness to rediscover the art of storytelling. Highlighting the challenges faced by unconventional cinema, he said, “Anything that is new, different or unconventional needs more time to find its audience. We must not judge a film only by its opening weekend.”

Sharing his insights into the craft of acting, he emphasised the importance of listening, expressions and pauses in bringing a character to life. “For me, a true performance lies in the pauses. Listening is one of the most important qualities of an actor. How an actor listens and reacts to a cue is equally important,” he said.

Reiterating that filmmakers should trust their stories rather than presume what audiences want, he stressed the importance of allowing viewers to form their own interpretations.

 

“Tell Your Story Fearlessly. Leave Your Ego at the Door.”

Championing originality and creative fearlessness, Farhan Akhtar urged aspiring filmmakers to trust their instincts and tell stories that reflect their own vision. Emphasising the importance of breaking away from conventional thinking, he said, “A director or writer must keep an open heart and mind, and leave their ego behind. Be fearless, believe in your vision and tell the story you truly want to tell.”

Describing a screenplay as a “living, breathing thing”, Farhan highlighted how a story evolves through the collective imagination of writers, actors and technicians. He stressed that filmmaking is a collaborative process, where setting aside individual egos allows a story to grow and find its true voice. He also cautioned against letting excessive promotions overshadow the essence of cinema, emphasising that meaningful storytelling and a genuine audience connect should always come first.

As the conversation drew to a close, one thought stood out: great cinema is born out of creative courage, original storytelling and the willingness to challenge conventions. Twenty-five years after Lagaan, Dil Chahta Hai and Chandni Bar explored different facets of Indian society and reshaped the cinematic conversation, their creators reaffirmed the enduring power of stories rooted in human experiences.

Echoing the spirit of the 57th International Film Festival of India, under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, the discussion highlighted how authentic stories, irrespective of their cultural or geographical origins, can transcend boundaries and resonate with audiences everywhere. As technology continues to transform filmmaking, it is ultimately human emotions, creative conviction and the universality of storytelling that give cinema its enduring appeal.

The session was moderated by acclaimed actor and producer Khushboo Sundar.

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

 

* * *

PIB IFFI Team | Rajith/ LekshmiPriya/ Swadhin/ Darshana | IFFI 57 - 117

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
NBA disburses Rs. 13.76 Crore  in ABS Funds across 28 States and 4 UTs: Linking Commercial Utilisation of Medicinal Plants with Biodiversity Conservation
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 5:43PM by PIB Delhi

The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 13.76 crore to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of biological resources across 28 States and 4 Union Territories. The allocation forms part of the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) contributions received from AYUSH products manufacturing companies for the commercial utilisation of medicinal plants and other plant-based biological resources.

These contributions pertain to three applications involving the utilisation of a total of 234 plant species. These biological resources were procured through market and trader networks, making it difficult to identify the individual benefit claimers associated with their supply chains. However, considering the majority of the medicinal plants used by companies are from forest areas, the State forest cover and occurrence of medicinal plants in the State/UT are taken into account for disbursing the benefit-sharing amount.

Among the 234 plant species, ten species, namely Guggul, Ashwagandha, Bhringraj, Punarnava, Sarpagandha, Kalmegh, Black Pepper, Indian Gooseberry, Gokhura and Shalparni, contributes for a benefit-sharing amount of Rs. 6.45 Crore, out of Rs. 13.76 Crore. The ABS mechanism provides a means to channel the monetary benefits arising from their commercial utilisation towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable harvesting and promoting cultivation of these valuable biological resources. The funds transferred can support strengthening of local biodiversity governance, Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs), updating People’s Biodiversity Registers, documentation of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge, research and capacity building, community-led conservation, restoration of degraded ecosystems, sustainable harvesting and cultivation practices, and biodiversity-based livelihood initiatives. The NBA has so far collected Rs. 278 crore through the ABS mechanism, of which around Rs. 218.86 crore has been disbursed towards biodiversity conservation and benefit-sharing initiatives across the country.

India’s ABS framework contributes to the global biodiversity agenda and the implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). The Yerevan Pathway, adopted at CBD COP 17 (19–30 October 2026), emphasises resource mobilisation, scientific and technical cooperation, and accelerated implementation of biodiversity targets. India’s ABS mechanism supports these priorities by advancing Target 13 of the KMGBF on fair and equitable benefit sharing from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge.

Medicinal plants are an integral part of India’s biological wealth, traditional healthcare systems and rural livelihoods. They support communities engaged in their collection, cultivation, processing and trade, while the associated traditional knowledge forms an important part of India’s cultural heritage. The growing commercial utilisation of medicinal plants underscores the need for responsible sourcing, sustainable harvesting and conservation of wild populations. The ABS mechanism facilitates benefit sharing from their utilisation, supporting biodiversity conservation, strengthening local institutions and promoting community-based livelihoods. These efforts complement Government initiatives such as the National AYUSH Mission, National Medicinal Plants Board programmes and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana, which promote medicinal plant cultivation, value addition and livelihood generation.

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS TRIBUTES TO SHRI G. V. MAVALANKAR ON HIS BIRTH ANNIVERSARY
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to Shri Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar, the first Speaker of Lok Sabha, in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, today, on his birth anniversary.

Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Members of Parliament; former Members; Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and other dignitaries also offered floral tributes.

Shri Mavalankar, born on 27 November 1888 in Baroda (present-day Gujarat), played a monumental role in shaping India’s parliamentary institutions. Beginning his legislative journey in 1937 as a member of the Bombay Legislative Assembly from Ahmedabad, he served as its Speaker until 1946. He later presided over the Sixth Central Legislative Assembly, guiding it through the crucial years leading to Independence.

After 1947, Shri Mavalankar served as Speaker of the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) and subsequently as Speaker of the Provisional Parliament. With the formation of the First Lok Sabha in 1952, he was unanimously elected as its Speaker on 15 May 1952, a responsibility he fulfilled with distinction until his demise on 27 February 1956. His vision, discipline and commitment continue to define the functioning and traditions of the Indian Parliament.

The portrait of Shri Mavalankar, painted by Shri Madhav Satawalekar, decorates the Lobby of Samvidhan Sadan. It was unveiled by the then Prime Minister Pt . Jawaharlal Nehru on 7 September, 1956.

संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में आज लोकसभा के प्रथम अध्यक्ष, श्री गणेश वासुदेव मावलंकर जी की जयंती पर पुष्पांजलि अर्पित की। श्री मावलंकर जी का जीवन स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, सार्वजनिक सेवा और संसदीय लोकतंत्र के प्रति उनकी अटूट निष्ठा का प्रेरक उदाहरण है। स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन में सक्रिय योगदान देने के साथ उन्होंने संविधान सभा और अंतरिम संसद में भी महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। लोकसभा के प्रथम अध्यक्ष के रूप में उन्होंने सदन की कार्यवाही के संचालन, संसदीय नियमों और प्रक्रियाओं की मर्यादा तथा अध्यक्ष पद की निष्पक्षता के ऐसे मानदंड स्थापित किए, जिन्होंने भारतीय संसदीय परंपराओं को सुदृढ़ आधार प्रदान किया। वे केवल एक कुशल संसदीय संचालक ही नहीं, बल्कि प्रखर राष्ट्रसेवी, समाजसेवी और शिक्षाविद् भी थे। सदन में सभी दलों और सदस्यों के अधिकारों के प्रति उनकी सजगता, धैर्यपूर्ण कार्यशैली और लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता उनके व्यक्तित्व की विशिष्ट पहचान रही। भारतीय संसदीय व्यवस्था की आधारभूत परंपराओं को आकार देने में उनका योगदान सदैव स्मरणीय रहेगा। उनका जीवन सार्वजनिक जीवन में शुचिता, कर्तव्यनिष्ठा और संस्थागत गरिमा बनाए रखने की प्रेरणा देता रहेगा।

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Power
Two-day Power Ministers’ Conference begins in New Delhi
Rs 200 lakh Crore Investment Opportunity in the Power Sector in Next Two Decades
Demands Teamwork of all Stakeholders: Shri Manohar Lal
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 12:40PM by PIB Delhi

The two-day Power Ministers’ Conference commenced in New Delhi today. The conference (November 27-28, 2026) brings together Power Ministers, senior officials and electricity regulators from 28 States and 8 Union Territories and is chaired by Shri Manohar Lal, Union Minister of Power and Housing & Urban Affairs. The last such conference at the national level was held in 2024.

The Conference provides a platform for Centre–State deliberations on key policy priorities and implementation challenges in India’s power sector, with discussions focusing on strengthening energy security, improving power infrastructure and accelerating sectoral reforms.

While welcoming the participating State Power Ministers and other dignitaries, Shri Manohar Lal emphasised the need for the Centre and States to work together to develop the power sector. He said that India has made significant progress in expanding generation capacity, integrating renewable energy and strengthening the national grid. The next phase of our journey requires us to move towards a more integrated approach to power sector planning, where generation, storage, transmission and distribution are planned as interconnected elements of a single system. He stressed the necessity for States to implement Smart Meters, which offer significant benefits to consumers. The Minister also stated that, through collaboration with States and initiatives from the Ministry of Power, DISCOMS have achieved profitability after a prolonged period.

The Minister noted that the country’s power sector presents investment opportunity of Rs 200 lakh crores over the next two decades, and all stakeholders have to work together to make this possible. We have to work together with the private sector to ensure that we accomplish this, he said.

Shri Manohar Lal complimented the States and DISCOMs, as the DISCOMs as a whole turned a positive PAT during FY 2024-25. He said that we need to ensure that financial position of our DISCOMs is strengthened and necessary changes in policy, operations and regulation should facilitate the continuation of this turnaround.

While listing the main agenda of the Conference, he informed that Conference will comprise interactions and in-depth discussions among the Ministry of Power, States and other stakeholders on key issues such as implementation of Resource Adequacy (RA) plans, including accelerated energy storage deployment; inter-state and intra-state transmission issues; financial viability of Distribution Companies (DISCOMs); implementation of the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with emphasis on smart metering, feeder separation and household electrification; and issues related to nuclear sites.

Shri Shripad Yesso Naik, Minister of State for Power in his address asked the participating States and UTs to share their experiences during the Conference, including difficulties in implementation, regulatory issues and areas where further support or intervention from the Central Government may be required. Our collective focus should be on moving from policy formulation to effective execution, from infrastructure creation to measurable outcomes, and from individual interventions to an integrated and sustainable power sector, the Minister said.

While addressing the participants, Shri Pankaj Agarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Power noted that the core guidance received from the Prime Minister is to move beyond energy security toward true energy independence in service of Viksit Bharat @ 2047. The past year has been one of record growth, he said, and noted that India’s installed capacity is now about 563 GW, and more than 55% of it is non-fossil. In the last 12 months around 60 GW of capacity was added, 87% of it from non-fossil sources, he said.

A key highlight on November 28 will be a joint session with the Forum of Regulators and State Electricity Regulatory Commissions (SERCs), bringing together State Power Ministers, SERC Chairpersons, State Secretaries for Power/Energy and Ministry officials to deliberate on issues concerning the power sector.

Senior officials from the Ministry of Power and representatives from participating States and Union Territories are also attending the Conference.

item.title: India’s Growth Story Remains Strong, Resilient and Trustworthy Amid Global Uncertainties: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Commerce & Industry
item.description: Ministry of Commerce & Industry India’s Growth Story Remains Strong, Resilient and Trustworthy Amid Global Uncertainties: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Shri Goyal Calls for Greater Long-Term Investments and a Broader Credit Ecosystem Shri Goyal Stresses Need for Innovative Financing Instruments to Support India’s Growth Ambitions Shri Goyal Highlights 12 Years of Economic Reforms, Resilience and Expanding Market Opportunities Shri Goyal Emphasises Export Growth, Manufacturing Investments and Value Addition to Make India a Global Manufacturing Hub Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
India’s Growth Story Remains Strong, Resilient and Trustworthy Amid Global Uncertainties: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
Shri Goyal Calls for Greater Long-Term Investments and a Broader Credit Ecosystem
Shri Goyal Stresses Need for Innovative Financing Instruments to Support India’s Growth Ambitions
Shri Goyal Highlights 12 Years of Economic Reforms, Resilience and Expanding Market Opportunities
Shri Goyal Emphasises Export Growth, Manufacturing Investments and Value Addition to Make India a Global Manufacturing Hub
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 12:09PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today said that India’s growth story remained strong, resilient and trustworthy despite global uncertainties, with the country delivering on the trust placed in it by the world. Addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026, he highlighted India’s economic performance, sustained reforms, expanding trade opportunities and the growing importance of debt markets in supporting the country’s development ambitions.

The Minister said India had delivered 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter of the current financial year and expressed confidence that the country was on track to maintain its growth momentum in the second quarter as well. Gross fixed capital formation had increased by about 12 per cent, while exports had already reached USD 570 billion in the first seven months of the year. He said India was well on track to achieve its USD 1 trillion export target, which had appeared unimaginable and aspirational when it was set in May this year. Credit growth of about 19 per cent was another positive indicator, particularly for credit markets.

Shri Goyal said India had demonstrated resilience amid two ongoing wars, an oil price shock, uncertainties surrounding tariffs and global trading opportunities, disruptions to sea routes and sporadic attacks affecting air travel. Despite these challenges, the world's trust in India's growth story had remained constant, and the country had delivered on that trust.

He said India had continued to reform processes, introduce policies, improve ease of doing business and maintain an open-door policy to engage with businesses and stakeholders. The Government was planning for the next 20 to 25 years, with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 firmly embedded in the system and the ambition of becoming a USD 30 trillion economy. The objective was to ensure that every child born in the country had access to a better quality of life, good education, healthcare and greater opportunities.

The Minister said India had continued to finalise free trade agreements (FTAs) and reform the GST system to make it simpler and reduce tax rates, thereby boosting consumption. He noted that GST collections continued to rise, with October recording an all-time high. Exports also registered a record performance in October, reaching USD 90 billion in a single month.

He said several substantive FTAs had not yet come into effect. The India-EU FTA was expected to be signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year. The India-US trade deal was also close to culmination, with the process and pathway for finalising the agreement beginning to take shape, he added.

Congratulating the organisers for bringing together the entire debt capital market ecosystem on a common platform, the Minister said the summit's theme, ‘Catalysts, Apex and Credit’, was contemporary and critical to India's growth story. He said the bond and credit markets embodied the importance of trust, as they depended on the trustworthiness of borrowers.

Shri Goyal said India's trusted partnership with countries around the world was central to its engagement in preferential, bilateral and free trade agreements. The country's growth story was anchored in the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the opportunities offered by a USD 4 trillion economy progressing towards USD 30 trillion, and the trusted partnerships India offered to its global partners.

The Minister said India had now emerged as a preferred partner, an attractive investment destination and a trusted companion for the next two to three decades. He highlighted the country's expanding manufacturing and export capabilities, its integration with the global economy through FTAs, and the rapid development of infrastructure.

He said India was expected to construct more buildings in the next 30 years than the entire existing stock of residential and commercial buildings in the country. This reflected the scale of infrastructure development and the opportunities emerging across sectors.

Shri Goyal said that while rising oil prices had a significant impact on an economy, their implications for India's long-term growth needed to be assessed in the context of the country's changing economic fundamentals. He noted that India had significantly higher foreign exchange reserves, remittances and foreign direct investment inflows than it had 20 years ago.

He said India was exporting over USD 700 billion, while its overall export basket was expected to reach USD 1 trillion this year. The country had a GDP of USD 4 trillion, placing it among the world's top five or six economies. On a purchasing power parity basis, India's GDP was approximately USD 18 to 19 trillion, demonstrating its capacity to absorb goods and services and produce at competitive prices.

The Minister said that at India's current economic scale, fluctuations of a few dollars in oil prices could not determine the country's long-term future. He noted that India continued to have among the lowest levels of national debt in the world, with its external debt being significantly lower within its overall debt. These factors demonstrated the sustainability of India's growth story. He emphasised that India had never defaulted on its obligations to the world, including during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Shri Goyal said India continued to have moderate interest rates and expressed confidence in the country's economic prospects. He noted that domestic institutional investors and retail investors had supported the markets through periods of volatility, including when foreign investors were withdrawing funds. He said India's growth story remained safe, strong, resilient and trustworthy.

The Minister emphasised that India's economic transformation was the result of 12 years of sustained reforms and transformational initiatives across sectors, rather than coincidence or luck. He highlighted the Government's focus on meeting the daily needs of citizens, including food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, education, good roads, quality electricity and digital connectivity.

He also highlighted the Jal Jeevan Mission's efforts to provide water to every household in every village and said that bringing 50 crore people out of poverty in 12 years was a significant achievement. As incomes rise and people move into the new middle class, middle class and upper middle class, they would create substantial market opportunities.

Shri Goyal said infrastructure development, rising consumption and economic growth, together with FTAs opening up new markets, would create opportunities for India's manufacturers, agricultural exporters, seafood exporters and service providers. He expressed confidence that India would continue to grow while undertaking steady reforms and making sustained efforts to improve the lives of its people.

The Minister called for taking India's exports to the next level and increasing investments in manufacturing to make the Make in India initiative a globally competitive manufacturing base. He emphasised the need for greater value addition and quality in India, along with building a larger pool of talent to enable the country to participate at the forefront of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning and quantum computing.

He said India was a global partner and highlighted the expansion of its preferential market access through FTAs. Until 2014, India's FTAs covered countries with a combined GDP of approximately USD 10 trillion, against a global GDP of about USD 115 trillion. He said the nine FTAs covering 38 developed countries finalised in the last four and a half to five years covered a GDP of USD 60 trillion. Together with the earlier agreements, India now had preferential market access to economies accounting for USD 70 trillion of global GDP.

The Minister said India was negotiating eight or nine additional agreements and expected to add another USD 15 trillion in market access, taking the total to USD 85 trillion out of a global GDP of USD 115 to 120 trillion. He said almost every country in the world wanted to enter into an FTA with India, reflecting the country's growing position as a trusted partner and the opportunities available for Indian businesses.

Referring to the summit's theme, Shri Goyal said the Government and the private sector were collectively catalysing new growth opportunities, while opening doors for higher capital expenditure by both. The upward trend in credit growth reflected the attractiveness of India's growth story and the renewed opportunities for investment.

He said the expansion of semiconductor fabrication facilities, electricity grids, data centres and the next port coming up in Vadhavan outside Mumbai would collectively generate substantial debt requirements in the economy. The Minister said debt markets would play an important role in financing India's growth and called for the country's financing system to match the scale, diversity and duration of the opportunities emerging over the next two to three decades. He emphasised the need for faster and more efficient financing, along with attractive and innovative instruments to meet the economy's debt requirements.

He said private capital would become an increasingly meaningful source of capital in the coming years. India's inclusion in global bond indices would also play an important role in the growth of debt markets.

The Minister outlined five key priorities for the debt capital market ecosystem:

First, he called upon bond issuers, including large corporates, public sector undertakings and infrastructure developers, to make the bond market their first port of call for capital expenditure, including for longer-gestation projects. He emphasised the need to develop innovative solutions to meet their financing requirements.

Second, he urged investors to support long-term debt and the broader credit ecosystem. He said insurance companies, pension companies, pension funds, provident funds and mutual funds were increasingly holding patient capital and encouraged them to look beyond AAA-rated instruments.

Third, he called upon the market to make bonds easier to trade and enable transactions to take place instantaneously, on the lines of the share market.

Fourth, he urged exporters and their financiers to translate the opportunities created by FTAs into investment decisions and build capacity to serve the markets that had opened up.

Fifth, he reiterated that the Government was open to working with all stakeholders and invited suggestions and ideas from the sector on further reforms and improvements.

The Minister concluded by expressing confidence in India's continued growth and resilience, and emphasised the importance of collaboration between the Government and the private sector in realising the country's economic ambitions.

 

***

Abhishek Dayal/ Shabbir Azad/ Ishita Biswas

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MWCD and MSDE to jointly launch NAVYA 2.0 in Haridwar on 28 November 2026
Joint initiative to empower adolescent girls and young women through skills, confidence-building and livelihood opportunities across 100 districts in 24 States/UTs
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 12:02PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) will jointly launch the second phase of NAVYA – Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls (NAVYA 2.0) on 28 November 2026 at 3:30 PM at the Uttarakhand Sanskrit Academy Auditorium, Haridwar. Building on the learnings of its pilot phase, NAVYA 2.0 aims to advance women-led development by nurturing the aspirations of adolescent girls and young women, strengthening their capabilities and enabling them to achieve greater confidence, self-reliance and economic independence.

The programme will be graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development; Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; Smt. Rekha Arya, Cabinet Minister for Women Empowerment and Child Development, Food and Civil Supplies, Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Mandan Kaushik, Cabinet Minister of Panchayati Raj, Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, Ayush and Ayush Education, Reorganization and Census, Government of Uttarakhand; and Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Uttarakhand.

The launch programme will feature the formal launch of NAVYA 2.0 by the Union Ministers. It will also include the inauguration of Saksham Anganwadi Centres and new Anganwadi Centres constructed under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand, and distribution of certificates to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).

NAVYA: Nurturing aspirations and enabling empowerment

NAVYA is a collaborative initiative of MWCD and MSDE that brings together the strengths of the women and child development and skill development ecosystems to empower adolescent girls and young women. The initiative recognises that empowerment goes beyond training and entails nurturing aspirations, building confidence, developing capabilities and enabling informed choices about the future.

The pilot phase was launched on 24 June 2025 in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh, with an envisaged coverage of 27 Aspirational Districts across 19 States. Approximately 1,200 adolescent girls were trained in industry-relevant job roles such as Drone Manufacturing and Assembly Technician, Solar PV Installation Helper and Fashion Designer. The initiative also emphasised digital and financial literacy, career readiness and entrepreneurship to strengthen their confidence and socio-economic independence.

NAVYA 2.0: Expanding the horizons of empowerment

Building on the pilot experience, NAVYA 2.0 will expand its reach to 100 districts across 24 States/UTs, with a particular focus on aspirational and hard-to-reach areas. The eligible age group has also been widened from 16–18 years to 16–25 years, bringing a larger cohort of adolescent girls and young women within its ambit.

The expanded initiative will provide greater access to vocational training in industry-relevant, new-age and non-traditional job roles, while strengthening pathways to employment, apprenticeships and entrepreneurship. It places emphasis on institutional convergence, coordinated district-level implementation and outcome-oriented support. A structured Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has also been introduced to facilitate effective coordination and implementation at the district level.

Technology-enabled implementation

The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) will serve as the digital platform for facilitating access to skilling opportunities and supporting candidates throughout their journey from enrolment to training and certification. It will also enable real-time tracking of beneficiary registration, attendance, training progress and certification, strengthening transparency and accountability. Digitally verifiable credentials will further help candidates demonstrate their skills and competencies.

Advancing women-led development

Through the convergence of MWCD and MSDE, NAVYA 2.0 seeks to create an enabling ecosystem where adolescent girls and young women, particularly from aspirational and underserved regions, can realise their potential, pursue their aspirations and participate meaningfully in economic and social development.

NAVYA 2.0 is a step towards transforming aspirations into opportunities and opportunities into empowerment, enabling every young woman to shape her own future and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Electronics & IT
STPI Inaugurates its 75th Centre in Bareilly to Strengthen Uttar Pradesh’s IT/ITeS and Startup Ecosystem
New Centre to Strengthen Technology Infrastructure and Support IT/ITeS Enterprises, Startups and Technology-led Entrepreneurship in the Rohilkhand Region
Initiative Aims to Promote Innovation, Facilitate Business Opportunities and Encourage Employment Generation in the Region
Posted On: 27 NOV 2026 9:52AM by PIB Delhi

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, inaugurated its Bareilly Centre in Uttar Pradesh. The centre was inaugurated by Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, in the presence of Dr. Arun Kumar Saxena, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Forest & Environment, Zoological Garden and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh; Shri Chhatrapal Singh Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Bareilly and Smt. Shruti Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI among other dignitaries.

The inauguration marks an important milestone for STPI as Bareilly becomes its 75th centre in the country, further expanding its nationwide network and commitment to strengthening India's technology ecosystem beyond established metropolitan hubs. Of STPI's 75 centres, 67 are located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities, reflecting its sustained focus on decentralising technology infrastructure and enabling regional entrepreneurship. Developed with an investment of approximately ₹18.25 crore on a 2-acre land parcel, the Bareilly Centre will strengthen the regional IT/ITeS ecosystem by providing an institutional platform for technology enterprises and emerging entrepreneurs.

Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly centre is a landmark gift not only for Bareilly, but for the youth of the entire Rohilkhand region especially Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, and Badaun so they no longer have to migrate to major hubs like Mumbai, Noida, and Hyderabad for IT, startups, incubation, innovation, and research, instead gaining world-class technical facilities right at home while shaping the future of coming generations and driving local job creation. Under the visionary leadership and long-term policies of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, just as center-state coordination drives growth, trade and technology serve as twin engines of India's progress, while commitments to train one crore youth in artificial intelligence (AI), build a semiconductor chip manufacturing and packaging ecosystem to reduce foreign dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience after disruptions like the COVID-19 pandemic, expand data centers and software exports, and advance Atmanirbhar Bharat are accelerating India's technological self-reliance and creating new opportunities for young people."

"In the IT sector, India stands today as the world's Talent Capital, powered by youth technical skill and design capabilities, and providing free technical facilities through STPI alongside skill development and support ensures that financial constraints never hold back talent and enterprise. As local MSMEs, IT industries, chambers of commerce, and entrepreneurs utilize the center to full capacity, we will expand additional buildings and technical facilities, while Common Service Centers (CSCs) under Digital India continue expanding rural access to Aadhaar, banking, electricity bill payments, and citizen services—giving me complete confidence, alongside commendations to STPI Director General Arvind Kumar and his team, that like Noida, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Gorakhpur, Bareilly will emerge as a major IT hub propelling technical and economic growth across Rohilkhand.”

Dr. Arun Kumar Saxena, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Forest & Environment, Zoological Garden and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said, “The establishment of the STPI Bareilly Centre is a welcome development for the region and will contribute to expanding opportunities in the technology sector. Bareilly and the surrounding areas have considerable potential in terms of talent and entrepreneurship. The centre will provide an important platform for young people, startups and technology enterprises to explore new opportunities, develop innovative ideas and contribute to the state's economic progress.”

Shri Chhatrapal Singh Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Bareilly, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly Centre is a significant milestone for the region. It will help create a stronger foundation for technology-led entrepreneurship and provide aspiring entrepreneurs and young professionals with access to a wider ecosystem of opportunities.

Smt. Shruti Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly Centre is an encouraging development for the region, particularly for its young talent and aspiring entrepreneurs. Access to technology infrastructure and a supportive startup ecosystem can help unlock local potential, encourage innovative thinking and create new avenues for professional growth. ”

Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, said, “The inauguration of the Bareilly Centre marks a significant milestone in STPI's journey, taking our nationwide network to 75 centres, of which 67 are located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. This reflects our continued commitment to extending technology infrastructure and entrepreneurial opportunities beyond established IT hubs and enabling emerging regions to participate in India's digital economy. Developed with an investment of approximately ₹18.25 crore on a 2-acre land parcel, the Bareilly Centre is an important addition to this network and will provide an enabling environment for IT/ITeS enterprises, startups and aspiring entrepreneurs in the Rohilkhand region. Through our infrastructure, incubation initiatives and industry linkages, we aim to nurture local talent, facilitate business growth and support the development of innovative technology-led enterprises.”

The Bareilly Centre further expands STPI's nationwide presence and its efforts to promote the IT/ITeS industry beyond established technology hubs. Through its network of centres, incubation facilities and entrepreneurship initiatives, STPI continues to support startups and technology enterprises through infrastructure, industry linkages and opportunities for product development and intellectual property creation.

The event was also attended by several prominent dignitaries and public representatives.

The inauguration marks an important step towards strengthening Uttar Pradesh's regional technology ecosystem, encouraging entrepreneurship and enabling technology-led economic growth through greater collaboration among government, industry, academia and startups.

About STPI:

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), engaged in promoting the IT/ITES industry, innovation, research and development, startups, and product and intellectual property creation in emerging technology domains. These include the Internet of Things, blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, augmented and virtual reality, animation and visual effects, and data science and analytics. STPI supports innovation across domains such as gaming, fintech, agritech, medtech, autonomous and connected mobility, ESDM, cybersecurity, Industry 4.0 and drones.

The mission marks an…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
WOAH PVS Mission Begins Evaluation of India's Aquatic Animal Health Services
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 8:36PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India today commenced the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) Performance of Veterinary Services (PVS) Evaluation of India's Aquatic Animal Health Services (AAHS) with an orientation meeting held at the National Agricultural Science Complex, New Delhi. The mission marks an important milestone in India's efforts to strengthen aquatic animal health governance and align its systems with internationally recognized standards and best practices.

The orientation meeting was chaired by Gunjan Krishnan, Joint Secretary (Inland Fisheries), Department of Fisheries and WOAH National Focal Point for Aquatic Animals-India; Dr J. K. Jena, Deputy Director General (Fisheries Science), ICAR; K.C. Devasenapathi, Secretary, Coastal Aquaculture Authority; Ana Luisa da Silva Afonso, Team Leader of the WOAH PVS Mission; and K. Mohammed Koya, Fisheries Development Commissioner, Department of Fisheries, along with representatives from ICAR Fisheries Research Institutes, State Fisheries Departments, MPEDA, Export Inspection Council, FSSAI, BIS, the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying and other stakeholder organizations.

Addressing the gathering, Gunjan Krishnan highlighted India's vibrant fisheries and aquaculture sector and outlined the country's institutional, legislative and regulatory framework for aquatic animal health management. Ana Luisa da Silva Afonso emphasized that the evaluation would support India in identifying priorities and developing strategic plans consistent with WOAH standards and international good practices.

The orientation programme covered key dimensions of aquatic animal health governance, including research and development, disease surveillance, capacity building, trade facilitation, export quality assurance, food safety, regulatory compliance and standards relating to aquaculture inputs and feed.

The WOAH PVS Pathway is a globally recognized framework designed to support countries in assessing and strengthening Veterinary Services and Aquatic Animal Health Services through an evidence-based and independent evaluation process. The assessment examines four core areas: human, physical and financial resources; technical authority and capability; stakeholder engagement; and regulatory capability and market access.

As part of the mission, the WOAH expert team will undertake field visits to aquaculture farms, fisheries establishments, research institutes, aquatic animal disease diagnostic laboratories and quality control facilities across multiple States from 27 November to 9 December 2026.

The voluntary evaluation is expected to help identify priorities for capacity enhancement, targeted investments and institutional strengthening. It is also expected to contribute to improved disease prevention and surveillance, stronger collaboration under the One Health approach, enhanced confidence among trading partners and greater facilitation of international seafood trade.

The WOAH PVS Evaluation represents an important opportunity for India to further strengthen its aquatic animal health systems, support sustainable growth of the fisheries and aquaculture sector and reinforce its position as a responsible and globally competitive fisheries nation.

Scindia Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 8:08PM by PIB Delhi India Post is set to…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
India Post Accelerates Its Transformation with ₹2,632 Crore Financial Outlay Following Cabinet Approval
Investment to modernise postal infrastructure, strengthen logistics and enhance citizen-centric services across the country
With the vision and continued support of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India Post is being transformed into a modern, efficient and citizen-centric public logistics organisation: Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 8:08PM by PIB Delhi

India Post is set to accelerate its transformation with a combined financial outlay of ₹2,632 crore for the Postal Operations and Estates Management Schemes for the 16th Finance Commission Cycle (FY 2026 - 27 to FY 2030 - 31). This includes ₹1,141 crore for the proposed continuation of the Postal Operations Scheme and ₹1,491 crore for the Estates Management Scheme, whose continuation has been approved by the Union Cabinet.

The details of these initiatives were highlighted during a press briefing addressed by Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, Union Minister of Communications and Development of North Eastern Region; Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development; and Shri Subrat Das, Secretary (Posts), along with other senior officials.

The Union Minister expressed his gratitude to  Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, for his visionary leadership and continued support in transforming post offices into modern, citizen-centric service touchpoints across the country. He particularly acknowledged the Prime Minister’s support in securing the Cabinet approval of the financial outlay for the modernisation of post offices, which will provide fresh impetus to this transformative journey.

The Union Minister also thanked all the employees and stated, “Every member of the India Post family has worked with unwavering dedication and determination to bring about the transformation of this institution, whose potential extends far beyond national boundaries to the global stage. United by a shared resolve to turn commitment into achievement, the entire workforce has contributed tirelessly towards realising this vision.”

In a detailed presentation, Secretary (Posts) highlighted the Department's growth trajectory, future roadmap and segregation of budgetary allocations across various areas of development. He also highlighted the transformative impact of the integrated Insurance Management System (IMS), through which the end-to-end process of purchasing a PLI policy can be completed in approximately 20 minutes. The initiative has already facilitated premium transactions for around 2 lakh customers, generating revenue of approximately ₹60 crore.


Secretary (Posts) further highlighted the Department's institutional approach to innovation and growth, emphasising the role of its Data Analytics Team, Six Sigma Team and Chief Marketing Officer. Working in close collaboration with the six key verticals, these teams focus on developing new products and services, identifying revenue-generation opportunities and continuously improving service quality.

The Union Minister further said that this combined institutional approach forms the backbone of India Posts’s Transformation, while the six service verticals are its soul. This integrated approach aims to continuously innovate and enhance products and services, ensuring the highest standards of quality, efficiency and customer satisfaction.

Reaffirming the Department's growth ambitions, the Secretary (Posts) outlined the vision of taking India Post's annual revenue to approximately ₹19,803 crore, in the FY 2026-27,  driven by operational efficiency, expansion of parcel and logistics services, technology adoption and enhanced customer engagement.


Strengthening Operations and Modernising Infrastructure

The ₹1,141 crore Postal Operations Scheme focuses on six key areas, including rural postal access, mail network optimisation, parcel network optimisation, international mail infrastructure, marketing and service quality, and philately operations.

The ₹1,491 crore Estates Management Scheme will focus on modernising postal buildings and improving customer-facing infrastructure. Key initiatives include construction of 190 new departmental postal buildings, reconstruction of 50 buildings, renovation and branding of 2,550 departmental Sub-Post Offices, upgradation of 2,500 rented post offices and preservation of 20 heritage postal buildings. The scheme will also support the renovation of 150 residential colonies and the development of a permanent Integrated Technology Centre for CEPT in Bengaluru.

With renewed investment, technology-led modernisation and a clear growth vision, India Post is preparing to take its nationwide network into its next phase of expansion and service excellence.

Speaking at a press…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Through Aaryan’s Lens: Sreehari Haridas discusses mockumentary storytelling, personal influences and the making of his feature ‘Ajayante Maranam: Oru Case Study’
Director pays Tribute to ‘Utharam’ through his Debut Feature
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 8:01PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 26 November 2026

 

Malayalam film Ajayante Maranam: Oru Case Study, directed by Sreehari Haridas, was featured today in the Indian Panorama – New Horizons section at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

Speaking at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Haridas expressed his gratitude for the audience response to his debut feature, admitting that he had not anticipated such an encouraging turnout at the festival.

Describing the film as a character study centred on Ajayan, Haridas said it adopts a mockumentary format, a relatively less explored genre in Malayalam cinema. He acknowledged that this approach brought its own challenges during filming and production.

Explaining the narrative, Haridas said the story of Ajayan unfolds through Aaryan, an aspiring filmmaker who investigates the circumstances surrounding Ajayan's life and death. He revealed that he had drawn upon aspects of his own personality while developing Aaryan's character, while also recognising certain similarities between himself and Ajayan. “There are glimpses of me in Aaryan. And there are some similarities of Ajayan in me,” he said.

Speaking about the screenplay, Haridas recalled completing the first draft in a week, followed by nearly a month of work to develop the final script. He explained that using a central character as a narrative device to explore the experiences of others was an approach he frequently adopted. While the characters and narrative structures may change, he said, he enjoys building stories around individuals and following their journeys.

Haridas also described Ajayante Maranam: Oru Case Study as a tribute to the Malayalam film Utharam, acknowledging its influence on his directorial venture.

Responding to questions about the film's target audience and release plans, he said the project was conceived primarily for the film-festival circuit. The team is looking at festivals as a platform to reach audiences, rather than prioritising a conventional theatrical release at this stage.

Ms Gopika moderated the press conference.

The meeting was co-chaired by Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh from the Indian side and Under Secretary, Ministry of Defence, UAE Lieutenant General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi. item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
India and UAE agree to accelerate co-development & co-production of next generation defence equipment at 14th JDCC meeting in Abu Dhabi
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 8:00PM by PIB Delhi

The 14th meeting of the India-UAE Joint Defence Cooperation Committee (JDCC) took place in Abu Dhabi on November 26, 2026. The meeting was co-chaired by Defence Secretary Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh from the Indian side and Under Secretary, Ministry of Defence, UAE Lieutenant General Ibrahim Nasser M. Al Alawi.

The meeting provided strategic direction to the initiatives laid out in the India-UAE Strategic Defence Partnership Framework signed in May 2026 during the visit of the Prime Minister to UAE. Both sides agreed to enhance bilateral defence ties under a wide range of areas, specifically defence industry, defence innovation & advanced technology, artificial intelligence, cyber, military training and maritime safety.​​ They agreed to accelerate co-development and co-production partnerships in next generation defence equipment.

The co-chairs decided to review the progress made in defence cooperation at regular intervals in the interim before the next JDCC. The Indian delegation comprised representatives from the Department of Defence, Indian Defence Forces, National Security Council Secretariat and Ministry of External Affairs.

To facilitate business-to-business (B2B) partnerships, a delegation from the Indian defence industry also accompanied the JDCC delegation. A B2B interaction between defence industries of the two countries was held on the sidelines of the meeting. The Indian defence industry delegation visited Tawazun Industrial Park and held a meeting with the Tawazun Economic Council, UAE, to explore potential areas of mutual cooperation with their UAE counterparts.

The Indian delegation, led by the Defence Secretary, also called on Minister of State for Defence Affairs, UAE Mr Mohamed bin Mubarak Fadhel Al Mazrouei. The two dignitaries exchanged views on the emerging geopolitical situation in the Gulf & West Asia region, and reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening the Strategic Defence Partnership. The Defence Secretary conveyed greetings from Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh.

Earlier, the Defence Secretary paid solemn tributes at Wahat Al Karama, Abu Dhabi, dedicated to the courageous soldiers who sacrificed their lives in the service of the UAE.

India and the UAE share centuries-old historical ties rooted in trade and cultural exchanges, complemented by strong people-to-people connections. The bilateral relations have been elevated to a Strategic Partnership which now includes Strategic Defence Partnership.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Pension Reforms Division in Department of Financial Services tops Grievance Redressal Assessment & Index (GRAI) ranking in Group B Category by Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances for October, 2026
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:58PM by PIB Delhi

The Pension Reforms Division of the Department of Financial Services (DFS) has secured the 1st rank in the Group B category (ministries/departments registering fewer than 500 grievances) in the Grievance Redressal Assessment and Index (GRAI) for October 2026, released by the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG)

The GRAI framework, developed by the DARPG, evaluates ministries and departments on the effectiveness and timeliness of grievance resolution through the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS).

This achievement reflects the DFS commitment to “Seamless, Time- bond and Empathetic Resolution”. A dedicated Grievance Redressal cell monitors CPGRAMS daily with regular review in Senior Officers’ Meeting. Also, the AS/ JS/ Divisional Heads concerned are reviewing 20 grievances on a monthly basis.

Since January 2024, Secretary (DFS) also has been personally reviewing 20 randomly selected closed grievances on a monthly basis. Such a practice reinforces confidence amongst customers by ensuring that their concerns are being addressed appropriately at the top most level.

This achievement underscores the DFS's sustained efforts towards strengthening the grievance redressal mechanism and ensuring prompt, effective and satisfactory resolution of grievances received from citizens.

The DFS has consistently focused on improving service delivery through regular monitoring of pending grievances, timely disposal of complaints, effective coordination with concerned organisations and continuous improvement in grievance handling processes.

The DFS reiterates its commitment to further strengthening grievance redressal systems, enhancing responsiveness and ensuring accessible, transparent and efficient public service delivery.

Ambedkar’s Vision in Advancing Social Justice, Equality and Inclusive Development Shri B L Verma, Shri Ramdas Athawale Pay Tributes To Bharat Ratna Dr B R Ambedkar for His Historical, Visionary Role, Contribution To The Nation Former Chief Justice of India, Justice Uday Umesh Lalit Leads Reading of the Preamble to the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Dr. Ambedkar Foundation Celebrates Constitution Day 2026; Reaffirms Commitment to Constitutional Values, Social Justice and Inclusive Democracy
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar Highlights the Enduring Relevance of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s Vision in Advancing Social Justice, Equality and Inclusive Development
Shri B L Verma, Shri Ramdas Athawale Pay Tributes To Bharat Ratna Dr B R Ambedkar for His Historical, Visionary Role, Contribution To The Nation
Former Chief Justice of India, Justice Uday Umesh Lalit Leads Reading of the Preamble to the Constitution
Delivers Constitution Day Lecture On ‘Constitutional Governance And The Legacy Of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’; Highlights The Significance Of The Preamble, Constitutional Uniqueness And Democratic Values
Academicians, Researchers, Students, Practitioners and Scholars Eulogize Dr Ambedkar’s Constitutional Philosophy And The Future Of Indian Democracy
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:52PM by PIB Delhi

Commemorating 77 years of the adoption of the Constitution of India, the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, celebrated Constitution Day at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), in the National Capital here today, reaffirming the commitment to upholding constitutional values, advancing social justice and strengthening inclusive democracy.

The programme was organised on the theme ‘The Constitution @77: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s Constitutional Vision and the Future of Indian Democracy’, paying tributes to the monumental contribution of Bharat Ratna Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, in shaping the constitutional and democratic foundations of the country.

The celebration was graced by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment and Chairman, Dr Ambedkar Foundation, Dr. Virendra Kumar, as the Chief Guest.

Union Ministers of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale and Shri B.L. Verma, and Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Sudhansh Pant, were among the distinguished dignitaries present on the occasion.

A significant highlight of the programme was the reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India, led by former Chief Justice of India, Justice Uday Umesh Lalit, followed by his special Constitution Day Lecture on ‘Constitutional Governance and the Legacy of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’.

In his address, Justice Lalit elaborated on the significance and utility of the Preamble as an expression of the fundamental philosophy, objectives and guiding principles of the Constitution. He explained how the Preamble provides an essential framework for understanding the constitutional vision and the values that must guide the institutions of the Republic.

Justice Lalit also highlighted the distinctive features of the Indian Constitution, its comprehensive character and its unique place among the constitutional systems of the Asian continent.

Tracing the early constitutional history of independent India, the former Chief Justice of India referred to the landmark judgment in State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951), which examined the validity of the communal allocation of seats in educational institutions in the light of the fundamental rights guaranteed under Article 29(2) of the Constitution.

He elaborated on the subsequent constitutional developments, particularly the enactment of the Constitution (First Amendment) Act, 1951, which inserted Article 15(4), enabling the State to make special provisions for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Justice Lalit also drew attention to the institutional transition following the adoption of the Constitution, highlighting how the Constituent Assembly, in its legislative capacity, functioned as the Provisional Parliament until the first general elections based on universal adult franchise were held in 1951–52.

He explained that this formative period of constitutional development reflected India’s remarkable transition into a democratic Republic founded on the principles of popular sovereignty and equal political participation.

Emphasising that the Constitution is not merely a legal document or an instrument for the distribution of governmental powers, Justice Lalit described it as a living framework that sustains democratic governance and protects the rights and dignity of citizens.

He underscored the importance of constitutional morality, the rule of law and respect for democratic institutions in preserving the spirit of the Constitution, while highlighting the continuing relevance of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity as the guiding principles of the Indian Republic.

The address brought into focus the enduring significance of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s constitutional philosophy and his vision of a society founded upon social democracy, equal citizenship and human dignity for citizenry of the country. It also provided an opportunity to reflect upon the collective responsibility of constitutional institutions and citizens in preserving and strengthening the democratic foundations of the Republic.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar emphasised the continuing relevance of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s ideals in advancing social justice, equality and inclusive development, underscoring the importance of upholding constitutional principles in building an equitable and inclusive society.

Dr Kumar enjoined upon the younger generation to imbibe great principles and values enshrined in the Constitution for equitable, dignified and inclusive socio economic development of all the sections of citizenry in the country. He said the Constitution provides all the citizens the sense of pride, honour, dignity, equality and equitable opportunities to live an honourable, safe and prosperous life.  

The Union Minister said the Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas & Sabka Prayas’ gives sense of security and equality for inclusive socio economic development of all sections of people.

Union Ministers of State, Shri B L Verma and Shri Ramdas Athawale paid rich tributes to Dr B R Ambedkar for his historical and visionary role besides monumental contribution to the nation.

Shri B L Verma underscored the need to uphold all the golden ideals and commandments enshrined in the Constitution adding all sections of people deserve honour, dignity and equitable opportunities for inclusive development.

Shri Ramdas Athawale called for working for the protection and preservation of philosophy, objectives and guiding principles of the Constitution. He added that spirit of democracy, is the cornerstone of unity in diversity in the country.   

Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, shared his perspective on the significance of constitutional values and the continuing efforts towards realising the ideals enshrined in the Constitution. He also urged people to imbibe the spirit of unique values and ideals in the Constitution and serve the people with sincerity and humanely.

Shri Rahul Kashyap, Secretary, National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), Joint Secretaries MoSJE Shri Parveen Kumar Thind, Dr Sandeep R Rathod, Shailendra Kumar, Smt Monali P Dhakate; DDG Ms Pratima Gupta; Ms Nishtha Tiwari, CEO, DWBDNC ; Economic Adviser, Shri Rahees M, Director MoSJE, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat, Director DAF, Shri Vinesh Pachnanda and other senior officers and officials of the Ministry, were present on the occasion.

Deputy Secretary, Shri Kumar Nityananad conducted the proceedings.

The celebration witnessed the participation of Chair Professors, Assistant Professors and Doctoral Fellows associated with Dr. Ambedkar Chairs established in universities across the country, besides academicians, researchers, scholars, Law students, Law practitioners, senior officials and other distinguished invitees.

The participation of representatives of Dr. Ambedkar Chairs added an important academic dimension to the occasion, facilitating meaningful deliberations on constitutional governance, democratic institutions and the contemporary relevance of Dr. Ambedkar’s philosophy.

The programme also reinforced the role of these Chairs and academic institutions in promoting research, teaching, scholarship and dissemination of knowledge about the life, ideas and contributions of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

The Constitution Day celebrations underscored the importance of sustained academic engagement, informed public discourse and greater constitutional awareness in ensuring that the Constitution continues to serve as a living instrument of social transformation and democratic progress.

Through the initiative, Dr. Ambedkar Foundation reaffirmed its commitment to carrying forward the vision and ideals of Babasaheb Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, strengthening constitutional values in public life and fostering a socially just, equitable and inclusive democratic society.

Member of the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal jury , Shri Manouj…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Humane Character of the Story and Alignment with Gandhian Ideals Foremost Consideration for Evaluation: ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal Jury Member Manouj Kadaamh
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:50PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 26 November 2026

 

Ten fiction feature films are competing for the prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), exploring themes of peace, tolerance, empathy, social justice and intercultural dialogue. Member of the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal jury, Shri Manouj Kadaamh and IFFI Creative Director Shri Pankaj Saxena interacted with the media at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of the festival.

Speaking at the interaction, Shri Manouj Kadaamh highlighted the shared commitment of the selected films to using cinema as a medium to communicate meaningful ideas and promote a culture of peace.

Explaining the jury's approach to evaluating the films, Kadaamh said that the foremost consideration was the humane character of the story and its alignment with Gandhian ideals, particularly non-violence and the promotion of peace through cinema. A film's aesthetic and technical qualities, along with the sincerity and conviction with which the filmmaker communicates the intended message, were also important considerations, he said.

Referring to this year's IFFI theme, 'Stories Beyond Borders', he observed that the selected films had taken viewers across various parts of the world offering insights into unfamiliar cultures and perspectives. "Every film has its own potential and aesthetic values. It reflects the socio-economic and cultural aspects of that country. The films which are travelling the whole world are making the juries travel along with them to know their culture. That's the strength of cinema, which introduces you to the world," he said.

Highlighting some of the films in the competition, Kadaamh cited Strawberries as a portrayal of the struggle against injustice towards women and an affirmation of women's strength. He also pointed to The Fall of the Queen, which raises concerns about the patenting of medicines and access to healthcare, and Scroll, which carries an important message for the younger generation. He noted that several films go beyond depicting social problems and encourage audiences to think about workable solutions. He also opined that audience reactions alone could not alone determine a film's merit.

Speaking at the press conference, Pankaj Saxena, Artistic Director of IFFI, said that the ICFT-UNESCO mandate provided a clear framework for selecting films that promote tolerance, peace, understanding and intercultural exchange. He highlighted the responsibility of cinema in shaping society, cautioning that films could be both beneficial and harmful depending on how the medium is used.

Saxena noted that societies in the Global South, particularly those undergoing rapid social and cultural transitions, offer fertile ground for cinematic creativity. He added that films from countries such as Kenya, Haiti and Turkey provide audiences with valuable insights into evolving social realities and cultural dynamics.

He also emphasised that filmmakers need not always provide definitive solutions to social problems, as raising pertinent questions and stimulating public thought are equally essential functions of art. "An artist's job can be to provide solutions, but it can also be to leave open-ended questions. It is absolutely fine, and we care for artists of both types," he said.

Responding to a question on what enables stories to transcend geographical and cultural boundaries, Saxena identified aesthetics and relevance, or form and content, as the essential elements.

Shri Mahesh Kumar moderated the press conference.

About ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal

Instituted at the 46th edition of IFFI in collaboration with the International Council for Film, Television and Audiovisual Communication (ICFT), Paris, under the aegis of UNESCO, the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal recognises films that reflect Mahatma Gandhi's ideals of non-violence, tolerance, intercultural understanding and a culture of peace. The ten films (seven International and three Indian) selected for this year's competition bring together stories from diverse cultural backgrounds, highlighting human relationships, social challenges and shared values.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE CONSTITUTION DAY CELEBRATIONS ORGANISED BY THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
SYNERGY BETWEEN JUDICIAL INDEPENDENCE AND JUDICIAL ACCOUNTABILITY LENDS STRENGTH TO THE ROLE OF THE JUDICIARY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
TIMELY DELIVERY OF JUSTICE IS AN ESSENTIAL COMPONENT OF THE VERY CONCEPT OF JUSTICE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
GREATER EMPHASIS ON INCLUSIVITY AND MERIT WILL FURTHER STRENGTHEN OUR JUDICIARY: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, graced the Constitution Day Celebrations, being organised by the Supreme Court of India, in New Delhi today (November 26, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President extended her greetings to the fellow citizens on Constitution Day. She said that on November 26, 1949, the people of India adopted their Constitution. In 2015, on the auspicious occasion of the 125th birth anniversary of the principal architect of our Constitution, Dr. Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar, it was decided to observe 'Constitution Day' annually on this date. It is a day to pay respectful tribute to the great architect of the Constitution and to the ideals enshrined within it.

The President said that the Supreme Court, High Courts, and the district and lower courts have made an invaluable contribution to the glorious journey of our Republic. Over the past decades, there have been unimaginable changes across many spheres of life. In particular, the influence of technology and media has become increasingly pervasive and profound. While adapting its role to changing circumstances and expectations, the judiciary has upheld and strengthened the fundamental ideals of justice. From time to time, the Indian judiciary has placed special emphasis on judicial accountability, thereby bringing to execution the ideals envisioned by the framers of the Constitution. The synergy between judicial independence and judicial accountability lends strength to the role of the judiciary.

The President said that the timely delivery of justice is an essential component of the very concept of justice. To ensure that justice is accessible in a timely manner, the judiciary is undertaking various initiatives such as simplifying procedures, leveraging technology, and establishing special courts. She noted that despite these efforts, the massive backlog of pending cases remains a significant challenge for our justice delivery system. She expressed confidence that this challenge will be addressed through the concerted efforts being made at every level of the judiciary.

The President said that not everyone possesses the resources required to access the High Courts or the Supreme Court. Our Constitution mandates the provision of justice on the basis of equal opportunity, which includes the facilitation of free legal aid. The objective of this mandate is to ensure that no citizen is denied the opportunity to seek justice due to economic constraints or any other form of hardship. The President emphasized that the true progress of a nation lies in ensuring that every citizen has an equal opportunity to thrive and succeed. She underscored the importance of providing every child with equal access to quality education.  It is also crucial to focus on the quality and reliability of legal representation available to the poor and marginalized sections of society. In this context, the District, State, and National Legal Services Authorities must intensify their efforts to ensure that justice reaches these vulnerable and disadvantaged groups.

The President said that empathy and ethics should be given as much importance as the study of laws in legal education in our country. She urged the leading lights in the lawyers’ community to present inspiring examples for young lawyers. She said that the young lawyers should see that excellence can be blended with empathy, and competence with compassion.

The President said that larger and more active participation of women in the Bench and Bar will help make our society more fair, just, equitable and inclusive. She highlighted that a woman’s perspective can add to inclusion, diversity and balance to judicial decision-making. She underlined the need to encourage greater participation by women as judges and lawyers. Greater emphasis on inclusivity and merit will further strengthen our judiciary.

The President noted that the Supreme Court has taken steps to promote access to justice by prioritising cases relating to specially abled persons, acid attack victims, senior citizens aged above 80 years and persons below the poverty line. She appreciated the steps taken for more effective case management and listing, promoting digital transformation, and encouraging amicable resolution of disputes. She expressed confidence that our judicial fraternity will continue to uphold the idealism with which the members of the Constituent Assembly framed the provisions on the judiciary.
