item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Decoding the Oscars: Natalie Wade Walks Filmmakers Through Submission Process and Global Opportunities at 57th IFFI
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 26 November 2026

 

Filmmakers, students and cinema enthusiasts gained insights into the Academy Awards submission process, eligibility criteria, campaigning and opportunities for emerging talent at a masterclass titled ‘Decoding Academy Awards’, held today at Kala Academy on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

The masterclass was conducted by Ms. Natalie Wade, Vice President of Member Relations and Awards Administration at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. IFFI Festival Director Mr. Ashutosh Gowariker felicitated her on the occasion.

Observing that filmmakers are often unaware of the extensive process involved in submitting a film for Academy Awards consideration, Ms. Wade said the masterclass aimed to demystify the process and familiarise filmmakers with the formal procedures, rules and requirements involved, from the initial submission to the final stages of the awards. Referring to the global recognition of Indian cinema, including The Elephant Whisperers, she highlighted how cinema transcends geographical boundaries, with the Academy representing filmmakers and cinema professionals from across the world, including India.

In her presentation, Ms. Wade explained the eligibility requirements and qualification pathways for General Entry and Best Picture consideration. She outlined the theatrical exhibition requirements, including a qualifying seven-day run in at least one of six designated U.S. metropolitan areas, and discussed eligibility across categories such as Acting, Cinematography, Directing, Film Editing, Music, Sound, Visual Effects and Writing.

She also explained the submission requirements for the International Feature Film, Documentary Feature and Short Film categories, including qualification through recognised international film festivals. The session covered the Academy Screening Room, the platform through which films are made available to Academy members, along with submission requirements, technical specifications and applicable fees.

Highlighting the Academy’s Scientific and Technical Awards, Ms. Wade discussed the recognition of innovations that advance filmmaking technology. She also introduced the Academy’s Global Talent Development Programmes, including the Student Academy Awards, Nicholl Fellowships in Screenwriting and Academy Gold Fellowship for Women, which provide emerging filmmakers and screenwriters with mentorship and professional opportunities.

The masterclass concluded with an interactive session, during which Ms. Wade addressed queries on film eligibility, international submissions, festival qualification pathways and technical requirements. She encouraged filmmakers to reach out for guidance and emphasised that the Academy’s representatives and local contacts could assist filmmakers in navigating the submission process.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman concludes extensive pre-budget consultations for Union Budget 2027-28
More than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the pre-budget consultations
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Finance and Corporate Affairs, Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired a series of pre-budget consultation meetings for the preparation of the Union Budget 2027-28 between 16 and 26 November 2026.

Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman chaired the 13th and final Pre-Budget Consultation with Yuva for the upcoming Union Budget 2027-28, in New Delhi, today.

More than 200 stakeholders representing 13 sectors and stakeholder groups participated in the consultations. These included industry associations, domain experts, leaders of India Inc, academics, youth representatives and practitioners from Agriculture and Rural Development; Manufacturing; MSMEs and Startups; Capital Markets and Banking, Financial Services and Insurance (BFSI); Information Technology; Infrastructure, Energy and Sustainability; Employment and Labour; Housing, Urbanisation and Culture; Health and Social Issues; Research & Development and Higher Education; School Education, Vocational Education, Skilling and Sports; Youth Affairs; and Economics. The consultation meeting with youth representatives was a novel initiative this year.

Ms. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs; Dr. V. Anantha Nageswaran, Chief Economic Adviser; senior officials of the Ministry of Finance; and Secretaries of Ministries and Departments concerned also participated in the discussions.

The consultations generated a wide range of forward-looking recommendations aimed at strengthening India's human capital, innovation ecosystem, manufacturing competitiveness, agricultural productivity, housing security, and educational outcomes. Stakeholders emphasized the need for reforms that can further accelerate economic growth while ensuring broad-based and inclusive development.

Among the key suggestions received were measures to promote the domestic manufacturing of biofertilisers and advanced biotechnology-based agricultural inputs; initiatives to enhance India's competitiveness in Artificial Intelligence through the development of sector-specific AI models optimised for locally available hardware; programmes to strengthen cyber-hygiene awareness among MSMEs and smaller financial institutions; and targeted interventions to support rural youth and workers in transitioning to productive non-farm employment and sustainable enterprises.

Participants also recommended launching a nationwide reading movement to ensure that every child can read and comprehend a newspaper by the end of Grade 5. In the housing sector, stakeholders highlighted the importance of promoting rental housing as a significant avenue for expanding affordable housing in urban areas. Suggestions were also made to accelerate the development of Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities to support young Indians as they transition from education to employment and to entrepreneurship.

Collectively, the recommendations focused on promoting innovation-led growth, expanding employment opportunities, strengthening social and economic infrastructure, and building a more resilient and future-ready economy.

The pre-budget consultations form an important part of the Government's participatory and consultative approach to budget-making, enabling diverse stakeholders to contribute to shaping India's development priorities and growth agenda.

item.content:encoded:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI
Office of PSA in collaboration with MEA, IISc, ORF and GIS to organise 3rd edition of Technology Dialogue focusing on Charting Technological Convergence from 30 November to 2 December 2026
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:33PM by PIB Delhi

The third edition of the Technology Dialogue, themed “Charting Technological Convergence,” will be held from 30 November to 2 December 2026 at the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru. The Dialogue is being convened by the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, in partnership with the Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India; Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru; Observer Research Foundation (ORF); and Global Innovation Square (GIS).

Over the years, Technology Dialogue has emerged as one of India's premier Track 1.5 platforms for technology diplomacy, bringing together senior government officials, policymakers, researchers, industry leaders, investors, and innovators from India and across the world to deliberate on critical and emerging technologies and foster strategic partnerships. While the 2023 edition explored the opportunities and risks associated with disruptive technologies, the 2025 edition focused on technology diplomacy and India's strategic partnerships in critical and emerging technology domains.

Building on these discussions, the 2026 edition will focus on the growing convergence of frontier technologies across sectors and domains. The key domains in focus will be - Artificial Intelligence and Quantum Computing, Semiconductors, Bioeconomy, Neurotechnology, Cybersecurity and Post-Quantum Readiness, and Space Capabilities. As these technologies increasingly intersect, they are transforming global innovation ecosystems and creating new opportunities for scientific advancement, while raising important questions around economic competitiveness, national security, technology governance, and international cooperation. The Dialogue will examine how these technologies can integrate with national technology missions, eventually contributing towards building a globally competitive, resilient, and strategically autonomous innovation ecosystem.

The Dialogue will feature a distinguished and diverse group of thought leaders, including senior representatives from the Government of India and diplomatic missions, international agencies and multilateral institutions, and leading scientists, global technology companies, research organisations, venture capital firms, and deep-tech startups. Leaders and experts from several organisations alongside representatives from India's scientific and technology institutions, will bring perspectives spanning scientific research, industrial innovation, investment, policy, and international cooperation. Their participation will facilitate exchanges between those shaping technology policy, advancing frontier research, developing commercial applications, and financing emerging innovations.

Over the three days, the programme will feature high-level plenary sessions, expert panels, fireside conversations, closed-door policy roundtables, and curated walkthroughs of India's deep-tech and innovation ecosystem. Deliberations will explore the following thematic areas:

· AI x Quantum: Shaping the Future of Computational Intelligence

· Frontier Technologies Unlocking the Bioeconomy Century

· The Brain, the Next Frontier: Neurotechnology Augmenting Human Potential

· Beyond Cybersecurity: What it takes to secure the critical systems

· What and Who Will Determine Semiconductor Competitiveness in the Coming Decades

· Space 2050: Advancing Tech Frontiers for the Great Convergence

Complementing these domain-specific discussions, the Dialogue will address broader issues relating to deep-tech financing and commercialisation, access to advanced computing and foundation models, strategic technology partnerships, advancement in security technologies and responsible AI governance.

Dedicated engagements, including the India–Switzerland AI Policy Roundtable, organised in partnership with Swissnex as a satellite event under the Road to Geneva initiative, leading up to the Geneva AI Summit 2027, will provide opportunities to deepen bilateral technology cooperation. In parallel, a discussion on advances in security technologies will examine their readiness to protect critical infrastructure, identifying solutions that are ready for deployment and those that require further testing and validation.

Consultations on responsible industry behaviour in strategic AI will bring together policymakers, industry leaders, and technology practitioners to contribute to the evolving global discourse on technology governance. Complementing these policy engagements, curated visits to India's space, defence, and deep-tech innovation facilities will offer international delegates and stakeholders first-hand insights into India's emerging technological capabilities and their real-world applications.

A dedicated, activity-driven workshop in partnership with DSCI and GESDA will bring together national and international experts to demonstrate how technology foresight can be practised, moving beyond conceptual discussions to practical application. The workshop will introduce quantitative and qualitative methodological approaches and showcase how advanced digital tools, including artificial intelligence and machine learning, are enhancing foresight capabilities and informing strategic decision-making.

Hosted at IISc, one of India's foremost institutions for scientific research and innovation, the Dialogue seeks to strengthen strategic partnerships, foster cross-sectoral collaboration, and contribute to shaping the future of technology convergence, diplomacy, governance, and innovation.

Read more about the dialogue: www.technologydialogue.in

But what if…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Is Your Smartphone Controlling You? Tamil Thriller SCROLL Sparks a Digital Wake-Up Call at IFFI 2026
Nominated for the Prestigious ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, the Unconventional Film Unfolds Entirely through a Smartphone Screen
“A Thriller That Makes You Think, Not Preach”: Director Kannan S on Scroll and the Perils of Digital Addiction
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:32PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 26 November 2026

 

We scroll for a moment, stay for hours, chase the next notification and surrender to the next swipe. But what if the screen begins to scroll our lives instead? Exploring this unsettling possibility, Tamil feature film Scroll examines smartphone addiction, algorithmic manipulation and digital enslavement at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

Director-producer Kannan S, along with lead actors Aravind Sundar and Kavya Anil, discussed the film's unconventional storytelling, experimental filmmaking techniques and contemporary themes at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of the festival.

Selected for the Indian Panorama section, Scroll is the only Tamil film nominated for the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal at IFFI 2026. The 128-minute psychological thriller uses an innovative screen-life format, unfolding its narrative entirely through a mobile phone interface.

The film follows a young man battling smartphone addiction who downloads an application in an attempt to regain control of his life. What begins as a promise of digital liberation through gamified tasks and rewards soon turns into a cycle of disturbing challenges and psychological coercion.

Speaking about the film's nomination for the ICFT-UNESCO Gandhi Medal, director Kannan S highlighted the relevance of Gandhian values of truth, non-violence and self-restraint in an increasingly technology-driven world. Drawing inspiration from real-world digital phenomena such as the Blue Whale Challenge, he said the film seeks to encourage young audiences to reflect on unchecked digital dependence without sounding preachy. “We wanted to deliver a powerful social message through an engaging thriller rather than a lecture,” he remarked.

Kannan also spoke about the challenges of making a film entirely within a mobile phone interface. Most actors shot their portions independently from different locations, with several cast members meeting in person for the first time at the festival. “The biggest challenge was to sustain cinematic tension within the limited frame of a mobile screen while keeping the narrative gripping and impactful,” he explained.

Lead actor Aravind Sundar, who plays the protagonist, reflected on the irony of trying to overcome smartphone addiction through another application. He said everyday life itself became his preparation for the role, “we are constantly rehearsing this reality every single day.” He added that the film's distinctive format immerses audiences in the protagonist's claustrophobic digital world.

Kavya Anil highlighted the script's unconventional narrative and contemporary relevance. She said the film neither glorifies harmful digital challenges nor sensationalises their consequences but offers a thought-provoking examination of technology's ability to both connect and control.

The press conference was moderated by Shri Suresh Kumar M.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Jal Shakti
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, Ministry of Jal Shakti Organises the Second Regional Conference at Agra
​​​​​​​Union Jal Shakti Minister Shri C.R. Paatil said that access to tap connections must be complemented by assured delivery of safe drinking water to rural households
Seven Northern States and Union Territories deliberate on accelerating implementation and ensuring long-term functionality of rural drinking water supply schemes
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:17PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, organised the Second Regional Conference on Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 at Agra, Uttar Pradesh, bringing together representatives of seven northern States and Union Territories to deliberate on key strategies for accelerating implementation, strengthening sustainability and ensuring long-term functionality of rural drinking water supply systems. The conference forms part of a series of regional consultations being organised following the Departmental Summit on Water and provides a platform for States and Union Territories to review progress, share best practices and discuss solutions to common challenges.

Senior officials from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh participated in the conference along with representatives from the National Jal Jeevan Mission, State Water and Sanitation Missions, line Ministries viz. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MoSDE), and Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD). Deliberations focused on sustainability, institutional reforms, convergence, operation and maintenance, groundwater management and community-led water governance.

During the ministerial session, a Jal Kalash ceremony was performed by the dignitaries, symbolising respect for water and reaffirming the collective resolve towards water conservation, source sustainability and responsible water management.

Chairing the Ministerial Session at the Conference, Union Minister of Jal Shakti Shri C.R. Paatil highlighted the transformative impact of Jal Jeevan Mission in improving the quality of life in rural India and reducing the drudgery faced by women and girls. Referring to the vision of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for ensuring water security, he emphasised that while significant progress has been made in providing tap water connections across rural households, the next phase of Jal Jeevan Mission must focus on ensuring regular, adequate and safe drinking water supply through sustainable and community-owned service delivery systems.

Further, the Union Minister added that sustainability should remain at the core of all efforts under JJM 2.0. He also underlined the need for timely implementation, greater accountability and collaborative action by States and Union Territories to achieve the Mission's objectives.

Referring to Jal Sanchay Jan Bhagidari se Jan Aandolan, Shri Paatil highlighted the importance of transforming water conservation into a people's movement through active community participation. He emphasised the need to promote groundwater recharge, rainwater harvesting and source protection measures through convergence with ongoing development programmes. Stressing that water conservation is a shared responsibility, he called upon States to strengthen community ownership through initiatives such as Jal Arpan and Jal Utsav and to actively exchange best practices for ensuring sustainable drinking water services for every rural household.

Shri S. P Singh Baghel, Union Minister (Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairyings; Panchayati Raj) and Member of Parliament from Agra, highlighted the importance of sustained coordination among the Central and State Governments, district administrations and implementing agencies in addressing drinking water challenges and ensuring water security. Referring to the regional context, he noted the significance of effective water resource management and inter-regional coordination in ensuring adequate water availability. He expressed confidence that the deliberations during the conference would contribute to identifying practical solutions for strengthening reliable and sustainable rural drinking water services.

Welcoming the delegates, Shri Swatantra Dev Singh, Cabinet Minister for Jal Shakti and Flood Control, Uttar Pradesh, highlighted the remarkable progress achieved under Jal Jeevan Mission in the State. He noted that tap water coverage in rural Uttar Pradesh has expanded significantly since 2019, with drinking water supply schemes being implemented across the State through a transparent and accelerated approach despite operational  challenges. He said that sustained efforts have led to substantial improvement in rural drinking water access, with work on the remaining schemes progressing rapidly towards universal coverage.

Referring to the water-stressed regions of Bundelkhand and Vindhya, Shri Singh highlighted the transformative impact of Jal Jeevan Mission in addressing long-standing drinking water challenges. He noted that districts which once faced acute water scarcity and seasonal distress have witnessed significant improvements in access to safe drinking water through household tap connections. Emphasising the importance of knowledge sharing and collaborative learning, he observed that the Regional Conference provides an important platform for States and Union Territories to exchange experiences, share best practices and strengthen implementation strategies for ensuring sustainable rural drinking water service delivery.

Secretary, DDWS, Shri Ashok K.K Meena, highlighted that sustainability of rural drinking water services requires a whole-of-government approach and cannot be achieved through the drinking water sector alone. He emphasised the importance of convergence across sectors, including skilling, source sustainability, financing, Panchayati Raj institutions and community ownership, for ensuring long-term functionality of rural water supply systems.

Emphasising the need to move beyond infrastructure creation, Shri Meena called upon States and Union Territories to focus on source sustainability, sustainable operation and maintenance, financial planning, skilled local manpower and strengthened Gram Panchayat-led governance. He highlighted the role of tools such as the Decision Support System (DSS) for evidence-based planning, end-to-end digital mapping of water supply assets under Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and empowerment of Gram Panchayats, Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) for improving service delivery, accountability and long-term sustainability.

During another session of the conference Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM, outlined the need for transitioning from infrastructure development to sustainable rural drinking water service delivery under Jal Jeevan Mission 2. It was highlighted that the focus would be on ensuring regular, adequate and quality drinking water supply through effective operation and maintenance of existing infrastructure for the next 25–30 years. The importance of clearly defined roles and responsibilities of district administrations, District Magistrates and Panchayati Raj Institutions at all levels was underscored for ensuring long-term sustainability of rural water supply systems.

Shri Soan also shared about the importance of inter-departmental convergence among Public Health Engineering, Rural Development, Panchayati Raj, Skill Development and Tribal Affairs Departments for strengthening source sustainability and O&M. It was informed that five regional conferences were being organised to deliberate on key reforms and implementation strategies, with their outcomes to be reviewed at a national-level conference. The consolidated progress would subsequently be presented to the Hon’ble Prime Minister, with collective efforts of the Centre, States and local institutions being emphasised for achieving the objectives of Jal Jeevan Mission by December 2028.

Shri D. Senthil Pandiyan, Joint Secretary, DDWS, during the presentation by representatives of MoRD, emphasised the importance of source sustainability through geotagging of drinking water sources and implementation of the Decision Support System (DSS). Highlighting the integration of data from six departments and agencies to identify at-risk water sources, he urged States to undertake physical verification, pre- and post-monsoon water quality testing, and prepare village-level source augmentation plans through convergence with Rural Development and Panchayati Raj institutions and integration with GPDP. States were requested to expedite geotagging, water quality testing and DSS implementation, and update progress by 31 December 2026.

As the conference coincided with Constitution Day, the dignitaries and participants also jointly read the Preamble to the Constitution of India, reiterating their commitment to the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

The key reform pillars under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0 were presented by Shri Y.K. Singh, Director, NJJM with emphasis on strengthening Gram Panchayats and district-level institutions for sustainable rural water service delivery. The importance of performance benchmarking, healthy competition, third-party inspections, water quality monitoring, source sustainability and digital governance through the Sujalam Bharat portal was highlighted. States were urged to expedite the creation of Sujalam Bharat IDs, GIS-based asset tagging and pipeline mapping, and strengthen community participation through Har Ghar Jal certification, Jal Arpan, Jal Seva Arpan and Jal Utsav initiatives.

The need for time-bound capacity building of Gram Panchayat functionaries, VWSC members and district technical teams was underscored, along with the deployment of trained Nal Jal Mitras to strengthen village-level operation and maintenance. States were also encouraged to formulate O&M policies, adopt preventive maintenance practices, ensure financial sustainability, and promote research, innovation and outcome-based financing. The importance of adhering to the timelines for implementing the identified reforms, which were linked to the payment mechanism, was emphasised to ensure smooth financial flows and sustainable drinking water service delivery.

Shri Y.K. Singh further presented on Institutional and Financial Sustainability, highlighting the utilisation of 16th Finance Commission tied grants earmarked for water and sanitation to strengthen the financial capacity of Gram Panchayats for operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems. The importance of integrating these resources with other convergence funds and user-charge collections and incorporating water and sanitation activities into GPDPs, was emphasised. Priority areas such as source sustainability, water quality management, electricity costs, solarisation of water supply schemes, drainage and greywater management were also highlighted to ensure sustainable service delivery at the village level.

Smt. Kritika Kulhari, Deputy Secretary, NJJM, presented on PMJANMAN and DAJGUA and highlighted the progress and implementation requirements, emphasising the need to ensure saturation of rural drinking water supply in identified tribal habitations. She focused on the need to ensure drinking water coverage in all identified PVTG and tribal-majority habitations within the stipulated timelines.

States were requested to submit complete proposals in accordance with the prescribed DPR checklist, supported by Chief Secretary-led Apex Committee approval, joint certification by the Tribal Affairs and concerned water supply departments, non-duplication certificates and appropriate technical justifications. States were urged to coordinate with their respective Tribal Affairs Departments to identify any uncovered habitations, update records and submit complete proposals at the earliest to facilitate timely approval and implementation of drinking water supply schemes.

Representatives from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MoSDE), Shri Avinash Kishore presented on the skilling of Nal Jal Mitras, Sujalam Shakti and skill formalization and highlighted ongoing efforts to strengthen skill ecosystems and capacity-building initiatives for rural water sector personnel, including local technicians, Plumbers, Masonry, Electricians and operators.

Shri Gowri Shankar and Shri Raj Kishore Singh, officials from Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), delivered a detail presentation highlighting convergence opportunities with programmes such as VB-G RAM G for creation of water conservation structures, source strengthening measures, support for sustainability interventions and incorporation of Sujalam Shakti.

Senior officials from the participating States and Union Territories made presentations focusing on updates on progress achieved under the Mission and shared experiences related to state initiatives, digital interventions, IEC, convergence, implementation of sustainability measures, institutional reforms and community participation initiatives.

Delegates exchanged best practices and discussed emerging challenges related to source sustainability, functionality of schemes, operation and maintenance, capacity building and financial sustainability. Participants also deliberated on innovative approaches adopted at the State level for improving service delivery and strengthening governance systems.

The conference featured deliberations on implementation of Comprehensive Implementation and Reform Plans (CIRPs), sustainable operation and maintenance, source sustainability, financial sustainability and institutional strengthening. Participants also discussed community ownership, Panchayat-led water governance, capacity development and inter-ministerial convergence as key enablers for ensuring long-term functionality and sustainable rural drinking water service delivery under JJM 2.0.

The second day of the conference will undertake field visits to five selected rural drinking water supply schemes and villages in Uttar Pradesh to observe Jal Arpan and best practices in service delivery, source sustainability, operation and maintenance and community-led water governance. The field exposure is expected to facilitate cross-learning and support replication of successful models across participating States and Union Territories.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Three Antiquities Repatriated from USA and Netherlands Handed Over to Tamil Nadu Police by ASI
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:14PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards the recovery and restitution of India’s cultural heritage, the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) today handed over three repatriated antiquities to the Idol Wing CID, Tamil Nadu Police, at Dharohar Bhawan, New Delhi.

The antiquities, comprising two bronze idols from the Smithsonian Museum, USA, and one bronze idol from The Hague, Netherlands, were formally handed over to the respective police officials by the ASI.

The antiquities include:

1. Saint Sundarar with Paravai Nachiyar: A 16th-century bronze idol belonging to the Vijayanagara period was photographed in 1956 at the Shiva Temple, Sri Narisvara, Viracholapuram, Kallakurichi Taluk, Tamil Nadu. It was repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum, USA.

2. Saint Kannappa Nayanar: This Chola-period bronze idol from Arulmigu Agneeswarasamy Temple, Thirupugalur, Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu, depicts the Shaivite saint in a tribhanga standing posture, with his right hand raised towards his eye. It was repatriated from The Hague, Netherlands.

3. Somaskanda (Shiva and Uma): This 12th-century Chola-period bronze idol was photographed in 1959 at Siva Temple, Sri Visvanatha, Alattur, Mannargudi Taluk, Thanjavur district, Tamil Nadu. It was repatriated from the Smithsonian Museum, USA.

The formal handover was undertaken by Shri Yadubir Singh Rawat, Director-General, Archaeological Survey of India along with other ASI representatives.

The restitution of these antiquities marks an important milestone in India’s ongoing efforts to bring its cultural treasures back to their rightful home. ASI continues to work towards the identification, recovery and repatriation of India’s lost heritage in coordination with national and international agencies.

 ***

President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA TO VISIT KERALAM, MIZORAM AND NAGALAND FROM NOVEMBER 27 TO DECEMBER 2
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 7:06PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu will visit Keralam, Mizoram and Nagaland from November 27 to December 2, 2026.

On November 27, the President will visit Adi Shankaracharya's birthplace at Thalayattumpilli, Kalady, Vadakkumbhagom, Keralam. On the same day, she will also grace the valedictory ceremony of the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College at Thrissur, Keralam.

On November 28, the President will grace the Autumn Term 2026 Passing Out Parade at Indian Naval Academy, Ezhimala, Keralam.

On November 29, the President will visit the Ropuiliani Tribal Freedom Fighters’ Museum at Kelsih, Mizoram.

On November 30, the President will grace Mizoram University's 21st convocation and the closing ceremony of its Silver Jubilee celebrations at Aizawl.

On December 1, the President will grace the inaugural ceremony of the 27th Hornbill Festival at Kisama, Nagaland.

item.title: Public Sector Banks (PSBs) grow stronger with prudent banking practices and strong underwriting capabilities
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance
item.description: Ministry of Finance Public Sector Banks (PSBs) grow stronger with prudent banking practices and strong underwriting capabilities PSB asset quality at all-time high with historically low stressed assets PSBs’ gross advances reach ₹127 lakh crore with 18.8% y-o-y growth Retail, agriculture and MSME advances grow at 17.0%, 19.5% and 20.4%, respectively Total deposits grow to ₹165.2 lakh crore at 12.9% y-o-y Net NPA ratio at 0.33%; Gross NPAs fall to ₹44,100 crore Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi The Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue to grow…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
Public Sector Banks (PSBs) grow stronger with prudent banking practices and strong underwriting capabilities
PSB asset quality at all-time high with historically low stressed assets
PSBs’ gross advances reach ₹127 lakh crore with 18.8% y-o-y growth
Retail, agriculture and MSME advances grow at 17.0%, 19.5% and 20.4%, respectively
Total deposits grow to ₹165.2 lakh crore at 12.9% y-o-y
Net NPA ratio at 0.33%; Gross NPAs fall to ₹44,100 crore
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 6:47PM by PIB Delhi

The Public Sector Banks (PSBs) continue to grow rapidly with high asset quality, ably supported by reform enabled prudent credit underwriting and effective risk management policies. The systemic reforms instituted in PSBs are showing fruitful results in the form of high quality rapidly paced credit growth across sectors, especially productive credit growth. Credit delivery to MSMEs and corporates by PSBs has also shown remarkable improvement with both growing at fast pace along with Agriculture and Retail. At the same time, the asset quality continues to improve to all-time best, supported by low slippages and strong recoveries in impaired assets. The institutionalisation of reforms has created a strong system of governance led banking in PSBs, supporting economic upcycle.

PSBs’ advances are growing rapidly at 15.1% in last 5-years and reached ₹127 lakh crore as on 30.9.2026. However, at the same time PSBs are also showing signs of strong prudence in credit underwriting through rapidly declining slippages. As against advances of ₹67.7 lakh crore as on 31.3.2021, the slippages were as high as ₹1.44 lakh crore at a rate of 2.35% in FY2021-22. It has now come down to just ₹38,780 crore against advances of ₹127 lakh crore in H1FY2026-27, recording slippage ratio of just 0.62%, a remarkable sign of growth with prudence.

 

The credit growth is not only prudent in terms of asset quality, but also is well diversified and focused across sectors. PSBs are extending credit to productive and consumptive sectors simultaneously with high credit growth in Retail, Agriculture, MSME and corporate sectors evenly balanced. While credit to retail and agriculture continues at strong rate over past more than 5-years, credit to MSME and corporates have also picked up to outpace other sectors marginally.

Looking at bank-wise performance in terms of credit growth, almost all banks are evenly extending credit with Bank of Maharashtra outpacing others, while large banks such as, State Bank of India, Canara Bank, Bank of Baroda and Punjab National Bank are also growing rapidly.

Even with high credit growth, continued improvement in slippages ratio is observed across banks with only Punjab & Sind Bank recording marginal decline in slippage ratio, though already having low slippage ratio of 0.57%. Amongst large banks, State Bank of India, Punjab National Bank and Canara Bank continues to have low slippages. All PSBs now have slippage ratio of less than 1%.

The lower slippages have helped banks in maintaining low NPA levels, though aided by sufficient provisioning and strong recovery also. As a result of combined efforts in prudent underwriting and efficient collections, PSBs are maintaining significantly low net NPAs of 0.33%, amounting Rs. 44,100 crore only, in advances of more than Rs. 127 lakh crore. PSBs continue to have significantly low stress in the form of SMAs also, with aggregate advances of only ₹18,800 crore falling in SMA 1 and 2 amongst advances above ₹5 crore. PSBs continue to improve in SMA levels also with ratio of SMA 1 & 2 advances of above ₹5 crore to total standard advances being only 0.14% as on 30.9.2026, as against 0.24% as on 30.9.2025.

Prudent credit underwriting and efficient risk management practices are paving way for a stronger and robust banking sector having capability to support credit needs of the economy for long term.

***

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
Ministry of Panchayati Raj observes Constitution Day; Panchayats and Rural Local Bodies across the country participate in Mass Readings of the Preamble in Local Languages
Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj, Dr. Vineet Joshi leads collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India in New Delhi; States/UTs coordinate participation of Panchayati Raj Institutions and Rural Local Bodies nationwide
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 6:46PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Panchayati Raj today commemorated the Constitution Day through a coordinated nationwide exercise, with programmes organised at the Ministry as well as at the Panchayat level to promote constitutional awareness and strengthen citizen engagement across rural India. Shri (Dr.) Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj led the senior officers and staff of the Ministry in the collective reading of the Preamble to the Constitution of India, at New Delhi.

Across the country, Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) and Rural Local Bodies (RLBs) organised mass readings of the Preamble in their respective local languages, witnessing enthusiastic participation at the grassroots. The Ministry coordinated closely with the Panchayati Raj Departments of States/UTs to ensure preparedness and wide participation in the nationwide observance. These collective efforts reaffirmed the constitutional values of Justice, Liberty, Equality and Fraternity and strengthened democratic awareness across rural India.

item.title: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Announces National Highway Projects Worth ₹75,000 Crore for West Bengal
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
item.description: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Announces National Highway Projects Worth ₹75,000 Crore for West Bengal 22 National Highway projects worth over ₹8,700 crore inaugurated and foundation stones laid; ₹14,000-crore Kolkata Ring Road, Dankuni–Kolaghat Eight-Lane Corridor and Moregram–Kishanganj High-Speed Corridor among major announcements Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Road Transport & Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 22 National Highway…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Road Transport & Highways
Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Announces National Highway Projects Worth ₹75,000 Crore for West Bengal
22 National Highway projects worth over ₹8,700 crore inaugurated and foundation stones laid; ₹14,000-crore Kolkata Ring Road, Dankuni–Kolaghat Eight-Lane Corridor and Moregram–Kishanganj High-Speed Corridor among major announcements
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 6:10PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Road Transport & Highways Shri Nitin Gadkari today inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 22 National Highway projects worth more than ₹8,700 crore at Kolaghat, East Medinipur, West Bengal. The programme was attended by West Bengal Chief Minister Shri Suvendu Adhikari, State Public Works Minister Shri Ajay Kumar Poddar, Minister of State Shri Nadiyar Chandra Bauri, Members of Parliament, Members of the Legislative Assembly, public representatives and senior officials from the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH), National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the State Government.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Gadkari announced a pipeline of road infrastructure projects worth approximately ₹75,000 crore for West Bengal, encompassing high-speed corridors, expressways, bridges, road widening and road safety improvements. Highlighting the role of infrastructure in economic and social development, he said that efficient road connectivity is essential for industrial growth, trade, agricultural development and tourism. It also facilitates investment, generates employment and improves people's access to markets, healthcare, education and other essential services.

The Minister stated that National Highway projects worth approximately ₹40,000 crore had been completed in West Bengal, while works worth around ₹35,000 crore were underway. He emphasised the need for timely land acquisition and necessary clearances to ensure the expeditious implementation of projects.

Two Major National Highway Projects Dedicated to the Nation

Two important National Highway projects were inaugurated and dedicated to the nation:

  • Palsit–Dankuni section of NH-19: The 63.83-km stretch has been upgraded to six lanes. It will strengthen connectivity between Howrah, Hooghly and Burdwan, facilitate faster freight movement and support commercial activities along the Kolkata–Durgapur industrial corridor.
  • Four-lane bridge over the Ganga at Farakka: Constructed at a cost of ₹521.20 crore, the bridge and its connecting roads will improve connectivity between Murshidabad and Malda, reduce travel time across the Ganga and facilitate movement towards North Bengal.

Foundation Stones Laid for 20 National Highway Projects

Foundation stones were laid for 20 projects aimed at improving road safety, strengthening bridge infrastructure and enhancing connectivity across the State.

Under the Road Safety Scheme, 57 Vehicle Underpasses (VUPs) and Light Vehicle Underpasses (LVUPs) on NH-12 and NH-19 will facilitate safer and smoother traffic movement. The Ramanagar Bypass on NH-116B will help ease congestion within the town, while road-widening and bypass works will reduce travel time and fuel consumption.

Under the Setubandhan Scheme, two major bridge projects at Norghat and over the Dwarkeshwar River will improve regional connectivity. These projects will strengthen access to tourism destinations such as Digha, Mandarmani, Tajpur and Bakkhali, supporting tourism and fisheries-related activities. Improved connectivity towards the Jharkhand border at the Gowai River check post will also facilitate interstate freight movement.

Collectively, these projects will improve connectivity between Kolkata, Krishnanagar, Baharampur, Malda and Durgapur.

Major Highway and Expressway Projects Announced

Among the major projects announced by Shri Gadkari are:

  • Kolkata Ring Road: A 250-km Ring Road at an estimated cost of ₹14,000 crore. It will connect Kolkata with Howrah and North and South 24 Parganas and link Kona Expressway, Belgharia Expressway and Kalyani Expressway, providing an alternative route for long-distance traffic and helping ease congestion in Kolkata.
  • Dankuni–Kolaghat Eight-Lane Corridor: A 58-km, eight-lane highway at an estimated cost of ₹20,000 crore. The project is expected to reduce travel time by approximately 1.5 hours for vehicles travelling from Kolkata towards Kharagpur, Balasore and Bhubaneswar and improve connectivity with Haldia Port.
  • Moregram–Kishanganj High-Speed Corridor: A 245-km, four-lane corridor at an estimated cost of ₹12,000 crore, including a 91-km stretch in West Bengal with an investment of ₹4,500 crore. It will strengthen connectivity between NH-12 and NH-27 and improve access to border areas.
  • Barasat–Petrapole Highway: A 75-km, four-lane highway at an estimated cost of ₹8,000 crore to improve connectivity between Barasat, Basirhat and Bangaon and strengthen cross-border connectivity with Bangladesh.
  • Belgharia Expressway: A 7-km, six-lane elevated road at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore to improve connectivity to Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose International Airport and ease traffic pressure between North Kolkata and NH-19.

District Connectivity, Bridge Development and Road Widening

The Minister also announced several projects to strengthen connectivity across districts and improve access to important economic and tourism centres. These include:

  • A four-lane bridge over the Mayurakshi River in Birbhum district at an estimated cost of ₹1,000 crore.
  • A 15-km, four-lane road from Rampurhat to Sinchura at a cost of ₹875 crore.
  • Improvement of 34 km of NH-131A between Malda and Durgapur at a cost of ₹750 crore.
  • Construction of bridges and four-lane roads in Malbazar, Gurjan, Jhora, Mal and Neora in Jalpaiguri district at a cost of ₹375 crore.
  • A six-km, four-lane bridge over the Damodar River at a cost of ₹300 crore.
  • A bridge over the Mahananda River in Darjeeling district at a cost of ₹270 crore.
  • Widening of 47.55 km of roads between Telipara–Jumuar and Birpara–Falakata at a cost of ₹1,500 crore.
  • Widening of 106.61 km of NH-512 between Gazole and Hili at a cost of ₹3,000 crore.
  • Widening of 31.24 km of NH-117 (New NH-12) between Joka and Diamond Harbour at a cost of ₹1,000 crore.
  • Widening of 89 km of NH-116B between Nandakumar and Digha at a cost of ₹2,700 crore.
  • A 54-km road project between Namkhana and NH-12 at an estimated cost of ₹500 crore to ease congestion between Diamond Harbour and Namkhana and improve identified accident-prone locations.

Strengthening Road Safety and Interstate Connectivity

Shri Gadkari also announced improvement works at 59 identified black spots across West Bengal at an estimated cost of ₹5,100 crore. These include 25 locations in Malda, 20 in Nadia, nine in Jalpaiguri and five in Paschim Bardhaman. The proposed works include Vehicle Underpasses, Light Vehicle Underpasses and service roads to improve traffic movement and address accident-prone locations.

Highlighting the importance of interstate connectivity, the Minister referred to the 570-km, six-lane Gorakhpur–Siliguri Greenfield Highway, approved at an estimated cost of ₹38,000 crore, and the proposed Siliguri–Guwahati High-Speed Corridor, for which the Detailed Project Report has been completed. He also highlighted the Kharagpur–Bardhaman–Moregram Greenfield Expressway, Varanasi–Kolkata Greenfield Highway and proposed Raxaul–Haldia corridor, which will strengthen connectivity with Bihar, Jharkhand and important economic centres, including Haldia Port.

Shri Gadkari emphasised that the planned highway network would facilitate the movement of goods, improve access to industrial and agricultural centres, support tourism and create new economic opportunities.

Shri Nitin Gadkari appreciated the State Government in facilitating timely land acquisition, removing encroachment and necessary clearances for expeditious implementation of the projects in last 6 months and expecting the same continuous support in future projects also.

The initiatives will strengthen West Bengal's road infrastructure and its connectivity with neighbouring States, ports, airports, industrial centres and international borders, supporting trade, regional development and improved mobility for citizens.

***

GDH/DS/HJ

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs Constitution Day 2026 Celebrated Across the Country with Enthusiasm and Wide Public Participation Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) was celebrated across the country today, 26th November, 2026, to mark the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. The occasion reminds us of the values and principles enshrined in the Constitution and our collective responsibility to uphold them. The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Constitution Day 2026 Celebrated Across the Country with Enthusiasm and Wide Public Participation
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:54PM by PIB Delhi

Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) was celebrated across the country today, 26th November, 2026, to mark the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. The occasion reminds us of the values and principles enshrined in the Constitution and our collective responsibility to uphold them.

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, facilitated an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. Citizens from across the country participated in the initiative by reading the Preamble, obtaining certificates and sharing them on social media.

The Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs also observed Constitution Day at Parliament House, where officers and officials of the Ministry collectively read the Preamble at 11:00 AM under the leadership of the Secretary, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. The reading reaffirmed their commitment to the constitutional values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.

The Constitution Quiz was also organised by Department of Youth Affairs through the MyGov and MyBharat portals from 18th to 26th November, 2026, to promote awareness about the Constitution, particularly among young people. Further, Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad was organised across 786 districts in all 36 States and Union Territories from 24th to 26th November, 2026, to encourage youth participation and engagement.

Various activities were organised by Ministries and Departments of the Government of India, State and Union Territory Governments, educational institutions and other organisations. These included reading of the Preamble, seminars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, cultural programmes and awareness campaigns.

Constitution Day provides an opportunity to remember the contribution of the makers of the Constitution, particularly Bharat Ratna Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, Chairman of the Drafting Committee, and to renew our commitment to the ideals of the Constitution.

The celebrations reaffirmed the importance of constitutional values, responsible citizenship and active participation in strengthening India's democracy.

***

ISA

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Rural Development
item.description: Ministry of Rural Development Department of Land Resources Showcases Land Records Modernisation Initiatives to Sri Lankan Delegation Shri Dilip Kumar, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, highlights India’s digital land governance reforms during interaction with Sri Lankan delegation Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, today hosted a delegation of civil servants from Sri Lanka visiting India under an exposure programme coordinated by the National Centre for Good…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Rural Development
Department of Land Resources Showcases Land Records Modernisation Initiatives to Sri Lankan Delegation
Shri Dilip Kumar, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, highlights India’s digital land governance reforms during interaction with Sri Lankan delegation
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Land Resources (DoLR), Ministry of Rural Development, today hosted a delegation of civil servants from Sri Lanka visiting India under an exposure programme coordinated by the National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG). The interaction focused on India’s experience in digitising and modernising land records, with emphasis on the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP), computerisation of registration process, survey and re-survey, NAKSHA and Land Stack initiative implementation.

The Sri Lankan delegation was led by Ms. I.B. Gunawardhana, Additional Land Commissioner and Team Leader, and included Dr. A.P. Singh, Associate Professor and Course Coordinator, National Centre for Good Governance (NCGG) and Ms. G.D. Nadeeka, Land Commissioner along with senior officials from Sri Lanka’s land, survey and administrative services.

Welcoming the delegation, Shri Dilip Kumar, Secretary, Department of Land Resources, highlighted India’s efforts towards strengthening land governance through digital transformation, technology-driven reforms and integrated land information systems. He provided an overview of the Department’s key initiatives and schemes, emphasising the role of digitisation in enhancing transparency, improving service delivery and making land administration more efficient and citizen-centric.

“Digital transformation of land records is essential for transparent, efficient and citizen-centric land governance. Sharing our experiences and learning from one another helps strengthen institutional capacity and advance land administration reforms,” said Shri Dilip Kumar.

During the interaction, Shri Shyam Kumar, Director, Land Resources presented an overview of DILRMP and NAKSHA, highlighting key achievements, technological interventions and the progress made in land records modernisation, geospatial mapping and integration of land-related databases.

The interaction also covered the integration of property registration with land records through paperless registration and automated mutation, enabling electronic transmission of registration details to revenue authorities for timely updating of land records, reducing delays and manual intervention.

The delegation was also briefed on the Bharat Land Stack, an integrated GIS-based platform bringing together land records, geospatial data, property registration, zoning, building approvals, litigation and other land-related information to provide a unified digital view of land parcels.

The interaction facilitated the exchange of experiences on digital land governance and technology-driven reforms, highlighting opportunities for greater cooperation and knowledge-sharing between India and Sri Lanka.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
National Workshop on Unlocking Market-Based Financing under the Urban Challenge Fund
There is need to change our approach towards urban development and build capacities in order to conceptualise and ground transformative projects across the urban landscape : Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:48PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), organised a National Workshop on “Unlocking Market-Based Financing for Urban Challenge Fund Projects” on 26th November 2026 at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi. The workshop was held to help cities prepare bankable projects and move towards market-based financing of urban infrastructure.

Municipal Commissioners and Chiefs of Development Authorities from 25 million plus cities and State Mission Directors of the respective States took part in the workshop, along with sectoral experts and senior officials of DoUD, MoHUA. Financial institutions, including Asian Development Bank (ADB), the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and Housing and Urban Development Corporation (HUDCO), also participated. Knowledge institutions, including CEPT University, IIT Kharagpur, ISEG, Janaagraha, NIT Calicut, NIUA and SPA, supported the cities in the sessions.

The workshop provided handholding to cities on different aspects of preparing and financing urban projects. The sessions covered the UCF architecture, international examples of how projects under each vertical were financed, and reforms and enablers, including improving own-source revenue, the urban road reform initiative, city economic plans, carbon credit markets and the expectations of private investors. Also, session on PPPs covered project screening, structuring, risk allocation, revenue streams followed by city specific experiences.

Cities then worked in groups, each facilitated by a sectoral expert and knowledge institution, to ideate and structure priority projects for their cities based on learnings during the workshop and cross-learnings from other states, and reported their outcomes and proposed projects during the session.

The UCF has been designed as a shift from a grant-based approach to a market-linked, reform-driven and outcome-oriented framework for urban infrastructure. A Central Assistance of ₹1 lakh crore is provisioned to catalyse nearly ₹4 lakh crore of investment. Projects are bucketed under three verticals: Cities as Growth Hubs, Creative Redevelopment of Cities, and Water & Sanitation. So far, Projects worth more than ₹50,000 crore from 16 States/UTs have been approved through National Apex Committee meetings across all three verticals.

The projects are structured to attract private capital and market finance. Against the minimum requirement of 50 per cent mobilisation through loans, municipal bonds or PPPs, around 61 per cent has been proposed to be mobilised through these modes by the States. Pushing reforms in the cities is an integral part of the UCF and foundational to the challenge mode, with reforms ranging from digital, financial, planning and governance measures.

National Apex Committee meetings are held in the first week of every month under the chairmanship of Secretary, DoUD, MoHUA and some notable projects approved included Creative Redevelopment of Cities projects in Patna, Lucknow and Varanasi; Comprehensive development of Warangal city, Lucknow (waste-to-energy) and Tamil Nadu (smart metering, water treatment and waste-to-energy); and Cities as Growth Hubs projects in Assam (Sarusajai, Guwahati) and Sikkim (Gangtok Gateway).

Secretary DoUD, MoHUA emphasised, ‘There is need to change our approach towards urban development and build capacities in order to conceptualise and ground transformative projects across the urban landscape. The workshop is an affirmative step in that direction to equip cities with the skills and ideas required to submit bankable projects under UCF.’

item.title: “One Person’s Holiday, Another’s Home”: When Two Worlds Collide in A Few Days in the Sun at IFFI 2026
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting “One Person’s Holiday, Another’s Home”: When Two Worlds Collide in A Few Days in the Sun at IFFI 2026 A Thriller from Mexico’s Riviera Maya asks how Privilege and the Struggle to Survive can Bring People Closer than they Expect Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:48PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 26 November 2026 At a press conference held at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today, director Mauro Mueller, writer José David Figueroa García and producer Leslie Holleran discussed their bilingual film A Few…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“One Person’s Holiday, Another’s Home”: When Two Worlds Collide in A Few Days in the Sun at IFFI 2026
A Thriller from Mexico’s Riviera Maya asks how Privilege and the Struggle to Survive can Bring People Closer than they Expect
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:48PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 26 November 2026

 

At a press conference held at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today, director Mauro Mueller, writer José David Figueroa García and producer Leslie Holleran discussed their bilingual film A Few Days in the Sun, featured in the Cinema of the World section. The interaction offered insights into the film's making and creative vision.

In Mexico’s Riviera Maya, a wealthy European couple uses illegal ways to force a local community off the land planned for development. Meanwhile, a working-class Mexican family makes a risky deal with a corrupt police officer to keep a teenager out of prison. When their paths cross, both couples become involved in a violent kidnapping that quickly spirals out of control. Trapped in a harsh landscape, they must face the consequences of their actions and discover how privilege and the struggle to survive can bring them closer than they expected.

The film is an international co-production across five countries (Mexico, the Dominican Republic, Germany, the USA and Switzerland), in two languages (English and Spanish). At its core is a simple idea: one person’s holiday is another person’s home and daily life. What happens when these two worlds collide?

Mueller spoke about how much of his own life shaped the story and its perspective. He grew up in Switzerland and has also lived in Mexico and the USA. He believes that travelling and living in different countries is necessary to cultivate empathy, and to learn that there is no one way of living, and that no way of living is better or worse than another. Knowing languages and travelling, he added, helps us understand why people make different choices, and recognise how the systems and institutions around them shape the consequences of those same choices.

Mueller is no stranger to IFFI. His earlier film The Janitor (El Conserje) had its world premiere at the 56th IFFI in Goa in November 2025. 

García emphasised the clash of cultures and social classes, a contrast that the film brings out clearly. He pointed out that when similar decisions are made, the wealthy European characters do not face the consequences that the working-class couple do, whose lives change drastically. Holleran echoed this, saying that for a poor person even the smallest mistake can bring everything crashing down. In the film, those holding the captives and the captives themselves are all, in a way, imprisoned by their circumstances.

García also explored how corruption runs through every level of society. At lower levels it is blunter, like bribery, while the wealthy couple’s attempt to illegally move a community off a piece of land is a higher-level corruption tied to power and politics, which is generally accepted. The film tries to place both kinds of corruption on the same level. Mueller and García also spoke about the widening inequality in the world, and how people are classified by their socio-economic class.

Mueller said the film aims to build empathy for why people make the morally grey choices they do. He chose the thriller genre to reach a newer and broader audience than a pure drama might. The result, he said, is a “character-driven thriller” standing at the border of arthouse and commercial cinema.

Holleran described the film as, in a way, women-focussed. The choices made by the women in both families, how they make them and how they connect to each other, drive much of the story. García added that stories of different classes clashing are relatable to everyone, as we all place ourselves in some class of society. By showing both sides facing similar dilemmas, the film invites viewers to understand, rather than ostracise, those from other classes, despite the difference in privilege.

Holleran said she finds inspiration when she sees something she recognises emotionally but is not a part of and wants to learn about it. The film’s exploration of outsiders entering a community comes from this. She also spoke about navigating the production process across so many producing countries. Discovering unfamiliar places `and collaborating with writers and directors, she said, is the best part of producing, along with meeting people from around the world. She spoke of falling in love with Mumbai, comparing its diversity and vibrance with her home city, New York.

Holleran observed that people worldwide are hungry for equality, recognition, and representation, and are trying to become comfortable with diversity as we find our way back to the arc of justice and fairness. She stressed the importance of travelling beyond the familiar, to hear a new language and to taste and smell a new culture. If people could travel more, she said, the world would be a better place.

Shri Labh Jain moderated the session.

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

 

* * *

PIB IFFI Team | Rabeehashmi/ LekshmiPriya/ Anushka/ Darshana | IFFI 57 - 108

item.content:encoded:
Lok Sabha Secretariat
INDIA’S CONSTITUTION IS THE BEDROCK OF ITS DEMOCRACY, NATIONAL UNITY AND FUTURE PROGRESS: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER CALLS UPON YOUTH TO EMBRACE CONSTITUTIONAL VALUES AND DISCHARGE THEIR DUTIES WITH PATRIOTISM, COMMITMENT AND DEDICATION
CONSTITUENT ASSEMBLY’S DELIBERATIONS REFLECT INDIA’S ENDURING TRADITION OF DIALOGUE, DEBATE AND CONSENSUS-BUILDING: LOK SABHA SPEAKER
LOK SABHA SPEAKER URGES YOUNG PARTICIPANTS TO CARRY IDEALS OF THE CONSTITUTION AND SPIRIT OF TRANSFORMATION TO EVERY CORNER OF THE COUNTRY
LOK SABHA SPEAKER ADDRESSES STUDENTS ON THE OCCASION OF SAMVIDHAN DIWAS
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:44PM by PIB Delhi

Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla said today that the Constitution of India is not merely the supreme law of the land but the very foundation of the nation's democratic ethos, national unity and collective aspirations. It has guided the world's largest democracy through successive phases of transformation while preserving its unity amidst extraordinary diversity. Emphasising the enduring vision and foresight of the makers of the Constitution, he said that the Constitution had laid the foundations of a robust parliamentary democracy and continues to illuminate India's journey towards peace, prosperity and progress.

Addressing young participants at the historic Central Hall on the occasion of Samvidhan Diwas, Shri Birla called upon the youth to move beyond merely reading the Constitution and make its ideals an integral part of their thoughts, conduct and everyday lives. He underscored that the vitality of a democracy rests not only upon the rights guaranteed to its citizens but equally upon their willingness to fulfil their duties and responsibilities towards society and the nation.

Recalling the historic legacy of Samvidhan Sadan, Shri Birla observed that the building had witnessed defining chapters of India's freedom struggle and subsequently the momentous deliberations that gave shape to the destiny of independent India. The historic premises, he said, stand as a lasting testament to the sacrifices, convictions and visionary aspirations that shaped the Republic. He added that the Constitution, with its universal ideals and democratic principles, continues to serve as a guiding light not only for India but also for democratic societies across the world.

Reflecting upon the extraordinary journey of the Constituent Assembly, the Speaker said that its members deliberated for two years and eleven months, bringing together diverse viewpoints, engaging in extensive discussions and resolving complex questions through dialogue, reasoned debate and mutual understanding. Despite differences of opinion, the members demonstrated an exemplary spirit of accommodation and consensus, placing the larger interests of the nation above all other considerations. This remarkable exercise, he said, remains a shining testament to India's democratic temperament and its enduring tradition of collective decision-making.

Shri Birla observed that the Constitution had provided an enduring framework for safeguarding India's unity and integrity while celebrating its immense diversity of languages, dialects, religions, traditions and cultures. By enshrining the foundational principles of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, it has ensured a common constitutional identity for all citizens and created a shared vision for the nation's future. India's parliamentary democracy, he said, draws its strength and legitimacy from these constitutional ideals and the faith of its people in democratic institutions.

Elaborating upon the distinct yet complementary responsibilities of the three organs of the State, Shri Birla said that the Legislature serves as the voice of the people's aspirations and translates their expectations into laws and policies; the Executive gives effect to these policies through their implementation; and the Judiciary upholds the Constitution, safeguards the rights of citizens and ensures justice. Functioning within their respective constitutional domains, these institutions collectively strengthen the foundations of democratic governance and reinforce public confidence in the constitutional order.

Lok Sabha Speaker further observed that the framers of the Constitution had displayed exceptional wisdom and foresight by envisioning a framework that transcended the immediate challenges of their times and remained capable of guiding future generations through changing political, social and economic circumstances. He emphasised that Parliament and other democratic institutions must continue to serve as vibrant forums for public aspirations, diverse perspectives and constructive deliberations, where ideas are transformed into meaningful outcomes for the people.

Shri Birla said that India's youth represented the country's greatest strength and an immense reservoir of talent, enterprise, innovation and creativity. At a time when young Indians are making remarkable strides in science, technology and emerging fields of knowledge, their vision, energy and determination would play a pivotal role in shaping the nation's destiny and realising the resolve of a Viksit Bharat. He urged them to remain fully conscious of the rights and opportunities bestowed upon them by the Constitution while recognising that their responsibilities towards society and the nation were equally significant. He expressed confidence that a generation equipped with constitutional awareness, legal understanding and a strong commitment to public service would make an invaluable contribution to strengthening democratic institutions and deepening the roots of constitutional governance.

Appreciating the enthusiasm and commitment of the young participants, Shri Birla urged them to take the insights and experiences gained at Constitution House beyond its historic walls and carry the message of constitutional values to their respective States, educational institutions, workplaces and communities. He encouraged them to become ambassadors of the Constitution, inspiring fellow students and young citizens to understand its ideals, participate meaningfully in democratic processes and contribute to positive and transformative change. He particularly emphasised the importance of ensuring that the benefits of development, justice and opportunity reach every citizen, especially those at the last mile.

Concluding his address, the Speaker called upon the participants to make patriotism, dedication, hard work and a steadfast commitment to constitutional values the guiding principles of their lives. He urged them to leave Samvidhan Sadan with renewed enthusiasm, enriched perspectives and a firm resolve to read, understand and imbibe the Constitution in letter and spirit. The collective commitment of every citizen to constitutional ideals, he emphasised, would remain the cornerstone of a strong, inclusive, progressive and developed India.

संविधान दिवस के अवसर पर संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में आयोजित कार्यक्रम में देशभर से आए विद्यार्थियों एवं युवा प्रतिभागियों के साथ भारतीय संविधान की गौरवशाली यात्रा, उसके मूल आदर्शों और लोकतांत्रिक परंपराओं पर संवाद किया। संविधान किसी राष्ट्र का केवल विधिक दस्तावेज नहीं, बल्कि उसकी लोकतांत्रिक चेतना, सामूहिक संकल्प और उज्ज्वल भविष्य का आधार होता है। भारत की भाषायी, धार्मिक और सांस्कृतिक विविधताओं के बीच हमारे संविधान ने राष्ट्र को एक साझा दृष्टि और दिशा प्रदान की है। संविधान सभा के सदस्यों ने दो वर्ष, ग्यारह महीने के गहन विचार-विमर्श, तर्क-वितर्क और सहमति-असहमति के बाद इस दूरदर्शी संविधान का निर्माण किया। संसद और विधानमंडल जनाकांक्षाओं को अभिव्यक्ति देते हैं, कार्यपालिका नीतियों एवं कानूनों का क्रियान्वयन करती है और न्यायपालिका नागरिकों के संवैधानिक अधिकारों की रक्षा करती है। यही संस्थागत संतुलन हमारे लोकतंत्र की आधारशिला है। नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम, 2023 जैसे प्रयास लोकतांत्रिक संस्थाओं में महिलाओं की भागीदारी को और सशक्त बनाने की दिशा में महत्वपूर्ण हैं। लोकतंत्र की वास्तविक शक्ति जागरूक, विवेकशील और कर्तव्यनिष्ठ नागरिकों में निहित है। युवाओं की नवाचार क्षमता, तकनीकी कौशल और राष्ट्र के प्रति समर्पण विकसित भारत की महत्वपूर्ण शक्ति हैं। प्रत्येक युवा अपने कार्यक्षेत्र में निष्ठा एवं परिश्रम से दायित्व निभाते हुए राष्ट्र निर्माण में योगदान दे सकता है। संविधान के आदर्शों की सार्थकता भी तभी है, जब वे हमारे विचारों और आचरण में प्रतिबिंबित हों। विकसित भारत 2047 का स्वप्न आर्थिक एवं तकनीकी प्रगति के साथ गुणवत्तापूर्ण शिक्षा, बेहतर स्वास्थ्य, समयबद्ध न्याय और समान अवसरों की सुनिश्चितता में निहित है। संविधान की वास्तविक सार्थकता उसके मूल्यों को आत्मसात कर प्रत्येक नागरिक के जीवन में समानता, स्वतंत्रता, न्याय और बंधुत्व की अनुभूति सुनिश्चित करने में है। संविधान दिवस पर हमारा संकल्प हो कि हम अपने अधिकारों के साथ कर्तव्यों और दायित्वों का भी पूरी निष्ठा से निर्वहन करते हुए लोकतांत्रिक भारत को और अधिक सशक्त बनाने में सहभागी बनें।

— Om Birla (@ombirlakota) November 26, 2026

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
MoSJE Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Crosses ₹1.81 Crore Sales Milestone As On November 25; Strong Consumer Patronage Boosts Livelihood Opportunities for Artisans
Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase India’s Rich Cultural Heritage and Entrepreneurial Talent
Aligned with the Guiding Principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’ of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
Trade Fair to Conclude Tomorrow November 27
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:35PM by PIB Delhi

With the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 entering its concluding phase, the pavilion of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment at Bharat Mandapam, in the National Capital here, continues to witness an encouraging response from visitors, with cumulative sales crossing ₹1.81 crore as of November 25, 2026, reflecting growing consumer appreciation for indigenous products, traditional craftsmanship and the entrepreneurial talent of artisans from diverse communities across the country.

The cumulative sales have registered an increase of nearly 40 per cent over the ₹1.81 crore recorded up to November 25, 2026. The sustained growth in sales reflects strong consumer patronage and the significance of providing direct market access to traditional artisans and entrepreneurs.

Located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, the Ministry’s pavilion has emerged as a vibrant platform showcasing India’s diverse cultural heritage, traditional skills and indigenous craftsmanship. Visitors are exploring and purchasing a wide range of authentic handcrafted products, thereby directly contributing to the economic empowerment of participating artisans.

With the Trade Fair scheduled to conclude tomorrow November 27, 2026, the remaining days offer visitors an opportunity to experience India’s rich artistic traditions, purchase authentic indigenous products and support the livelihoods of artisans and entrepreneurs from diverse communities.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said that more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC).

He said the participation of these Apex Corporations reflects the Ministry’s continued commitment to strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs).

The Official said these efforts are aligned with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi under his guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’, aimed at fostering inclusive growth, economic empowerment and equitable development.

The pavilion features an extensive collection of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products. These products represent the distinctive artistic identities, traditional skills and cultural diversity of different regions across the country, the Official said.

He said the growing consumer response underscores the importance of national-level exhibitions in enabling artisans to enhance the visibility of their products, interact directly with customers, understand evolving consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore new market opportunities.

The Official remarked that participation in a prestigious platform such as IITF also enables artisans to strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities, expand their customer base and build sustainable business prospects, contributing towards greater economic self-reliance.

A significant highlight of the Ministry’s participation is the promotion of TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme), which aims to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among consumers, he said.

Through the TULIP initiative, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation, strengthen entrepreneurial capabilities and create sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, he said.

The 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, has brought together producers, entrepreneurs, traders and consumers from across the country and abroad, providing a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange.

As the Trade Fair approaches its conclusion, the Ministry’s pavilion continues to offer visitors an opportunity to celebrate India’s rich cultural heritage while contributing directly to the economic empowerment and sustainable livelihoods of traditional artisans.

The Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 reinforces its commitment to promoting inclusive economic development, preserving traditional craftsmanship, strengthening grassroots entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities towards the realisation of the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
