Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
Union Health Secretary Calls for Strengthening State-Level Regulatory Capacity to Ensure Safer Food and Quality Medicines
Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava delivers keynote address at National-Level Conference on Food Safety and Drug Administration in Bengaluru; emphasises risk-based inspections, robust surveillance, digital solutions and stronger Centre-State coordination
Conference deliberates on strengthening food safety enforcement, drug quality oversight, laboratory infrastructure, digital traceability and consumer awareness
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:22PM by PIB Delhi

A National-Level Conference on Food Safety and Drug Administration was held today in Bengaluru, Karnataka, under the theme “Safer Food, Safer Medicine, Healthier Nation”, with a focus on strengthening food and drug regulatory systems through coordinated action, effective enforcement and enhanced institutional capacity.

The Conference brought together senior representatives of the Government of India, State and Union Territory Governments, regulatory authorities, public health institutions and enforcement agencies to deliberate on key challenges and identify measures to further strengthen food and drug safety across the country.

Addressing the Conference, Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava described food and drug regulatory authorities as the vanguards of public health, entrusted with the responsibility of safeguarding the health and well-being of every citizen. She emphasised that regulators must discharge their responsibilities effectively, efficiently and with integrity, while maintaining a balance between public health protection and ease of doing business.

Highlighting that regulatory decisions have a direct bearing on public health as well as on food business operators, manufacturers and retailers, she stressed the need to focus on essential regulatory requirements and strengthen coordination between Central and State authorities.

On food safety, the Union Health Secretary emphasised that regulatory efforts must go beyond preventing food adulteration and the sale of unsafe food to also promote healthy eating and better nutrition. She underlined the importance of capacity-building and the wider adoption of safe food-handling practices.

Referring to the perpetual validity of food safety licences, she noted that this places greater responsibility on regulatory authorities to ensure effective monitoring and robust, risk-based inspections. She also invited States to share their feedback on the risk-based inspection mechanism of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI).

On drug regulation, Smt. Srivastava emphasised the need to strengthen State-level regulatory capacity through improved inspection mechanisms and greater adoption of technology. She highlighted the proposal for a sub-national assessment framework, aligned with World Health Organization (WHO) maturity-level parameters, to assess the capacity and performance of State drug regulatory systems.

She encouraged States to review SHRESHT (State Health Regulatory Excellence Index), the virtual assessment tool, and share their feedback to help strengthen the framework. Underscoring the importance of State participation in the conceptualisation of the Digital Drug Regulatory System (DDRS), she called upon States to contribute their practical experience and suggestions to inform its development.

She also stressed the need to strengthen transparency and accountability in clinical trials, including in the functioning of Contract Research Organisations (CROs).

Conference deliberates on strengthening regulatory frameworks, surveillance and enforcement

The Conference provided a platform for detailed deliberations on strengthening food and drug regulatory frameworks, improving surveillance and enforcement, augmenting institutional and laboratory capacities, and promoting coordinated action between Central and State authorities. The discussions reaffirmed that access to safe food and safe, effective and quality-assured medicines is fundamental to protecting public health, preventing avoidable illness and maintaining consumer confidence.

The food safety sessions reviewed the implementation of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, with particular emphasis on risk-based inspections, surveillance, enforcement, food testing and evidence-based regulatory action. The discussions also covered good practices adopted by States in implementing food safety regulations, along with emerging challenges relating to e-commerce, novel foods and consumer trust.

The drug safety sessions focused on measures to combat spurious and adulterated medicines and address issues relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances through strengthened inter-State coordination in investigation and enforcement. Other key areas included greater uniformity in licensing and regulatory practices, risk-based inspections and surveillance, and adherence to good manufacturing and distribution practices under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the Rules thereunder.

The deliberations also addressed emerging challenges in the pharmaceutical sector, strategies to sustain India's position as the “Pharmacy of the World”, and the role of next-generation cellular and molecular platforms in accelerating discovery and therapeutic applications.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-IIIM, Jammu conferred as “Pioneering Institute of the Year in Skills & Higher Education” at the DIDAC India Awards 2026
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi

CSIR-Indian Institute of Integrative Medicine (CSIR-IIIM), Jammu, has achieved a prestigious international distinction by winning the DIDAC India Awards 2026 in the category of Pioneering Institution of the Year - Higher Education & Skills. The Institute has also been recognized as a Torchbearer in Higher Education & Skills, acknowledging its growing contribution to skill development, industry-oriented education and experiential learning. CSIR-IIIM emerged as the winner among several shortlisted finalists following multiple rounds of evaluation by the DIDAC Skills selection and expert jury.

The DIDAC India 2026 programme, being held from 25-27 November in Bengaluru, has brought together ministers and dignitaries from 19 countries, representatives of over 500 industry partners and approximately 1,000 educational and other institutions participating in the programme and associated competitions.

The achievement reflects CSIR-IIIM's sustained commitment to translating scientific expertise into practical skills, employment opportunities and regional development. Under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, the Institute has progressively moved towards intensive, job-oriented training programmes designed around actual industrial requirements, with emphasis on hands-on learning, sophisticated equipment handling, industry exposure and employability. By bringing industries and other stakeholders on board, CSIR-IIIM has strengthened the connection between scientific education and workplace requirements, creating opportunities for young people to acquire market-relevant skills.

A significant contribution to this transformation has come from Dr. Nasir-ul-Rasheed, Principal Scientist and Nodal Scientist for Skill Development at CSIR-IIIM, whose efforts have helped expand industry-linked, employment-oriented training, institutional collaborations and hands-on learning opportunities. His work in connecting scientific expertise with skill development, industry requirements and student mentorship has contributed to strengthening the Institute's skilling ecosystem.

At the CSIR level, Dr. Vinay Kumar, Nodal Scientist for the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative, has played an important role in coordinating and promoting the integrated skill development programme across CSIR laboratories. Congratulating the CSIR-IIIM Skill Development Team on this prestigious achievement, he appreciated the Institute's efforts in advancing industry-oriented training, strengthening institutional partnerships and translating the objectives of the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative into impactful programmes.

Dr. Zabeer Ahmed, Director, CSIR-IIIM, has played a pivotal leadership role in shaping and encouraging this institutional transformation. With his vision of taking scientific research beyond laboratory boundaries and connecting it with societal needs, he has consistently promoted industry partnerships, practical training, innovation, entrepreneurship and capacity building. His emphasis on strengthening the Institute's engagement with industry and creating meaningful opportunities for youth has provided the institutional direction and encouragement behind these achievements. The DIDAC recognition is a reflection of his leadership and the collective commitment of the CSIR-IIIM team towards making science and skills meaningful instruments of social and economic development.

Congratulating the Institute on this prestigious achievement, Dr. N. Kalaiselvi, Director General, CSIR and Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), appreciated Dr. Zabeer Ahmed and the entire CSIR-IIIM team, Jammu, for their dedication, institutional leadership and contribution to advancing skill development and higher education.

The recognition marks an important milestone for CSIR-IIIM and reinforces its commitment to building a skilled workforce, nurturing young innovators, strengthening industry partnerships and contributing to the development of Jammu and Kashmir and the nation.

The programme aimed to equip library and information science professionals, academicians, researchers, students and IT…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
CSIR-NIScPR Organises Capacity-Building Programme on Artificial Intelligence for Libraries
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi

The CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR), New Delhi, organised a three-day Skill Training Programme on “Artificial Intelligence for Libraries” from 17–19 November 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). The programme aimed to equip library and information science professionals, academicians, researchers, students and IT professionals with knowledge and practical skills in leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for library services, research support, information discovery and knowledge management.

During the inaugural session, Shri Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, introduced the objectives of the programme and highlighted the importance of capacity building in emerging technologies to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of library and information services. Shri Salim Ansari moderated the session.

The programme covered a range of topics, including the fundamentals of AI and its applications in libraries, chatbots and user interfaces, no-code web and app development, AI-based metadata extraction and smart cataloguing, research discovery and mapping, regional language translation, fact-checking, information integrity and the ethical use of AI.

A special session on “AI Tools for Research Support: Literature Search and Review, Summarising Papers and Checking AI Output Against Real Sources” was conducted on 18 November 2026 by guest faculty Dr. Ritesh Yaduwanshi, Assistant Professor, Indira Gandhi Delhi Technical University for Women (IGDTUW). The session introduced participants to AI tools for literature discovery, reviewing and summarising research papers, and verifying AI-generated information against authentic sources. It emphasised critical evaluation and responsible use of AI in academic and research activities.

The training highlighted the potential of AI in automating routine library tasks, improving information retrieval, facilitating intelligent knowledge discovery and enhancing user-oriented services. Sessions on smart cataloguing, metadata extraction, research mapping, chatbots and regional language translation demonstrated how emerging technologies can improve the organisation, accessibility and discoverability of information resources. Discussions on fact-checking and AI ethics underscored the importance of accuracy, transparency and human oversight.

The valedictory session was held on 19 November 2026, marking the successful completion of the programme. Participants were encouraged to apply the knowledge and skills acquired during the training to their professional practices and explore responsible integration of AI into library services.

The programme was coordinated by Shri Mukesh Pund, Scientist G and Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR. Ms. Meetali Bharti served as Nodal Principal Investigator, and Shri Salim Ansari as Co-Nodal PI.

Through such initiatives, CSIR-NIScPR continues to promote professional capacity building and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, contributing towards an inclusive, efficient and technology-enabled knowledge ecosystem.

item.title: “Stay Honest, Patient and True to Your Craft”: Mukesh Chhabra Shares the Secrets of Casting and Acting at IFFI 2026 Masterclass
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting “Stay Honest, Patient and True to Your Craft”: Mukesh Chhabra Shares the Secrets of Casting and Acting at IFFI 2026 Masterclass “My Focus is to Bring an Oscar for this Country”: Mukesh Chhabra No Age Barriers in Acting: Mukesh Chhabra Says Industry Needs Talent in their 40s, 50s and 60s Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:45PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 26 November 2026 Renowned casting director Mukesh Chhabra shared invaluable insights and practical tips for aspiring actors during a packed masterclass titled The Casting Magic:…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Stay Honest, Patient and True to Your Craft”: Mukesh Chhabra Shares the Secrets of Casting and Acting at IFFI 2026 Masterclass
“My Focus is to Bring an Oscar for this Country”: Mukesh Chhabra
No Age Barriers in Acting: Mukesh Chhabra Says Industry Needs Talent in their 40s, 50s and 60s
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:45PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 26 November 2026

 

Renowned casting director Mukesh Chhabra shared invaluable insights and practical tips for aspiring actors during a packed masterclass titled The Casting Magic: Auditions Unplugged, held today at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The session witnessed an enthusiastic and diverse audience comprising aspiring actors, mid-career professionals looking to pursue acting, writers, emerging filmmakers and media representatives. Participants from across the country, along with a strong local Goan presence, actively engaged with Chhabra, raising a wide range of questions on what makes a good actor, how to ace an audition and the nuances of navigating the world of casting.

Speaking about Chhabra, Festival Director Ashutosh Gowariker said, “What I like about Mukesh is his eye for character and he will go to any length to find the actors who fit in.”

With over 300 films and web series to his credit, Chhabra offered a glimpse into the extensive and often painstaking process of casting, emphasising that discovering the right actor goes far beyond looking at databases or familiar faces. “There is so much talent in our country. Earlier, when there were no casting directors, it used to be difficult. I send my team everywhere to scout for talent. You have to go to the roots. Our country has so many cultural arts and sub-cultures where so much raw talent is displayed,” he said.

Explaining his approach to casting, Mukesh Chhabra said that he is often the first person a director approaches after a script is ready. He begins by reading the script thoroughly and discussing the characters and the director's vision. The next step involves deciding whether a role calls for an established actor or a fresh face, followed by travelling to the region where the story is set to discover talent among local communities. His job, he explained, is to understand the character, identify the right personality and recommend an actor who fits the director's vision. “Directors hire me for my opinion, my ideas, not for my data,” he observed, describing himself as a bridge between the actor and the director.

The scale of this process can be immense. Recalling the casting of Dangal, Chhabra revealed that it took nearly two years, with around 14,000 girls auditioning for the roles. The casting process for Ramayana, he said, extended over six years. He also recalled casting 384 people for Gangs of Wasseypur, a film that proved to be a major turning point in his career. “Gangs of Wasseypur changed my life", he informed.

Sharing his experience of working with noted filmmakers, Chhabra noted that every director has a distinct vision and approach. His responsibility is to ensure that the actors fit the characters as imagined by the filmmaker. Sometimes, he said, the casting process can even influence the writing. Citing Kai Po Che!, he recalled how the character of Gattu was written with Rajkummar Rao in mind. He also highlighted how talented actors such as Nawazuddin Siddiqui and Manoj Bajpayee bring their own strengths to a character, sometimes inspiring directors to rethink and reshape roles.

Reflecting on his journey of over two decades, Chhabra spoke about how actor Aamir Khan was among the first people to notice his work. He said that his journey has been driven by an enduring passion for discovering new talent. With around 100 more films lined up over the next two to three years, he remains deeply invested in the process.

The casting director's larger vision

Chhabra acknowledged that casting is an evolving creative exercise, with requirements changing from one film and script to another. Sometimes actors have to be replaced even at the last moment if someone else is found to be a better fit for the character. Such decisions, he explained, are part of the creative process and are guided by the needs of the film.

For Chhabra, casting is not merely a profession but a way of life. “Casting is not just a job for me. I do it for a living, this is life. My focus is to bring an Oscar for this country. I do my work honestly,” he said.

“Rejection is part of the journey”

Addressing one of the most pressing concerns among aspiring actors, Chhabra spoke candidly about rejection and the importance of resilience. “It's a part of your life, you've got to deal with this. We only have to find the right talent for a character. If you feel rejected and sad all the time, you will miss a lot of opportunities,” he said.

Drawing from his own experience, he revealed that his journey in the industry was far from easy. He began as an assistant director, initially working primarily on casting, and spent years establishing himself. Many directors had rejected him in his early days, he recalled, adding that some of those very filmmakers work with him today. “Every single person has to struggle in life. I don't want to talk about my sad story, but I really had a hard time,” he shared.

“Acting has nothing to do with age, talent is the only thing”

His advice to aspiring actors was to remain patient, positive and committed to their craft rather than becoming disheartened by the pace of their careers. “If you think you can act, do the job. Just go with it,” he said, adding that talent has no age barrier. “Acting has nothing to do with age, talent is the only thing.” He encouraged people in their 40s, 50s and 60s to pursue acting, pointing out that the industry needs performers across generations.

What makes an actor stand out?

For Chhabra, talent alone is not the only consideration when identifying the right actor for a role. Personality, honesty, simplicity and the ability to take directions are equally important. “The actor should also be directable. It's important to follow directions. Honesty and following instructions are important,” he said. “If you understand life and human emotions, you understand acting,” he added.

How to crack audition for a role?

Chhabra advises all aspiring actors going for audition to make sure that they understand the character and its background. “Designing the scene in your head is important. We want to understand the actor's intellect. Please do your homework”, he said.

On self-tapes, Chhabra recommended keeping the background clean and uncluttered, avoiding unnecessary make-up and ensuring that the performance remains the focus. The person reading the lines alongside the actor should provide appropriate cues, while the framing should include a close shot that captures the eyes and expressions clearly.

He also cautioned young actors against seeking constant validation on social media. Instead, they should focus on improving their craft, building confidence and gaining experience. Theatre, he said, is an excellent platform for developing confidence and honing acting skills. He particularly encouraged aspiring performers to join theatre groups and participate in stage productions, regardless of their age or previous experience.

He urged aspiring actors to maintain their purity and honesty, stay committed to learning and never allow impatience or the pursuit of instant recognition to derail their journey. “It is all a game of patience and positivity. If it is meant for you, it will come to you,” he said. “Be natural and simple”- is another mantra he gave to budding actors.

His masterclass offered a compelling reminder that behind every memorable on-screen character lies a painstaking process of discovery, preparation and collaboration. And for every aspiring actor, the journey begins with understanding people, respecting the craft and having the patience to wait for the right role.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Earth Sciences
item.description: Ministry of Earth Sciences New approach to detecting solar particle events could expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi Indian research stations in the Arctic (Ny-Ålesund) and Antarctic (Maitri) regions through the gamma-ray detectors gamma-ray detectors installed in them have established a new approach to detecting rare and extreme solar events called Ground-Level Enhancement (GLE). This study of GLEs which could expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations and help…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Earth Sciences
New approach to detecting solar particle events could expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:36PM by PIB Delhi

Indian research stations in the Arctic (Ny-Ålesund) and Antarctic (Maitri) regions through the gamma-ray detectors gamma-ray detectors installed in them have established a new approach to detecting rare and extreme solar events called Ground-Level Enhancement (GLE).

This study of GLEs which could expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations and help improve understanding of the Sun–Earth connection and help in assessing the potential impacts of extreme space-weather conditions.

GLEs, generally associated with powerful solar eruptions, in which highly energetic particles, primarily protons, travel through interplanetary space and penetrate the Earth's atmosphere produce secondary particles of hadronic, mesonic and electromagnetic types.

They are among the most extreme manifestations of solar energetic particle (SEP) events and often produce intense solar flares and fast coronal mass ejections (CMEs).

Scientists at the Indian Institute of Geomagnetism (IIG), Mumbai, an Autonomous Institute of Department of Science and Technology (DST), have for the first time detected GLE signatures from records of the solar event of November 11, 2025, designated GLE #77, (associated with an intense X-class solar flare, a fast coronal mass ejection and a strong SEP events) using gamma-ray detectors installed at Indian research stations in both the Arctic (Ny-Ålesund) and Antarctic (Maitri).

Fig 1: NaI (Tl) scintillation detector

Fig 2: Gamma-ray and Neutron variations from  Antarctica (top) and Arctic (bottom) on 11 November 2025.

The NaI(Tl) scintillation gamma-ray detectors at Maitri in Antarctica and Ny-Ålesund in the Arctic were installed by IIG, as part of its research programme to investigate cosmic-ray and space-weather-related phenomena through ground-based observations at polar latitudes.

This new approach of detecting GLEs establishes the potential of ground-based gamma-ray observations, a comparatively cost-effective approach to complement conventional neutron-monitor measurements.

Gamma-ray detectors are relatively compact and cost-effective compared to conventional neutron-monitor installations. A wider network of such detectors could complement existing monitoring systems, expand the geographic coverage of ground-based observations, and improve our understanding of high-energy solar particles and their interactions with Earth's atmosphere.

The study involved a systematic analysis of gamma-ray observations recorded by NaI(Tl) scintillation detectors installed at Maitri and Ny-Ålesund. Systematic analysis was carried out to distinguish the GLE related enhancement from a variety of probable sources including background terrestrial radioactivity, terrestrial gamma-ray flashes (TGF), and thunderstorm ground enhancements (TGEs) associated with lightning activity, extra-terrestrial sources such as gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), solar flares, and so on.

Prof. G. Vichare, Ms. P. Thakur, Mr. C. Selvaraj from IIG and Prof. N. Gopalswamy from NASA processed the recorded data to obtain gamma-ray count rates in different energy ranges, and the variations were examined relative to the pre-event background level, along with the GLE signature in the traditional neutron monitor network and GOES particle data in different energy ranges.

Fig 3: Solar flare recorded by GOES

The gamma-ray detectors at the two polar stations recorded distinct temporal signatures of the event.

A prompt response was observed at the Antarctic station Maitri, while a more gradual response was observed at the Arctic station Ny-Ålesund. The gamma-ray observations were found to be consistent with measurements from neutron monitors, the instruments traditionally used for detecting GLEs.

The observations published in the journal Astrophysical Journal Letters, provided an important opportunity to study how high-energy solar particles enter and interact with the Earth's atmosphere at different geographic locations and under different geomagnetic conditions.

A wider network of such detectors at strategically selected locations could enhance the spatial coverage of ground-based observations and contribute to improved understanding of high-energy solar particle events.

The installation and operation of gamma-ray detectors at Maitri, Antarctica, and Ny-Ålesund, Arctic, represent an important contribution by India to the international effort to understand extreme space-weather events.

The successful detection of GLE #77 at both polar stations demonstrates the scientific value of India's polar observational capabilities and opens new possibilities for developing a complementary global network of gamma-ray detectors for space-weather monitoring.

Publication link: https://doi.org/10.3847/2041-8213/aeaee7

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Attends Closing Programme of Observance of 350th Shaheedi Diwas of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
The programme commemorates Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's supreme martyrdom for freedom of conscience and humanity
Shabad Kirtan, exhibition and short film presented as part of the closing ceremony at CCRT Campus, Dwarka, New Delhi
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Culture organised the closing programme of the year-long observance of the 350th Shaheedi Diwas of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji at the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) Campus, Dwarka, New Delhi. The programme commemorated the supreme martyrdom of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji for the freedom of conscience, religious freedom and the welfare of humanity.

The year-long commemoration of the 350th Shaheedi Diwas of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji was observed from 24 November 2025 to 24 November 2026. Inaugurated by the Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi at Kurukshetra, Haryana, the commemoration marked the beginning of a series of programmes across the country to highlight Guru Sahib's life, teachings and supreme martyrdom. As part of the commemoration, a commemorative coin and postage stamp were also released in honour of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji.

The closing ceremony was graced by Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, who attended as the Chief Guest. Shri Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Former Chairman, National Commission for Minorities, and Shri Amar Preet Singh, Former Chief of the Air Staff, Indian Air Force, were the Guests of Honour. Senior officials of the Ministry and other distinguished dignitaries were also present on the occasion.

The programme featured Shabad Kirtan, an exhibition and a short film highlighting the life, teachings and supreme martyrdom of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. These presentations provided an opportunity to reflect on his message of compassion, courage, human dignity and respect for freedom of conscience.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat said that the occasion marked not merely the conclusion of a programme, but the culmination of a year-long campaign of remembrance, reverence, reflection and public awareness dedicated to Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. He emphasised that the purpose of the observance was to draw inspiration from Guru Sahib's life and teachings and enable the present generation to understand, adopt and carry forward his ideals.

He further emphasised that human achievement cannot be measured only through material accomplishments. The true purpose of human life and progress is to build a society where the freedom and dignity of every individual are protected and upheld. He said that the teachings of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji continue to guide society towards these values and remain relevant for generations to come.

Shri Amar Preet Singh, Former Chief of the Air Staff, Indian Air Force, highlighted that Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji dedicated his entire life to protect the rights and freedom of belief of others. He observed that while individuals generally strive to safeguard their own faith and beliefs, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji devoted his life to protecting the beliefs and freedom of others. He noted that this makes Guru Ji's martyrdom truly extraordinary and an enduring example of selflessness and courage.

Shri Iqbal Singh Lalpura, Former Chairman, National Commission for Minorities, appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Culture in organising the year-long observance and taking the teachings of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji to people across the country.

Shri Samar Nanda, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Culture, spoke about the various programmes organised by the Ministry across different states to take the life, teachings and philosophy of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji to people across the country. He highlighted how these programmes brought scholars, artists, religious organisations and local communities together on a common platform to share and reflect on Guru Sahib's ideals.

He further informed that the Centre for Cultural Resources and Training (CCRT) organised educational and cultural programmes in schools to engage students with the life and teachings of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji. As part of this initiative, workshops were conducted in 220 schools, with the participation of around 68,000 students. These efforts were aimed at introducing the younger generation to Guru Sahib's message of compassion, selflessness, fearlessness, service and the welfare of all.

Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Culture reaffirmed its commitment to preserving and promoting India's rich spiritual and cultural heritage and taking the timeless teachings of great spiritual leaders to future generations.

***

M Annadurai

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Law and Justice
Updated edition of the Constitution of India released in all 22 Scheduled Languages on Constitution Day 2026
Vice President of India Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan graces the occasion at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi
Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal also addresses the gathering
Posted On: 26 NOV 2026 4:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Legislative Department of the Ministry of Law and Justice, celebrated Constitution Day 2026 with a special programme at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, marking the release of the updated edition of the Constitution of India in all 22 Scheduled Languages. The programme was graced by the Vice President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, as the Chief Guest, in the presence of Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Law and Justice, and Dr. Rajiv Mani, Secretary, Legislative Department and Department of Legal Affairs.

The programme commenced with the National Song and National Anthem, followed by the ceremonial lighting of the lamp by the Vice President and the Minister. A short film highlighting the initiative was screened. The film described the Constitution not merely as a publication but as an enduring symbol of the struggle, dedication, cultural heritage, linguistic pride and democratic consciousness of the people of India, and as the charter that guarantees every citizen equality, liberty, justice and fraternity. It recalled the inclusive, equal and just India envisioned by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar and the members of the Constituent Assembly, and the vital role of Indian languages in realising that vision. It also emphasised that the initiative would bring the Constitution closer to citizens in rural areas, tribal communities and the younger generation, and concluded with the resolve that the Constitution should not remain confined to Parliament and the courts but should reach every village, every home, every school and every citizen.

The Vice President then released the updated edition of the Constitution of India in all 22 Scheduled Languages. This marks an important step towards promoting constitutional awareness and making the country’s supreme law accessible to citizens across linguistic backgrounds.

In his special address, the Vice President underscored the enduring significance of the Constitution and its role in upholding the values of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. He also emphasised the importance of making constitutional knowledge accessible to every citizen.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister Shri Arjun Ram Meghwal recalled the contribution of Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, Member of the Constituent Assembly and Chairman of the Drafting Committee, in giving the nation a forward-looking Constitution that rests on the pillars of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. He described the Constitution as the foundation of India’s democratic framework and stressed the need to strengthen citizens’ awareness of their constitutional rights and duties.

Dr. Rajiv Mani delivered the welcome address and highlighted the significance of Constitution Day and the Department’s efforts to make the Constitution and other laws accessible to citizens in their own languages. He thanked all those who contributed to making this momentous occasion possible, noting that this is the first time since the Constitution came into force that an updated edition of the Constitution is available in all 22 Scheduled Languages.

The release of the updated edition of the Constitution of India in all 22 Scheduled Languages reflects the Government’s commitment to promoting inclusive access to constitutional knowledge, strengthening constitutional literacy and bringing the ideals of the Constitution closer to every citizen.

***

Samrat/AD/GGV

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Commerce & Industry
Statement on USTR Section 301 Determination
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 10:48PM by PIB Delhi

Government of India has taken note of the Notice of Determination and Request for Comments issued by the United States Trade Representative (USTR) in the Section 301 Investigation concerning Acts, Policies, and Practices of 14 economies, including India, relating to Structural Excess Capacity and Production in Manufacturing Sectors. The Notice is currently under examination.

India engaged constructively throughout this investigation. In response to the Notice of Initiation and in subsequent proceedings, the Department of Commerce stated that India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector.

India and the United States are engaged in negotiations for a Bilateral Trade Agreement. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations. Government of India remains committed to working closely with the United States towards the early conclusion of the India-U.S. Bilateral Trade Agreement, as announced on 2nd February 2026 and in accordance with the Joint Statement issued on 7th February 2026.

***

item.content:encoded:
Prime Minister's Office
PM chairs 55th PRAGATI meeting
PM reviews five infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors worth over ₹78,000 crore
PM stresses on timely execution accompanied by high standards of construction quality
PM also reviews the ITI ecosystem including the implementation of PM-SETU
PM calls for stronger PSU–ITI linkages and skilling aligned with industrial clusters and sectoral needs
PM advocates the 3C approach of Classroom–Company–Career to connect training with employment
PM notes that stronger links between ITIs and local employers could expand employment opportunities closer to home
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi chaired the 55th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth earlier today. The platform brings together the Central and State Governments to address implementation bottlenecks and improve the delivery of projects and welfare schemes.

During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed five critical infrastructure projects in the road, power, coal and railway sectors, with a total cost of over ₹78,000 crore. He also reviewed the Industrial Training Institute (ITI) ecosystem, including the implementation of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU).

Prime Minister emphasised that delays in infrastructure projects have consequences beyond cost escalation, as they postpone the benefits intended for citizens, businesses and the economy. He called upon the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve pending issues with clear responsibility and realistic timelines. He stressed that timely execution must be accompanied by high standards of construction quality.

Reviewing the road project, the Prime Minister called for expeditious implementation and reiterated the need to focus on outcomes over outlays. While reviewing the coal project, the Prime Minister emphasised that rehabilitation and resettlement should be undertaken in a timely and dignified manner alongside timely project implementation.

While reviewing the power project, the Prime Minister suggested exploring innovative models for decentralised solar and wind power projects. He emphasised that such projects should be developed closer to centres of consumption wherever feasible, taking into account local resource availability and demand. These efforts should aim to improve the availability of reliable and affordable power and ease pressure on transmission infrastructure.

Reviewing the ITI ecosystem and the implementation of PM-SETU, Prime Minister called upon Chief Ministers and Chief Secretaries to provide leadership in strengthening ITIs and deepening industry participation under PM-SETU. He emphasised that this was an opportune time for industry to partner with ITIs, contribute to their upgradation and help align training with current and future manpower requirements. He called for close collaboration between States, ITIs and industry to translate these partnerships into better training and employment opportunities for young people.

Prime Minister called upon Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to assess their future manpower requirements and strengthen linkages with ITIs for training and recruitment in relevant trades. He encouraged PSUs to support practical training and apprenticeships and give greater attention to the intake of trained ITI graduates. Such engagement would provide students with industry experience and help PSUs access a ready pool of skilled manpower suited to their operational needs.

Prime Minister emphasised that skilling should be organised around industrial clusters and the requirements of individual sectors. He called for ITI trades, curricula and training capacity to be aligned with existing industries and upcoming investments in each region.

Prime Minister highlighted the potential of locally relevant skilling to improve employment opportunities closer to home. He noted that Stronger links between ITIs and local employers could expand employment opportunities closer to home and help reduce distress-driven migration, while enabling young people to contribute to the economic development of their own regions.

Prime Minister advocated a ‘Classroom–Company–Career’ (3C) approach to ITI education, linking classroom learning with practical experience in industry, followed by employment and career progression. He stressed that ITIs and industry should work together to provide students with relevant technical knowledge, exposure to actual working conditions and a clear pathway from training to employment.

****

item.title: Celebrating the Joy of Cinema: IFFI Parade Brings Goa’s Cultural Extravaganza to the Streets
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Celebrating the Joy of Cinema: IFFI Parade Brings Goa’s Cultural Extravaganza to the Streets CM Dr. Pramod Sawant Reiterates Goa’s Commitment to ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’ Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:06PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 25 November 2026 Taking the celebrations of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) beyond the cinema halls and festival venues, the spectacular IFFI Parade, themed ‘Celebrating the Joy of Cinema’ , transformed the streets of Panaji into a vibrant showcase of Goa’s artistic and cultural…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Celebrating the Joy of Cinema: IFFI Parade Brings Goa’s Cultural Extravaganza to the Streets
CM Dr. Pramod Sawant Reiterates Goa’s Commitment to ‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:06PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

Taking the celebrations of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) beyond the cinema halls and festival venues, the spectacular IFFI Parade, themed ‘Celebrating the Joy of Cinema’, transformed the streets of Panaji into a vibrant showcase of Goa’s artistic and cultural heritage today. The parade commenced from the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) premises and proceeded to Kala Academy, bringing together a display of colourful floats, traditional craftsmanship, folk performances and enthusiastic community participation.

A visual celebration of Goa’s rich cultural traditions, the parade featured the award-winning floats from the state’s Carnival and Shigmo Utsav celebrations, alongside captivating folk dance performances. Blending the festive spirit of Goa with the universal appeal of cinema, the procession offered visitors, delegates and residents a unique opportunity to experience the state’s cultural vibrancy. It also reflected the spirit of IFFI’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, demonstrating how art and cultural expressions transcend linguistic and geographical boundaries.

Inaugurating the parade, Dr. Pramod Sawant, Chief Minister of Goa, welcomed the dignitaries, artists and visitors to the festival and reiterated the State Government’s commitment to the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat. He emphasised the importance of nurturing local talent, preserving cultural traditions and promoting self-reliance through community-led initiatives. Highlighting the Aakash Kandil competition, he appreciated the enthusiastic participation of Goans in showcasing their creativity through handcrafted traditional lanterns. He noted that such initiatives not only celebrate artistic expression but also strengthen community participation and keep age-old traditions alive. Observing that IFFI’s theme, ‘Stories Without Borders’, found a natural reflection in Goa’s traditional float parades and folk performances, he said that these cultural expressions enable visitors to appreciate the State’s artistic heritage beyond language barriers. He congratulated the participating artists and organisers and described the ongoing edition of IFFI as one of the most successful, extending a warm welcome to visitors on behalf of the Government of Goa.

    

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Delilah M. Lobo, Vice-Chairperson, Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG), highlighted the Aakash Kandil (traditional lantern-making) competition, which received over 350 entries this year, with the peacock as its theme. Congratulating the participants for their creativity and craftsmanship, she also highlighted the special parade showcasing award-winning Carnival floats and vibrant folk performances. She invited visitors and cinema enthusiasts to immerse themselves in Goa’s cultural richness and enjoy the diverse cinematic experiences offered by the festival.

The occasion was graced by the presence of Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting; Shri G. Krishnakumar, Chairman, National Film Development Corporation (NFDC); Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC; Shri Dipak Bandekar, Chief Executive Officer, Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG); and renowned film personalities Shri Aseem Bajaj, Shri Ashley Lobo and Shri Saini S. Johray.

item.title: India wins the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st Venice Art Biennale
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Culture
item.description: Ministry of Culture India wins the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st Venice Art Biennale La Biennale di Venezia names India’s Pavilion the Best National Participation, chosen by the votes of the public About 4.5 lakh visitors to the India Pavilion over the Biennale’s run; among the most visited national pavilions India’s return to Venice after seven years ends with the top honour for the national pavilion Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi: award sets the stage for The India Biennale in New Delhi from 4 December 2026 to 21 March 2027 Posted On: …
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
India wins the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st Venice Art Biennale
La Biennale di Venezia names India’s Pavilion the Best National Participation, chosen by the votes of the public
About 4.5 lakh visitors to the India Pavilion over the Biennale’s run; among the most visited national pavilions
India’s return to Venice after seven years ends with the top honour for the national pavilion
Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi: award sets the stage for The India Biennale in New Delhi from 4 December 2026 to 21 March 2027
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 9:05PM by PIB Delhi

India has won the Visitors’ Lion for Best National Participation at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia (Biennale Arte 2026). The Venice Biennale is widely called the Olympics of the art world. La Biennale di Venezia today announced the winners of the Visitors’ Lions on the basis of the preferences expressed by the public.

Commenting on the result, Mr Pietrangelo Buttafuoco, President of La Biennale di Venezia, said the audience had used the Visitors’ Award to make real Pablo Picasso’s idea that “a painting lives only through the person who looks at it.”

Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat the Union  Minister of Culture said that it is a moment of immense pride for the nation. “This global recognition is a testament to the new age Indian artists and the robust contemporary Indian art scene. It is a celebration of how India’s timeless artistic traditions can find powerful contemporary expression and resonate with people across the world. The award will inspire generations of Indian artists to engage with the world with verve and confidence.”

Secretary Culture Vivek Aggarwal said on this occasion:
“India’s recognition with the prestigious Visitor’s Lion at the Venice Biennale is an immense honour and a moment of national pride. It is a powerful affirmation of India’s contemporary artistic expressions, deeply rooted in our civilizational ethos and material traditions, finding resonance with audiences from across the world. India’s return to the Venice Biennale after a long hiatus marks a significant moment in our renewed engagement with the global cultural landscape. The Pavilion has been part of global conversations on art since its inauguration, reflected in the overwhelmingly positive reviews, enthusiastic feedback and extraordinary footfall of visitors and art connoisseurs from across the world.This recognition marks an important milestone in India’s cultural journey and reaffirms the universal relevance and appeal of our diverse, dynamic and evolving creative expressions.”

About the India Pavilion

The Ministry of Culture presented the National Pavilion of India in collaboration with the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC) and Serendipity Arts. The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), Ministry of Culture, was the Commissioner and IGNCA was the implementing partner for the India Pavilion titled Geographies of Distance: Remembering Home. It was housed in the historic Isolotto spaces of the Arsenale di Venezia. Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated the Pavilion on 6 May 2026.

The exhibition looks at how, for people whose lives are shaped by change or distance, home becomes less a fixed place and more a state they carry with them, made of memory, material, ritual and personal mythology. It responded to the Biennale’s theme, In Minor Keys, through the diversity of India’s regions, materials and craft practices. At the inauguration, Shri Shekhawat had said the exhibition “presents a contemporary India that is both rooted and forward looking.”

Artist

Artwork

Description

Alwar Balasubramaniam (Bala)

Not Just for Us

A series of sculptural panels made using clay and soil sourced from rural Tamil Nadu. Featuring natural fissures and fractures, the works capture the passage of time and environmental forces, exploring the relationship between land, memory and transformation.

Ranjani Shettar

Under the Same Sky

An intricately crafted suspended sculptural installation inspired by flowers and natural growth. Created through traditional hand-crafted processes, the organic forms create an immersive, garden-like environment, bringing together nature, craftsmanship and the idea of home.

Sumakshi Singh

Permanent Address

An immersive, life-size reconstruction of the artist's demolished family home in New Delhi, recreated using delicate embroidered thread. Exploring memory, domestic space and belonging, the installation transforms the idea of home into an enduring emotional and cultural experience.

Skarma Sonam Tashi

Echoes of Home

An installation using papier-mâché to explore the traditional architecture and ecological landscape of Ladakh. The work draws attention to the vulnerability of traditional building practices amid changing environmental conditions and modern construction, raising questions of sustainability and cultural continuity.

Asim Waqif

Chaal

A large-scale bamboo installation inspired by the visual language of scaffolding across India's urban landscapes. Drawing on a material deeply embedded in vernacular building practices, the work explores urban transformation, renewal and the evolving nature of contemporary cities.

Alongside the visual art exhibition, the India Pavilion featured an extended performance programme curated by Serendipity Arts, activating the Pavilion and cultural spaces across Venice through music, movement, storytelling and interdisciplinary performances throughout the Biennale, from May to November 2026.

Visitors’ Favourite in Venice

About 4.5 lakh visitors came to the India Pavilion during the Biennale, making it one of the most visited national pavilions of the edition. Visitors included leading figures from the international art world: museum directors, curators, collectors and critics, as well as well-known personalities from culture and public life.

Alongside the exhibition, Serendipity Arts ran a programme of performances and events across Venice from May to November 2026. It combined visual and performing arts, with interdisciplinary presentations drawn from Indian cultural traditions and the Biennale’s theme. The programme took the Pavilion’s ideas beyond the Arsenale to audiences across the city.

An extraordinary comeback, and the road ahead

India took part in the Venice Art Biennale in 2026 after a gap of seven years. Winning the top honour for national pavilions on its return marks an extraordinary comeback. It reflects India’s growing presence in global contemporary art and in cultural diplomacy.

Continuing with this momentum, the Ministry of Culture will present The India Biennale in New Delhi from 4 December 2026 for 108 days. Its principal venue is Purana Qila, with programming at heritage monuments like Red Fort, Qutub Minar, Jantar Mantar, Safdarjung Tomb, Agrasen ki Baoli and cultural venues across the city. The India Biennale will bring contemporary art, architecture and design into India’s historic monuments and will have a dedicated Students Biennale also. The India Biennale is being organized through a unique public private partnership in which the Ministry of Culture provides the shell and core infrastructure and access to venues while the exhibition set up is being done by private participants. The event will offer Indian and international audiences a city-wide celebration of the country’s living heritage and creative energy through a unique Biennale Pass, in the spirit of Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi.

 ***

M Annadurai

item.title: Subtitling is more than Translation, it is the Art of Carrying Emotions Across Languages: Rekhs at IFFI 2026
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Subtitling is more than Translation, it is the Art of Carrying Emotions Across Languages: Rekhs at IFFI 2026 Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:54PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 25 November 2026 Renowned subtitler Rekhs, who has translated more than 800 films across five languages, shared insights into the art of subtitling and its role in taking Indian cinema to global audiences during a masterclass titled ‘ Words Across Borders: Subtitling Across Cultures ’ at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Subtitling is more than Translation, it is the Art of Carrying Emotions Across Languages: Rekhs at IFFI 2026
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:54PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

Renowned subtitler Rekhs, who has translated more than 800 films across five languages, shared insights into the art of subtitling and its role in taking Indian cinema to global audiences during a masterclass titled ‘Words Across Borders: Subtitling Across Cultures’ at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

Emphasising that subtitling goes beyond translating words, Rekhs said it requires patience, creativity, cultural understanding, and sensitivity to the emotions embedded in a film. Highlighting the importance of precision, she said, “Patience is essential in subtitling. You have to check and recheck.”

Rekhs recalled that before the advent of OTT platforms, subtitles were largely prepared for films being sent to award programmes. Digital streaming has since expanded their reach, enabling regional cinema to find audiences worldwide. However, she expressed concern over OTT platforms altering subtitles and stressed the need to preserve the integrity of the original translation.

Sharing her creative approach, she explained that subtitling has no definitive rulebook and often requires individual methods. She prefers song subtitles to rhyme, helping audiences distinguish lyrics from dialogue. She also uses a pyramid-like structure, placing shorter sentences above longer ones, and favours yellow subtitles for better visibility.

Illustrating the nuances involved, Rekhs spoke about the challenges of translating colloquial expressions and songs, including Dangamari. She also cited the Tamil words ‘vaesham’ and ‘vesham,’ explaining how a small difference in pronunciation can change the meaning from disguise to poison. Recalling her work on Kabali, she shared how she used expressions such as “indulgent laughter” and “sceptical chuckle” to convey the different shades of Rajinikanth's laughter.

Highlighting subtitling as a tool for inclusion, she emphasised its importance for persons with hearing disabilities. She also pointed out that culturally specific expressions and relationships require careful interpretation rather than literal translation.

Addressing the growing use of artificial intelligence, Rekhs cautioned that AI-generated subtitles can distort meanings, alter gender references and miss the emotional context of a scene. “AI knows the dictionary, but it does not know the drama or the emotion of the soul,” she remarked, underlining the continuing importance of human creativity.

“Subtitles are not post-production leftovers,” she said, emphasising that good subtitling must convey the sense and emotion of a film rather than merely reproduce its dialogue. It enables stories to cross linguistic and cultural boundaries and connect with audiences worldwide.

Organised by the National Film…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
WAVES Film Bazaar Marks 20th Edition with 2,288 Delegates from 54 Countries
220 B2B meetings held at the Co-Production Market, with 14 MoUs and agreements nearing finalisation
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:41PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

The 20th edition of WAVES Film Bazaar brought together 2,288 delegates from 54 countries, including 471 buyers, marking two decades of connecting filmmakers, nurturing talent and building bridges between Indian and international cinema. Organised by the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) alongside the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), the five-day marketplace witnessed the signing of two letters of intent for India-Chile co-productions, while 14 MoUs and agreements are nearing finalisation following business interactions.

Sharing the key outcomes at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Shri Prabhat, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, said that the Co-Production Market facilitated around 220 scheduled one-to-one meetings.

Shri Ashutosh Gowariker, Festival Director, IFFI; Shri Dhiraj Singh, Managing Director, NFDC; and Shri Sreerag M, Officer on Special Duty, WAVES Film Bazaar, also participated in the interaction.

Key Highlights of the 20th Edition

Co-Production Market

  • 25 projects representing eight countries and 16 languages, including 13 Indian languages, participated in the market.
  • Around 220 scheduled one-to-one meetings were held, alongside additional business interactions.
  • Production house Khan & Kumar Media came on board as a producer for Hurda (That Tight Green Top), one of the selected feature projects.
  • Two letters of intent for India-Chile co-productions were signed.

Project Development and Industry Opportunities

WAVES Film Bazaar supported projects at different stages of development through its Co-Production Market, Screenwriters’ Lab, Work-in-Progress Lab and Viewing Room.

  • Recorded 170 project entries, in Viewing Room, with 155 films viewed by 608 visitors over nearly 100 hours. The projects represented 11 countries and a wide range of languages.
  • The Bengaluru International Short Film Festival will select four short films from the Viewing Room for consideration in its festival programme. Panorama Studios is considering projects for theatrical distribution, in-flight entertainment and non-theatrical rights.
  • Five projects were selected from 53 submissions, from Work-in-Progress Lab section. Each project received three feedback sessions from industry mentors.
  • At Screenwriters’ Lab, filmmaker Santosh Singh and Super Zero Films came on board as director and co-producer, alongside Travelin Bone Entertainment, for The Japanese Wife, a selected project by Sanchita Sinha.

Awards and Professional Support

WAVES Film Bazaar extended financial and professional support to projects through cash grants, distribution opportunities, fellowships, casting services and post-production assistance.

  • NFDC Cash Grants:
  • USD 10,000 to Nose Bone, directed by Garima Pura.
  • USD 5,000 each to Goodbye Mr D’Mello, directed by Ridham Janve, and Fireflowers, directed by Sreemoyee Singh.
  • Reborn India Film Cash Grant: INR 1 lakh to And on That Day…, directed by Kushal Kishore and Kushagra Kishore.
  • Mukesh Chhabra Casting Award: Free casting services for Goodbye Mr D’Mello.
  • Prasad Corporation Post-Production Award: Nadhi, directed by Aditya Vempaty.
  • Mica Creative Fellowship: Aattumali (By the River), directed by Ajith Velayudhan.
  • Moviebuff Post-Production Awards: Aaram Nagar, Kaareng and Chakachaundh.
  • Reborn India Film Distribution Award: Bhai Band (One Two Three Mic Check), directed by Manish Saini.
  • Work-in-Progress Lab Awards:
  • Prasad Corporation Post-Production Award to The Garden of Us, with special mentions for Family Matter, Saja (The Blackstone Ratio) and Where Has the River Gone.
  • Nube Studio Post-Production Award to Aattumali (By the River).
  • IICT Work-in-Progress Lab Award to The Garden of Us.

Pavilions, Technology and Startups

  • 12 State Pavilions and four Country Pavilions were hosted, with Russia participating as the Partner Country.
  • The marketplace featured 22 market stalls.
  • The technology segment included companies such as Netflix and Dolphin AI, which launched its AI Studio at the marketplace.
  • The WaveX Startup Showcase brought together 10 startups working across media, entertainment and emerging technologies.
  • Based on post-event feedback, the participating startups reported more than 299 meetings and 14 deals and agreements across six startups, including one MoU.

Knowledge Series

Held from 21 to 24 November, the four-day Knowledge Series featured 25 panel sessions with around 127 panellists and 17 moderators from India and abroad along with Leading industry representatives such as Netflix India, Prime Video, Amazon MGM Studios. Discussions covered:

  • Indian stories and their evolution into global intellectual property.
  • Streaming trends and the changing entertainment landscape.
  • Independent cinema and international co-productions.
  • Film financing and regional filmmaking ecosystems.
  • AVGC-XR, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
  • Future creative skills and opportunities in the media and entertainment sector.

The sessions brought together filmmakers, actors, producers, OTT executives, festival programmers, distributors, policymakers, investors and technology professionals.

Observing that the impact of the marketplace would unfold over time, Shri Prabhat said, "These interactions, so many B2B meetings, and animated discussions would show result maybe next year, next to next year, or coming three-four years."

Shri Ashutosh Gowariker emphasised the need to embrace emerging technologies while retaining the centrality of human creativity and emotion. He described AI as a tool that can assist filmmakers but cannot replace human intervention. He added that technological advancements would expand the possibilities of cinematic expression without diminishing the importance of content-driven films.

Shri Sreerag M highlighted the platform's contribution to independent Indian cinema, citing films such as Aattam, Boom and Angh as examples of projects supported by WAVES Film Bazaar that subsequently received national and international recognition.

The press conference was moderated by Shri Sayyid Rabeehashmi.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
MSDE partners with Ministry of Jal Shakti to skill one lakh youth under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
The initiative will leverage the nationwide network of ITIs and NSTIs to develop a skilled workforce for rural water supply operations and maintenance
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:31PM by PIB Delhi

In an effort to align vocational training with emerging employment opportunities in the rural water sector, the Directorate General of Training (DGT), under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti. The partnership will focus on implementing the Water Supply Operation & Maintenance Skilling Programme (Nal Jal Mitra) under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0.

The initiative aims to train and certify at least one lakh candidates, with an estimated financial outlay of ₹111.93 crore, entirely funded by DDWS.

The MoU was signed in the presence of Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship; Shri C. R. Patil, Union Minister of Jal Shakti; and Shri V. Somanna, Minister of State, Jal Shakti.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Minister of State for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, underscored that the initiative represents a significant example of inter-ministerial convergence aimed at addressing the skilled manpower requirements of a key national programme. He highlighted that the country's extensive network of Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs) offers an effective platform for imparting specialised skills required for rural water supply operations and maintenance.

The 165-hour training programme has been developed by the Central Staff Training and Research Institute (CSTARI) under DGT, in consultation with DDWS. It will be offered as an optional elective to existing and former trainees of the Craftsmen Training Scheme (CTS) Fitter and Plumber trades across ITIs and NSTIs.

The programme combines 120 hours of institutional training with 45 hours of mandatory on-the-job training. Candidates will learn plumbing, water distribution, pump and motor maintenance, basic electrical work and water quality monitoring. Upon successful completion, trainees will receive a National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF)-aligned short-term training certificate from DGT in addition to their National Trade Certificate (NTC).

The National Instructional Media Institute (NIMI), under DGT, will oversee training coordination, assessment, certification and fund disbursement. DDWS will make the details of certified candidates available at the district and Gram Panchayat levels, where they may be engaged for work as per the policies of the respective states.

Nearly 16 crore rural households in India now have tap water connections. Keeping these water supply systems functional requires trained personnel at the village level. The programme seeks to meet this requirement and, in the process, open up employment avenues for rural youth.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
ICGS Sujay Concludes Visit to Trincomalee
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:29PM by PIB Delhi

Indian Coast Guard Ship (ICGS) Sujay, a Samarth-class Offshore Patrol Vessel, concluded its three-day visit to Trincomalee, Sri Lanka, from 23 to 25 November 2026. The visit aimed at strengthening bilateral maritime cooperation, particularly in the field of Marine Pollution Response (MPR).

During the visit, the specialist Pollution Response team embarked onboard ICGS Sujay conducted hands-on training for Sri Lanka Coast Guard (SLCG) personnel on the operation and deployment of MPR equipment. The training enhanced professional exchanges and strengthened joint operational preparedness towards ensuring cleaner and safer seas.

The visit also featured a series of engagements to promote camaraderie and people-to-people connect, including a joint yoga session themed 'Yoga for Healthy Ageing', a friendly volleyball match and an open-ship visit for local citizens.

A key highlight of the deployment was the embarkation of 22 NCC cadets, three officers and seven support staff participating in the India-Sri Lanka Maitri Sethu Yatra Joint International Cycling Expedition. The team embarked onboard ICGS Sujay for their sea passage from Trincomalee to Karaikal and is scheduled to arrive on 26 November 2026.

The visit of ICGS Sujay underscores India's commitment to its 'Neighbourhood First' policy and the vision of SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region). It further reinforces the enduring India-Sri Lanka maritime partnership through enhanced operational cooperation, capacity building and contributing towards safe, secure and clean seas in the Indian Ocean Region.

item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Krishnavataram brings Lord Krishna’s life to the screen through Satyabhama’s eyes First part of a three-film series explores love, devotion, and lesser-known chapters of Krishna’s life Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:00PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 25 November 2026 Makers of the Hindi feature film Krishnavataram (Krishnavataram Part 1: The Heart), screened under the Indian Panorama Feature Films section at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, addressed a press conference organized by the Press Information…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Krishnavataram brings Lord Krishna’s life to the screen through Satyabhama’s eyes
First part of a three-film series explores love, devotion, and lesser-known chapters of Krishna’s life
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 8:00PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

Makers of the Hindi feature film Krishnavataram (Krishnavataram Part 1: The Heart), screened under the Indian Panorama Feature Films section at the International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026, addressed a press conference organized by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) today. Director Hardik Gajjar and producer Sajan Raj Kurup shared insights on bringing a visually enriched, contemporary cinematic interpretation of Lord Krishna’s life to global audiences.

Speaking on the core idea behind the film, producer Sajan Raj Kurup said that in India, Lord Krishna cannot be boxed into the category of mythology. “Krishna in India is beyond mythology. This is faith, an emotion, and a living part of our history,” he remarked. Raised in a cultural tradition centred around Adikeshava, he recalled the belief that “everything comes from Krishna,” adding that the team worked deliberately to portray his life with sincerity and deep respect.

The filmmakers also shared that Krishnavataram is the first chapter of a three-part trilogy built around Heart, Mind, and Soul. Adapted from Raam Mori’s novel Satyabhama, with a screenplay by Prakash Kapadia, Raam Mori, and Hardik Gajjar and drawing on the Srimad Bhagavatam and Harivamsa, the opening part follows Krishna’s journey from Vrindavan and Mathura to his rule in Dwarka through Satyabhama’s eyes. While Part 1 centres on love, sacrifice, separation, and devotion, the next two parts will examine his statecraft and strategy (The Mind) and the teachings of the Bhagavad Gita (The Soul). Featuring lesser-known episodes from Krishna’s life, the film stars Siddharth Gupta, Sanskruti Jayana, Sushmitha Bhat, and Nivaashiyni Krishnan play key roles.

Addressing the need to connect traditional narratives with modern viewers, director Hardik Gajjar explained that the movie is specially built for the younger generation so they can discover and relate to their history in an engaging cinematic language. “Storytelling can keep on changing, and we are fortunate to live in a time where we can create visually enriched experiences,” the makers shared. Drawing on Gajjar’s visual effects background and built on a massive 7.5 acre set with some of the best talent working on VFX, the film has been made in multiple languages, including English, specifically to resonate with young people worldwide.

Highlighting the pivotal role of the soundtrack in driving emotional connection, Gajjar spoke about collaborating with music director Prasad S. Under the guidance of renowned maestro Dr. Bharat Balvalli, the team included as much classical music as they could, seamlessly blending traditional purity with a contemporary touch to connect with today’s audience.

The session was moderated by Shri. Sandeep Prasad.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Only Five Days Left to Apply for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Encourages Eligible Students to Avail Opportunity for Quality Residential Education SHRESHTA Scheme Opens Doors to Quality Education in Reputed Private Residential Schools for Meritorious Scheduled Caste (SC) and Eligible De-notified Tribe (DNT) Students Eligible Students and Parents Encouraged to Complete Online Registration by November 30, 2026 National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) Scheduled to be Held on January 10, 2027 Candidates Can Apply Online…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Only Five Days Left to Apply for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027; Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment Encourages Eligible Students to Avail Opportunity for Quality Residential Education
SHRESHTA Scheme Opens Doors to Quality Education in Reputed Private Residential Schools for Meritorious Scheduled Caste (SC) and Eligible De-notified Tribe (DNT) Students
Eligible Students and Parents Encouraged to Complete Online Registration by November 30, 2026
National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) Scheduled to be Held on January 10, 2027
Candidates Can Apply Online at https://exams.nta.nic.in/shreshta
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 7:51PM by PIB Delhi

With only five days remaining for the closure of online registration for the National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, has called upon eligible students across the country to come forward and avail themselves of the opportunity to pursue quality education in reputed private residential schools under the SHRESHTA Scheme.

The Scheme for Residential Education for Students in High Schools in Targeted Areas (SHRESHTA), implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, aims to provide quality education to meritorious students belonging to Scheduled Castes (SCs) and De-notified Tribes (DNTs) not covered under the SC, ST and OBC categories, thereby creating greater opportunities for academic advancement, social mobility and holistic development.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Scheme seeks to bridge educational disparities by enabling meritorious students from targeted communities to access conducive learning environments, pursue academic excellence and realise their full potential. Access to quality school education plays a pivotal role in strengthening academic capabilities and creating opportunities for a brighter and more secure future, the Official said.

With the registration deadline fast approaching, eligible students and their parents have been asked to complete the application process at the earliest and avoid last-minute difficulties, the Official said.

Wider awareness and dissemination of information about the Scheme, particularly in rural, remote and underserved areas, can help ensure that deserving students do not miss this important educational opportunity due to a lack of awareness, he said.

The Official said the online registration process for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027, being conducted in collaboration with the National Testing Agency (NTA), commenced on November 14, 2026, will remain open until November 30, 2026 (up to 11:50 PM).

The Official said to facilitate candidates in making necessary corrections to their submitted application forms, a correction window will remain operational from December 2 to December 4, 2026.

The National Entrance Test for SHRESHTA (NETS) 2027 is scheduled to be conducted on January 10, 2027, he said.

Eligible candidates may submit their online applications through the official National Testing Agency (NTA) portal at https://exams.nta.nic.in/shreshta.

Candidates and their parents have been advised to carefully read the eligibility criteria and application-related instructions available on the official portal before completing the registration process.

Teachers, educational institutions, community organisations and other stakeholders have been urged to disseminate information about the Scheme among eligible students and their families to facilitate wider participation and ensure that the benefits of the initiative reach the intended beneficiaries across the country.

Through targeted educational interventions such as SHRESHTA, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to reaffirm its commitment to promoting equal educational opportunities, empowering future generations and ensuring that socio-economic disadvantages do not become barriers to educational advancement, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.
