item.title: Tago Explores the Search for Home, Human Fragility and the Consequences of Force; Makes World Premiere at 57th IFFI
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Tago Explores the Search for Home, Human Fragility and the Consequences of Force; Makes World Premiere at 57th IFFI Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 25 November 2026 Addressing a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, director Aleksandr Anisimov and co-screenplay writer Veronika Oznobishina spoke about Tago , which had its World Premiere at the festival in the Cinema of the World section.…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Tago Explores the Search for Home, Human Fragility and the Consequences of Force; Makes World Premiere at 57th IFFI
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 7:43PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

Addressing a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa, director Aleksandr Anisimov and co-screenplay writer Veronika Oznobishina spoke about Tago, which had its World Premiere at the festival in the Cinema of the World section. Made with non-professional actors drawn from local communities and set against Georgia's natural landscapes, the film explores the search for home and belonging, human fragility, gender dynamics and the consequences of responding to conflict through force.

Set in a remote Georgian village surrounded by mist-covered mountains, the story begins when a local man discovers the body of a young stranger on a riverbank and brings him home to his wife and young son. The unexpected arrival disrupts the family's already fragile existence, setting off a chain of events that compels its members to make difficult and extreme choices.

Speaking about the film's portrayal of gender dynamics and the emotional confinement experienced by its female protagonist, Oznobishina said, "The very first thing we wanted to show was that the woman lives in a cage within her own house, while the man fails to understand the predicament she faces in her everyday life."

She explained that the film also follows the upheavals confronting the male protagonist, whose response is driven by an overwhelming surge of energy that prevents him from making the right choices. She emphasised the importance of inner resilience and the strength required to confront unfavourable circumstances.

Anisimov spoke about the protagonist's approach to conflict, observing that he chooses to resolve his problems in the old-fashioned way, through force. Drawing parallels with human behaviour across societies, he noted that people often resort to force when faced with difficult situations. The film examines the consequences of such choices and questions whether force can resolve life's complex problems.

The film took shape during Anisimov's travels across Georgia, where he observed the lives of ordinary people, their motivations and the circumstances shaping their experiences. During one such journey, he encountered a Georgian theatre actor, and the two joined hands to bring the story to the screen. They decided to cast non-professional actors from local communities, making the participation of local residents central to the project.

Anisimov discovered the film's female lead, Magdalena Bolqvadze, at a bus stop. Something in her persona suggested a tragic story to him, prompting him to envision how the camera could capture that emotion without filters. This chance encounter eventually led to her casting in the film.

The team also recorded hundreds of videos of local residents before finalising the cast. Working with a modest budget, the filmmakers gradually involved more people from the surrounding communities. Anisimov expressed particular gratitude to the people of Georgia, whose generosity and support included providing costumes and helping the crew with logistical arrangements.

Actor Egor Skorokhodov, who also comes from a non-professional acting background, shared that he connected with the director by chance and subsequently became part of the filmmaking journey.

The team expressed happiness at presenting the film at IFFI, appreciating the opportunity to watch films from across the world and engage with diverse cinematic voices.

The press conference was moderated by Sandeep Sunil.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
The Ministry of Women and Child Development launched #NumberSaveKiya? Campaign, released Advisory on 16 Days of activism against gender based violence & signed an inter-ministerial MoU for strengthening services for Women Safety at Nayi Chetna 5.0
Union Minister Smt. Annpurna Devi addressed the national campaign on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment on 25 November 2026
#NumberSaveKiya? campaign urged every woman to save Women Helpline 181 and Emergency 112 on her phone
MoWCD, DoJ, NALSA and DoRD signed Joint MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 7:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Women and Child Development joined the Ministry of Rural Development for the inauguration of Nayi Chetna 5.0, the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women Empowerment, on 25 November 2026 at the Bharat Ratna C. Subramaniam Auditorium, PUSA, New Delhi. The event coincided with the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women and the start of the 16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence.

The national event was graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Union Minister of Women and Child Development, along with Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister of Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers' Welfare.

The Secretaries of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the Department of Rural Development also attended the event.

Key announcements

Advisory on the 16 Days campaign: The dignitaries released a Joint advisory issued by 10 Ministries and NALSA, guiding States and Union Territories to spread awareness, open access to support and legal aid, make women's safety everyone's responsibility, with the theme ‘From awareness to action & From access to agency’.

#NumberSaveKiya? Campaign: Built around one simple question, “Number save kiya?” (Have you saved the number?), the campaign video urged every woman, and those around her, to save the Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Support System 112 on their phones. Helpline 181 is a 24x7, toll-free service, linking women facing violence to police, One Stop Centres, medical care and legal aid. The campaign will be amplified through the Ministry’s digital platforms and its grassroots network of Anganwadi workers, One Stop Centres and Mission Shakti hubs.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Annpurna Devi launched the #NumberSaveKiya? campaign and the Helpline Anthem, and urged everyone to save the Women Helpline 181, Emergency Helpline 112 and Child Helpline 1098 on their phones and to spread awareness among others. She said, “In this digital age, the mobile phone has become a great companion. In times of distress, a woman can get immediate help with just one call to a One Stop Centre, Gender Resource Centre or the Women Helpline near her. But sometimes, under extreme stress, she may not remember the number, and help may be delayed. Knowing the right information and the right contact number at the time of need can be the first step towards handling even the biggest difficulty. Our message through this campaign is: know the number, save the number and share it with others. I would like to ask each one of you, ‘Number save kiya?’”

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages. He also encouraged everyone to save the Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Helpline 112 on their phones.

Inter-Ministerial MoU: An Inter-Ministerial MoU was signed by the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Department of Justice, NALSA and Department of Rural Development to launch the Violence-Free Village Initiative, bringing legal aid, women’s support services and community institutions together at the village level.

Convergence on the ground

The morning sessions featured two panel discussions: one on ministerial convergence through Gender Resource Centres, One Stop Centres, the Legal Services Authority and the health system, and another with women leaders from the field. New Gender Resource Centres were launched, and SHG leaders and One Stop Centre administrators shared their experiences. The event also saw the release of video resources and the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report, and the launch of the Nayi Chetna 5.0 Campaign.

As a part of Nayi Chetna 5.0, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, through its ‘Mission Shakti’, reaffirmed its commitment to the safety, security and empowerment of every woman.

             ****

During the journey, the participants visited…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Culture
Over 1,100 Students Complete Five-Day ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ Under Somnath Swabhiman Parv; Return to New Delhi
Students visit Somnath temples, pilgrimage sites and historical landmarks to understand India's rich cultural and spiritual heritage
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 7:25PM by PIB Delhi

The five-day ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’, organised under the Somnath Swabhiman Parv from 20 to 25 November 2026, concluded with the return of more than 1,100 students to Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi. During the journey, the participants visited various temples, pilgrimage sites and historical landmarks in Somnath, gaining a closer understanding of India's rich spiritual and cultural heritage.

The journey began on 20 November when Union Minister for Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat flagged off the special train from Safdarjung Railway Station, New Delhi. The train reached Veraval Railway Station in Gujarat on 21 November, where the students received a vibrant traditional welcome with folk dance performances and flower showers.

On 22 November, the students visited Shri Ram Temple at Prabhas Patan, Golokdham Tirth and the revered first Jyotirlinga, Shri Somnath Mahadev Temple. They also attended the ‘Jai Somnath’ Light and Sound Show at the Somnath Temple, which presented the temple's rich history and its enduring significance.

On 23 November, the youngsters visited Baan Ganga, Bhidbhanjan Mahadev Temple, Bhalka Tirth and Ahilyabai Temple. They also visited the museum and the Swadeshi Haat, where they got an opportunity to learn about local culture and indigenous products. The day's activities concluded with students experiencing the divine Aarti at Triveni Ghat.

On 24 November, the students departed from Veraval Railway Station for New Delhi by the special train. The journey concluded on 25 November with their arrival at Safdarjung Railway Station, where they received a warm welcome.

The five-day journey offered students an opportunity to experience the religious and historical significance of Somnath and understand the resilience of India's cultural heritage. Sharing their experiences, participants described the Yatra as more than a spiritual journey, calling it a memorable experience that brought them closer to India's culture, heritage and history.

The Somnath Swabhiman Parv is being organised to mark 1,000 years since the first recorded attack on the Somnath Temple. As part of the celebrations, special journeys are being organised to connect devotees and visitors from different parts of the country with the spiritual and cultural heritage of Somnath. More than 35,000 people have so far visited Somnath Mahadev through these initiatives.

The ‘Yuva Somnath Yatra’ was part of this broader initiative, aimed at connecting the younger generation with India's historical legacy, cultural values and rich heritage. Through such initiatives, the Ministry of Culture continues to encourage young people to learn about and engage with the country's diverse cultural traditions and historical landmarks.

 ***

M Annadurai

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Ego We Reach All Explores Street Childhood, Identity and Resilience in Ghana; Filmmakers Highlight the Potential of International Collaborations
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 7:01PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

The team behind Ego We Reach All (Our Time Will Come), an international co-production from Ghana, France and Saudi Arabia, interacted with the media today at the Press Conference Hall on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Panaji, Goa. Screened under the International Cinema section, the 104-minute feature is celebrating its Asia Premiere at the festival.

Director Amartei Armar and Producer Yemoh Ike shared insights into the film’s creative journey, its exploration of childhood and survival on the streets of Ghana and the importance of international collaborations in bringing locally rooted stories to audiences across the world.

Speaking about the film’s thematic inspiration, Director Amartei Armar said he has long been fascinated by street childhood in Ghana and the stories of young people navigating life on the margins. The film, he said, seeks to explore how stories of those often overlooked by society can be brought into the larger national and cinematic discourse. Through the narrative, the filmmakers seek to affirm that young people from diverse circumstances are equally part of the country and its future.

Reflecting on his filmmaking journey and his continued connection with Ghana, Armar emphasized the need for filmmakers to take ownership of their stories and make their voices heard. He noted that independent filmmakers often work within financial constraints, making it imperative to create films that demonstrate cinematic quality and storytelling potential to attract investors and strengthen the industry.

Highlighting the scope for cultural exchange between India and Ghana, the filmmakers drew parallels between the cinematic cultures of the two countries, citing Ghana’s ‘Ghallywood’ as a counterpart to India’s Bollywood. They noted that audiences in both countries could find cultural resonances in each other’s storytelling traditions, given the similarities in certain cultural experiences and social realities.

The filmmakers also expressed interest in exploring greater collaboration between Indian and Ghanaian filmmakers, including opportunities to bring creative talent, stories and cinematic experiences from Ghana to India and vice versa. Such partnerships, they observed, could foster cultural understanding, create new opportunities for filmmakers and strengthen the visibility of African cinema on international platforms.

The Press Conference was moderated by Shri. Manan Singh.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Addresses HealthX Elevate 2026, Highlights India’s Growing Healthcare Innovation Ecosystem
India’s Start-up Ecosystem Expands from Around 350 in 2014 to Over 2.5 Lakh, with More Than 60% from Tier-II and Tier-III Cities: Dr. Jitendra Singh
AI, Genomics and Precision Medicine to Strengthen Early Diagnosis and Individualised Healthcare: Dr. Jitendra Singh
India Needs Greater Industry Participation to Translate Healthcare Research into Globally Recognised Innovations: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 6:54PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh today highlighted India’s expanding StartUp ecosystem, growing capabilities in biotechnology and healthcare innovation, and the increasing role of artificial intelligence (AI), genomics and precision medicine in transforming healthcare, while addressing HealthX Elevate 2026.

The Minister noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest start-up ecosystem, with more than 60 per cent of StartUps coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities and smaller towns.

The event, themed around healthcare start-ups and innovation, brought together healthcare leaders, entrepreneurs, investors and experts to discuss the evolving landscape of healthcare innovation in India.

Speaking during a Fire Chat session, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India’s start-up ecosystem has undergone a remarkable transformation, expanding from around 350 start-ups in 2014 to more than 2.5 lakh today. He noted that India has emerged as the world’s third-largest start-up ecosystem, with more than 60 per cent of start-ups coming from Tier-II and Tier-III cities.

The Minister said that the growth of start-ups is no longer confined to major metropolitan hubs such as Bengaluru, Delhi and Mumbai. Digital access and an enabling ecosystem have made information, resources and opportunities available to aspiring entrepreneurs across the country, allowing talent from smaller cities and towns to participate in the start-up movement.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the emergence of entrepreneurship beyond conventional technology and science-led fields. Referring to the growth of agri-based start-ups, he said that entrepreneurial success does not necessarily require a highly advanced academic qualification, but calls for passion, focus and the ability to use technology effectively. He added that the Government is extending technological and financial support to encourage entrepreneurship.

The Minister highlighted the significant expansion of India’s biotechnology start-up ecosystem, which, he said, has grown from around 50–60 start-ups in 2014 to nearly 10,000 today. He said that India is increasingly developing solutions not only for diseases prevalent in tropical regions, but also for conditions that were earlier primarily associated with other parts of the world.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India’s progress in vaccines has transformed the way the country’s healthcare capabilities are viewed globally. He referred to the development of the country’s DNA vaccine for COVID-19 and its supply to around 30 countries. He also highlighted advances in genetic and therapeutic research, including a successful trial of a genetic therapy for haemophilia, the findings of which were published in the New England Journal of Medicine.

Referring to developments in nuclear medicine, the Minister said that Indian researchers are working on cost-effective solutions for diseases, including acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. He noted that India is moving beyond addressing diseases traditionally associated with the country and is developing affordable therapeutic and diagnostic solutions with wider global relevance.

Dr. Jitendra Singh emphasised the need for greater private-sector participation in biotechnology, healthcare research and innovation. He said that the Government is encouraging private partners to contribute to research and development, and expressed hope that India would produce a globally recognised blockbuster drug in the coming decade.

The Minister also highlighted India’s unique advantage in healthcare research due to its diverse population and genetic resources. He said that a comprehensive understanding of genetic data could help researchers generate insights relevant not only to India but also to the global scientific community.

On the role of artificial intelligence in healthcare, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that AI should be viewed as an enabling tool across disciplines rather than as a separate domain. He highlighted its potential in diagnosis, data collection and analysis, noting that processes which earlier took hours or days could now be completed in minutes with AI support.

Referring to the Genome India initiative, the Minister said that AI is facilitating the analysis of genetic information and supporting the study of diverse population groups. He noted that the Government had completed gene sequencing of 10,000 individuals, with the data covering 80 different population groups.

The Minister said that India is entering an era of individualised and precision medicine, in which treatment may be tailored to the genetic profile, lifestyle, environment and molecular characteristics of each patient. He noted that advances in research could enable doctors to move towards more personalised prescriptions, even for patients presenting with similar disease or investigation profiles.

He also underscored the growing importance of preventive healthcare, early detection and research into biomarkers that may help identify the likelihood of diseases before they develop. Referring to research on diabetes-related pregnancy, he said that scientists are working on biomarkers that could help assess the risk of diabetes in women at the time of delivery, enabling more targeted follow-up and preventive care.

During the interaction, Dr. Jitendra Singh said that India is witnessing a gradual shift towards deep-tech and science-led enterprises, including biotechnology, quantum technology, artificial intelligence and space. He noted that the opening of new sectors to private participation is creating opportunities for entrepreneurs and said that the emergence of successful businesses in these areas would encourage further industry investment.

Responding to a question on the challenges faced by deep-tech start-ups in securing their first major customer, the Minister said that the Government is working towards creating a more enabling environment. He referred to changes made to allow greater risk-taking in the support extended to start-ups, including the removal of a requirement under a CSIR provision that a start-up must have been in existence for at least three years before it could receive funding.

Dr. Jitendra Singh also highlighted the importance of collaboration between government, industry, researchers and healthcare professionals. He said that the era of working in silos is over and that pooling expertise, resources and investment can help accelerate innovation and bring research closer to practical application.

Concluding his remarks, the Minister emphasised that the goal of healthcare innovation must be to ensure affordable and accessible healthcare for all. He said that this would require an integrated, whole-of-nation approach, with the government, industry and medical professionals working together, alongside a stronger culture of philanthropy to support research and innovation.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Shri B L Verma Launches ‘SAMAVESH’ and New e-Anudaan Portal to Strengthen Digital Governance and Inclusive Welfare Delivery
SAMAVESH Provides Unified Digital Access to Department’s Schemes, Services and Organisational Portals, Strengthening Citizen-Centric Governance
AI-Powered ‘Samajik Sahayak’ Chatbot to Facilitate Access to Welfare Scheme Information in 22 Indian Languages through BHASHINI
New e-Anudaan Portal to Simplify Grant-in-Aid Processes, Promote Ease of Doing Business and Strengthen Transparency and Accountability
MoUs with BHASHINI and National Skill Development Corporation to Strengthen Multilingual Service Delivery, Skill Development and Employment Opportunities
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

In a significant step towards strengthening technology-enabled governance and ensuring accessible, transparent and efficient delivery of social welfare services, Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, along with Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri B. L. Verma, launched SAMAVESH (Single Access Mechanism for All Verticals of Empowerment & Social Harmony) and the new e-Anudaan Portal, at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, in the National Capital here today.

The launch of SAMAVESH and the new e-Anudaan Portal marks a significant milestone in the Department’s digital transformation journey. These initiatives seek to make social welfare schemes and services more accessible, reduce procedural difficulties for beneficiaries and implementing organisations, and strengthen transparency, accountability and technology-enabled delivery of social welfare programmes.

Senior officers of the Ministry, representatives of NeGD, NIC, NGOs and other stakeholder organisations were also present on the occasion.

Addressing the gathering, Dr. Virendra Kumar described the launching of SAMAVESH and new e-Anudaan portals as historical and a game changer and highlighted the Department’s commitment towards leveraging technology to strengthen the delivery of welfare schemes and services.

The Minister emphasised that SAMAVESH represents an important step towards integrated, transparent and citizen-centric governance by bringing the Department’s digital services onto a common platform.

Dr Kumar also underscored the potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital integration and data-driven monitoring in improving the accessibility, transparency and effectiveness of welfare delivery.

Speaking on the occasion, Shri B. L. Verma highlighted the importance of making Government schemes more accessible to beneficiaries through simplified digital services. He emphasised that technology-driven initiatives such as SAMAVESH would enable citizens, particularly those belonging to disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society, to access information and services more conveniently while promoting transparency and inclusion.

Shri Sudhansh Pant, Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, described the launch as a golden day in the Ministry’s history, marking a significant leap in digital governance with the integration of 33 different portals into a single SAMAVESH Portal.

He highlighted that e-Anudaan 2.0 has reduced the number of forms from 283 to 182, significantly easing procedural requirements for NGOs and institutions. The introduction of real-time remote inspections through Bharat VC with 15 minutes’ prior notice will further strengthen institutional monitoring and accountability. He also underscored the integration of AI, BHASHINI, DigiLocker and PFMS to enhance accessibility and efficiency.

Appreciating the efforts of the IT team under the leadership of Additional Secretary Ms. Mona K. Khandhar and Director Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, along with NeGD and NIC, the Secretary reaffirmed the Ministry’s commitment to advancing the Hon’ble Prime Minister’s vision of Ease of Living through technology-enabled governance.

Developed by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), SAMAVESH provides a unified digital gateway to the Department’s schemes, services and organisational portals through https://www.dosje.gov.in/samavesh-citizen-portals/,enabling citizens to access a wide range of welfare-related information and services through a common platform.

The platform brings together six major scheme-related portals, including Senior Citizens Welfare (SCW), National Overseas Scholarship (NOS), Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan (NMBA), SAMBAL - National Helpline Against Atrocities (NHAA), Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) and Support for Marginalised Individuals for Livelihood and Enterprise (SMILE), covering welfare initiatives for transgender persons, rehabilitation of persons engaged in begging and Garima Greh.

SAMAVESH also brings together 12 organisational and institutional portals, including those of Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), Babu Jagjivan Ram National Foundation, National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), Dr. Ambedkar International Centre (DAIC), National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC), National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC), National Commission for Safai Karamcharis (NCSK), Development and Welfare Board for De-notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Communities (DWBDNC) and the Department’s Social Justice Portal.

The unified platform is designed to simplify access to welfare schemes and services, eliminating the need for citizens to search across multiple websites. A common login facility provides a more consistent user experience, while a consolidated Beneficiary Dashboard is intended to facilitate access to beneficiary-related information and strengthen monitoring of scheme implementation.

A key citizen-centric feature of SAMAVESH is ‘Samajik Sahayak’, an AI-powered chatbot that provides information on welfare schemes, eligibility criteria and services in 22 Indian languages through BHASHINI. The initiative seeks to overcome linguistic barriers and enable citizens to access Government information in languages they are comfortable with, thereby promoting digital inclusion and improving awareness of welfare schemes and services.

Integration with national digital platforms such as DigiLocker and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) further supports secure access to documents and improved visibility of service and payment-related information. The platform also incorporates a common design and content framework aligned with applicable Government standards, including Guidelines for Indian Government Websites (GIGW) 3.0, Digital Brand Identity Manual (DBIM) and accessibility guidelines, with emphasis on secure, accessible and user-friendly digital services.

In a significant step towards strengthening multilingual digital service delivery, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was exchanged between Shri Astik Kumar Pandey, Director MoSJE & CEO, BHASHINI Shri Amitabh Nag, on the occasion. The collaboration will facilitate the use of language technology to make information pertaining to the Department’s schemes and services accessible in multiple Indian languages. The initiative is expected to particularly benefit citizens facing linguistic barriers, enabling them to better understand scheme provisions and access welfare services more conveniently.

Shri Amresh Bahadur Pal, Director MoSJE, also exchanged an MoU with Shri Prashant Sinha, Chief Operating Officer, National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) to strengthen skill development and employment opportunities for beneficiaries under the Grant-in-Aid component of the Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY).

The partnership will facilitate access to skill development support and employment-oriented interventions, enabling beneficiaries to enhance their skills, improve employability and access better livelihood opportunities. The collaboration seeks to strengthen the link between welfare support, skill development and economic empowerment.

The newly launched e-Anudaan Portal (https://eanudaan.dosje.gov.in/) brings grant-in-aid processes under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), SMILE, Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) and SHRESHTA (Modes 1 and 2) onto a unified digital platform. The initiative seeks to promote Ease of Doing Business for Non-Governmental Organisations (NGOs), institutions and other implementing organisations through simplified application procedures, reduced documentation and automated document verification.

The portal provides a common Project ID, pre-filled information at different stages of application, application status dashboards and online notifications, thereby reducing repetitive data entry and enabling applicants to track their applications and pending actions more conveniently. Automated document checks and verification against relevant databases, including NGO Darpan and UDISE+, are intended to identify deficiencies at an early stage and minimise avoidable procedural delays.

The new e-Anudaan Portal also strengthens monitoring mechanisms through video-based e-Inspection, geo-tagged photographs and videos, and attendance records. Integration with PFMS enables tracking of fund disbursement and payments, thereby strengthening transparency and accountability in grant-in-aid management. These features are expected to improve the efficiency of grant administration for NGOs and institutions while supporting effective monitoring by the Department.

The development and implementation of SAMAVESH have been undertaken under the overall guidance and leadership of Ms. Mona K. Khandhar,  Additional Secretary, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment. Her guidance and continuous review have played an important role in facilitating coordination among the concerned Divisions and organisations and ensuring alignment of the initiative with the Department’s broader objectives of digital transformation and citizen-centric service delivery.

The IT Division of the Ministry has played a central coordinating role in the implementation of the initiative, working closely with concerned Divisions, organisations and technology partners, including the National e-Governance Division (NeGD) and the National Informatics Centre (NIC), for portal integration, migration, testing, content coordination, technical review and implementation of common digital standards.

The phased integration of scheme-related portals and organisational websites has facilitated the creation of a common digital gateway while supporting improved coordination and management of digital services across the Department.

Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment reiterates its commitment towards building an inclusive, accessible and citizen-centric digital governance ecosystem, ensuring that the benefits of technology-driven welfare delivery reach disadvantaged and marginalised sections of society.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Beyond the Final Frame: The Magic of IFFI Evenings
Goa's Evenings Come Alive with Open-Air Screenings, Cultural Performances and Creative Exchanges
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 6:47PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

As the sun sets over the Mandovi River and the streets of Panaji light up, the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) assumes a different rhythm. While the day is filled with film screenings, masterclasses, red-carpet appearances and conversations on cinema, the evenings bring their own charm. At IFFI, the setting sun does not signal the end of the festival day; it marks the beginning of another celebration.

Moving beyond the conventional confines of cinema halls, IFFI 2026 brings the cinematic experience closer to the public through open-air screenings at Miramar beach, Ravindra Bhavan in Margao and the helipad area at Vagator beach. Scheduled between 7 PM and 10 PM, these screenings feature a curated selection of films. Under the open skies of Goa, residents, visitors and cinema enthusiasts can come together to experience the joy of watching films, reflecting the festival’s commitment to making cinema more accessible and inclusive.

The festive atmosphere extends to the Mandovi promenade, where cultural performances of Romtamel bring Goa’s rich artistic traditions to the forefront. Scheduled across four evenings on November 23rd to 27th, the performances by seven cultural groups add a distinct local flavour to the international gathering. The coming together of indigenous cultural expressions and global cinematic traditions reflects the unique identity that Goa brings to IFFI.

Adding to the festivities, the IFFI Parade on 25th November, themed ‘Celebrating the Joy of Cinema’, proceeds from the Entertainment Society of Goa (ESG) premises to Kala Academy in Panaji, featuring colourful floats, cultural performances and community participation. The parade extends the festival beyond its designated venues, enabling local residents and visitors to become part of the cinematic celebration.

For filmmakers, delegates and aspiring artists, however, the festival evenings offer more than entertainment. Beyond the scheduled screenings and formal interactions, they provide opportunities for informal conversations, creative exchanges and meaningful connections. A discussion about a film can lead to an exchange of cultural perspectives, while a chance encounter between filmmakers can lay the foundation for a future collaboration.

Behind the illuminated festival venues also lies the sustained effort of volunteers, technical crews, media professionals and organizers who work beyond screening hours to ensure the smooth conduct of the festival. Their contributions form an integral, often unseen, part of the IFFI experience.

The transformation of Panaji after sunset is itself a spectacle. Canopies of golden fairy lights adorn the city’s tree-lined avenues, while illuminated buildings, colourful installations and IFFI’s iconic peacock motifs lend a festive character to the streets. The city’s architecture and public spaces become an extension of the festival, reflecting how Goa’s association with IFFI has evolved into a distinctive celebration where the character of the host state complements the universal appeal of cinema.

In keeping with the theme of IFFI 2026, ‘Stories Without Borders’, the festival nights embody cinema’s ability to transcend not only geographical and linguistic boundaries but also the physical boundaries of the auditorium. They remind audiences that the magic of a film festival lies as much in the conversations it inspires and the connections it creates as in the stories unfolding on screen.

At IFFI, the credits may roll, the curtains may close and the lights inside the theatres may fade, but the celebration of cinema continues. In Goa, the festival clock simply refuses to stop.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs
Constitution Day, 2026 to be observed on 26th November
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

The Constitution Day (Samvidhan Diwas) will be observed on 26th November, 2026, to commemorate the adoption of the Constitution of India by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November, 1949. The day has been observed as Constitution Day since 2015, under kind guidance of the Prime Minister of India.

As part of the celebrations, Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs is facilitating an online reading of the Preamble to the Constitution through the MyGov portal in 23 languages, comprising 22 Scheduled Languages and English. This initiative will provide an opportunity to citizens across the country to read the Preamble and reaffirm their commitment to the ideals and values enshrined in the Constitution.

Members of the public, Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, State/UT Governments, educational institutions, schools, colleges, universities and other organisations are encouraged to participate in the initiative through the following platform:

MyGov: https://pledge.mygov.in/constitution-day-2026/ , read the Preamble, get a certificate and share it on social media.

Constitution Quiz through the MyGov and MyBharat portals from 18th to 26th November, 2026 and Viksit Bharat Yuva Samvad is being organised across 786 districts in all 36 States/Union Territories from 24th to 26th November, 2026, to encourage participation and engagement of youth.

Various activities are being organised across the country by Ministries/Departments of the Government of India, State/UT Governments and their respective field formations, attached and subordinate offices, autonomous bodies and institutions to mark the occasion. These activities include collective reading of the Preamble, seminars, webinars, quizzes, essay and debate competitions, poster-making, cultural programmes, awareness campaigns, walks, runs and other community engagement activities.

Educational institutions are also being encouraged to organise special morning assemblies, discussions and competitions to familiarise students with the making of the Constitution, its salient features.

Special emphasis is being laid on extending the celebrations to the grassroots level through active participation of citizens, young people and students. Various awareness and outreach activities are also being undertaken through digital platforms and community-based initiatives to promote understanding of the Constitution and its significance in the country's democratic framework.

Constitution Day provides an occasion to reflect upon the principles and values enshrined in the Constitution of India and to renew our collective commitment to its ideals. The observance seeks to strengthen constitutional awareness, promote responsible citizenship and encourage active participation in upholding the democratic values of the nation.

Citizens, particularly young people and  students are encouraged to participate enthusiastically in the Constitution Day activities and join in reaffirming their commitment to the Constitution of India.

***

They become part of our childhood, accompany us through life’s milestones and remain with us long after a…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
When Words Fall Short, Music Speaks: Singer K.S. Chithra Remembers the Voices of Lata Mangeshkar, Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki at the 57th IFFI
The Celebrated Singer Revisits the Voices and Songs that Shaped Generations and Her own Musical Journey through Cherished Memories and Heartfelt Anecdotes
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 6:22PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

Some voices do more than fill a room with music. They become part of our childhood, accompany us through life’s milestones and remain with us long after a song has ended. For celebrated singer K. S. Chithra, the voices of Asha Bhosle, S. Janaki and Lata Mangeshkar have been just that. At a masterclass titled “Lata Mangeshkar Talk: The Voice That Echoes Forever in the Memory of Asha Bhosle and S. Janaki” at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), Chithra took the audience on a deeply personal journey through the music and memories of the legendary singers, moderated by actor and filmmaker Suhasini Maniratnam.

The conversation began on a note of warmth and familiarity, with Chithra admitting that she was a little tense but confident that Suhasini would put her at ease. Their shared history soon found its way into the conversation, as Suhasini recalled how songs from films in which Chithra had lent her voice had become an integral part of her own journey. What followed was less a formal discussion and more a meeting of memories, with anecdotes often giving way to melodies.

Looking back at her beginnings, Chithra spoke of growing up in a family with a strong musical environment, participating in competitions and learning classical music. Singing, she said, was the one thing she knew she could do well, although she had never imagined it would take her so far. Her entry into film music seemed almost accidental. She recalled singing film songs at recreational clubs, often beginning with songs made popular by P. Susheela.

Asked about the voices she admired most, Chithra named P. Susheela, S. Janaki and Lata Mangeshkar. She even used to imitate Janaki in her childhood days, laughing as she admitted that the singer’s distinctive style was impossible to reproduce. Speaking of Lata Mangeshkar, Chithra reflected on the emotional depth of her singing, particularly her devotional songs, and shared one of her favourite Lata Mangeshkar melodies with the audience.

Her memories of Asha Bhosle revealed a different kind of admiration. Chithra spoke of Asha Bhosle’s extraordinary versatility and willingness to experiment across musical forms, including ghazals, one of which she herself hummed during the session. She recalled that Asha had always wanted to carve out her own musical identity rather than be compared with her sister Lata Mangeshkar. Chithra also shared a memorable first meeting, when Asha Bhosle asked her why she was singing in such a high range. It was a small exchange that offered a glimpse into the frankness and individuality of the legendary singer.

The memories of S. Janaki, however, carried a particularly affectionate note. Chithra recalled the early days of S. Janaki’s musical journey, when mimicry artists performed on stage and Janaki was often invited to sing in between their performances to fill the gaps. These opportunities gave audiences a chance to hear her voice, eventually leading her towards a career in playback singing. She also spoke of Janaki’s distinctive voice, expressive range and ability to bring life to every song. Beyond the music, Chithra remembered her as a mother figure. Recalling visits to Janaki’s home, she spoke fondly of how the veteran singer would lovingly feed her by hand, adding that even spicy food tasted sweet when it came from her.

Throughout the session, Suhasini brought songs into the conversation, connecting memories with the emotions they had carried on screen. She reflected on how film music accompanies people through love, weddings, grief and happiness, often expressing what words cannot. Chithra, in turn, revealed that the Malayalam song ‘Swarnamukile’ was one that could still bring her to tears.

A playful musical quiz added another dimension to the afternoon. Presented with film scenes without their background scores, Chithra identified and sang the songs from all five sequences, including songs from Suhasini’s films. The session also touched upon the demands of recording, difficult songs and the importance of recognising one’s vocal limitations with age.

The conversation reached its most memorable moment as Chithra began singing ‘Paadariyen’ from Sindhu Bhairavi. Suhasini joined her, lip-syncing to the song, as the two shared a moment that brought their conversation full circle. It was a beautiful meeting of music and memory, a reminder that songs are never just melodies, but pieces of lives, friendships and journeys that continue to resonate across generations.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Women and Child Development
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Smt. Annapurna Devi Launch Nayi Chetna 5.0
15 Ministries/Departments Join Hands for Women’s Safety, Gender Equality and Empowerment
Landmark MoU Signed to Make Villages Violence-Free
Month-Long Nationwide Campaign to Be Conducted Across All States and UTs from 25 November to 23 December 2026
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 6:16PM by PIB Delhi

Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, Union Minister for Rural Development and Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare, and Smt. Annapurna Devi, Union Minister for Women and Child Development, today launched the fifth edition of “Nayi Chetna: Pahal Badlaav Ki”, the National Campaign on Gender Equality and Women’s Empowerment, at NASC Complex, PUSA, New Delhi. Shri Rohit Kansal, Secretary, Department of Rural Development; Shri Anil Malik, Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development; and Shri Niraj Verma, Secretary, Department of Justice, were present, along with senior officials of participating Ministries, State Governments, development partners and women leaders from across the country.

The centrepiece of the event was a landmark Quadripartite MoU on the Violence-Free Village Initiative (VFVI), signed by the Department of Rural Development, the Ministry of Women and Child Development, the Department of Justice and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The MoU links DAY-NRLM’s Gender Resource Centres with One Stop Centres, Women Helpline 181, Disha 2.0 and legal aid services into a single chain of support, from prevention and protection to legal assistance and rehabilitation. To be piloted in 9 States and Union Territories, it rests on a simple promise: no woman facing violence should be left to find her way to help alone.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan affirmed that women’s empowerment, dignity and respect lie at the heart of the vision of Viksit Bharat, and lauded the contribution of nearly 3.75 crore Lakhpati Didis to the rural economy. Asserting that economic independence must go hand in hand with dignity, safety and equal opportunity, he called for collective effort to challenge patriarchal mindsets. Describing the MoU as a framework that brings safety, justice, rehabilitation and livelihood support together, he urged States, SHGs, Anganwadi networks and communities to turn the campaign into sustained grassroots action and to integrate the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan towards drug-free and violence-free villages.

Smt. Annapurna Devi highlighted the role of community institutions in taking the campaign to every household. Calling for wider use of support services, she urged citizens to remember, save and share Women Helpline 181 and Emergency Response Number 112, so that no woman in distress goes without timely help.

Shri Rohit Kansal traced Nayi Chetna’s journey from an awareness campaign to a nationwide, community-led movement, with 5.3 crore participants and nearly 7,000 Gender Resource Centres established so far. The fifth edition, he said, will turn that awareness and community trust into effective support, legal assistance and timely access to justice.

Shri Anil Malik called for seamless convergence of helplines, legal services and support institutions, backed by timely response and consistent follow-up. Highlighting the 16-day action agenda, he underlined the collective responsibility of families, communities and institutions towards women’s safety.

Shri Niraj Verma stressed the need to turn existing legal safeguards into services women can actually reach, particularly in rural and remote areas. He highlighted the role of NALSA, Tele-Law, Nyaya Bandhu, paralegal volunteers and Gender Resource Centres in strengthening legal awareness, referrals and free legal aid.

An Inter-Ministerial Joint Advisory was also unveiled, extending the Whole-of-Government approach to address gender-based discrimination and violence and advance women’s economic empowerment. The collaborating Ministries/Departments are: Rural Development, Women and Child Development; School Education and Literacy; Home Affairs; Panchayati Raj; Agriculture and Farmers Welfare; Social Justice and Empowerment; Youth Affairs and Sports; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises; Information and Broadcasting; Justice; Labour and Employment; Revenue; and Road Transport and Highways.

Led by DAY-NRLM, the campaign will run across all States and Union Territories until 23 December 2026, built around four themes: Identity, Assetization, Mobility, and Redistribution of Unpaid Care Work. Through Self-Help Groups and community institutions, it will reach rural India with awareness drives, rallies, community meetings, street plays and dialogues with men and youth.

The event also saw the release of the Nayi Chetna 4.0 Assessment Report and the Nayi Chetna Anthem, and Gender Champions and One Stop Centre administrators shared experiences from the field. SHG women, Anganwadi workers, State Rural Livelihoods Missions and civil society partners took part in large numbers, reaffirming Nayi Chetna as a true Jan Andolan for gender equality.

 

***

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE NATIONAL SCIENTIFIC CONVENTION ON HOMOEOPATHY AT BHUBANESWAR
OUR INSTITUTIONS, RESEARCHERS, TEACHERS AND HEALTHCARE PROFESSIONALS MUST CONTRIBUTE TOWARDS BUILDING AN ACCESSIBLE, EQUITABLE, SCIENTIFICALLY RESPONSIBLE AND RESPONSIVE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy at Bhubaneswar, Odisha today (November 25, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that homoeopathy represents an important part of India's diverse healthcare landscape. Over the years, it has developed a wide institutional presence in India and has become accessible to people through educational institutions, healthcare facilities and public health networks.

The President underlined that the future credibility and academic standing of homoeopathy will depend significantly on the scientific integrity of its research and the quality of clinical evidence it generates. She urged research institutions, medical colleges, universities and professional organisations to collaborate in developing a strong research culture. She stated that the National Scientific Convention on Homoeopathy provides an excellent platform for meaningful academic engagement, institutional partnerships and a shared vision for the future. She advised participants, particularly young researchers and professionals, to make full use of this opportunity.

The President said that the development of homoeopathy should be accompanied by an unwavering commitment to scientific inquiry, academic excellence and professional accountability. Research should be guided by sound methodology, adequately designed clinical studies, systematic documentation and transparent reporting. She emphasised on the need to encourage multicentric studies, systematic reviews, evidence synthesis, pharmacological and fundamental research and the development of reliable clinical databases. She said that intellectual honesty to acknowledge research limitations, report unfavourable findings and allow scientific evidence to guide conclusions is equally important.

The President said that the medical profession demands much more than academic qualifications. It requires intellectual discipline, scientific temper, integrity, empathy and a commitment to lifelong learning. She urged the young practitioners of homoeopathy to cultivate the habit of questioning and never stop learning. She said that they should have the courage to investigate, the patience to seek evidence and the humility to accept new knowledge. They should never forget that behind every patient is a human being with hopes, fears and dignity.

The President said that as India advances towards the national goal of Viksit Bharat 2047, healthcare and education will remain two of its most important pillars. Our institutions, researchers, teachers and healthcare professionals must contribute towards building an accessible, equitable, scientifically responsible and responsive healthcare system. She expressed confidence that this National Convention will encourage scientific dialogue, promote institutional partnerships and inspire a new generation of competent, ethical and socially responsible healthcare professionals.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, efforts are being made to move sanitation work towards mechanisation, safety, formalisation and improved…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
From Informal Work To Dignified Employment
NAMASTE Scheme Facilitates Formal Employment And Stability For A Sewer And Septic Tank Worker Raja of Manipur
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi

Mr Raja’s (name changed) journey highlights the importance of identifying and formally profiling sanitation workers and facilitating opportunities that promote dignified employment.

Through the NAMASTE Scheme, efforts are being made to move sanitation work towards mechanisation, safety, formalisation and improved livelihood opportunities for workers.

For many workers engaged in sewer and septic tank cleaning, informal employment arrangements often mean uncertain income, hazardous working conditions and limited access to occupational safety or formal recognition.

For Raja, a 27-year-old graduate from Manipur, securing dignified and stable employment marked an important step towards greater financial security and professional recognition.

Despite completing his graduation, Raja had been working in informal sewer and septic tank cleaning under contractor-based arrangements. His work was characterised by irregular earnings, limited occupational safety measures and the absence of formal employment benefits. With his household dependent on uncertain income, the lack of employment stability posed continuing challenges.

The National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme seeks to formalise and improve the working conditions of Sewer and Septic Tank Workers (SSWs) by facilitating their identification, profiling and access to support and opportunities.

Through formal profiling under the NAMASTE Scheme, Raja was recognised as a Sewer and Septic Tank Worker, helping facilitate an opportunity for institutional employment.

On October 15, 2025, Raja was engaged as a Skilled Daily Wage Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) Operator at the High Court of Manipur. The employment opportunity provided him with a more predictable source of income and improved recognition of his work and skills.

He now earns ₹480 per day, amounting to approximately ₹14,400 per month. The transition from irregular contractor-based work to a formal institutional engagement has brought greater income predictability and improved employment conditions, helping him work towards long-term financial stability.

His experience reflects how formal recognition and employment opportunities can help sanitation workers move beyond informal arrangements towards greater stability, dignity and professional security.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
INDIA–NEPAL JOINT MILITARY EXERCISE ‘SURYAKIRAN XX’ COMMENCES IN NEPAL
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 4:21PM by PIB Delhi

The 20th edition of the India–Nepal Joint Military Exercise SURYAKIRAN commenced today at the Nepal Army Battle School, Saljhandi, Nepal. The exercise is scheduled to be conducted from 25 November to 08 December 2026. The Opening Ceremony was graced by Major General Purna Bahadur Khatri, General Officer Commanding, Mid Western Division, Nepal Army. The Indian Army contingent, comprising 334 personnel, is being represented by troops from the KUMAON Regiment. The Nepal Army contingent, comprising an equal number of personnel, is being represented by troops from Shri Jawla Dal Battalion.

The aim of the exercise is to enhance interoperability, operational coordination and mutual understanding between the two Armies through joint training in counter-insurgency and counter-terrorism operations in challenging terrain.

The scope of the exercise includes joint tactical operations, heliborne operations, disaster response and medical training. Troops from both Armies will exchange operational experiences and best practices while refining tactics, techniques and procedures to enhance joint operational effectiveness.

Exercise SURYAKIRAN is an annual bilateral military exercise conducted alternately in India and Nepal. The exercise will further strengthen bilateral defence cooperation, foster mutual trust and camaraderie between the two Armies and reaffirm the shared commitment of both nations towards regional peace, stability and security.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
Operation Drishti: AFMS doctors perform record 412 sight-restoring surgeries during surgical eye camp at Military Hospital, Meerut
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:51PM by PIB Delhi

A total of 412 sight-restoring surgeries have been conducted free of cost by an expert team of doctors of Armed Forces Medical Services (AFMS) during a surgical eye camp at Military Hospital, Meerut under Operation Drishti. The five-day camp, which concluded on November 25, 2026, brought a new lease of light to people across the region, including 197 underprivileged civilians, who underwent surgeries for cataract, glaucoma, vitreo-retinal and pterygium. The special highlight was the successful surgeries of approximately 60 mature cataract patients who were completely blind.

Over the past two months, more than 12,000 patients were screened by ophthalmologists and medical officers of AFMS for cataract and other eye ailments at Bagpat, Bulandshahar, Hapur, Shamli and Moradabad, ensuring that even residents of distant towns and villages were reached. Close to 5,000 patients were screened during the camp at Military Hospital, Meerut. Patients found in need of surgery were brought to the Military Hospital where 412 surgeries were performed between 22nd & 24th November 2026.

The closing ceremony of the camp was graced by Minister of State, Sainik Kalyan Vikas Nigam and PRD, Uttar Pradesh Dr Somendra Tomar as the Chief Guest. He interacted with patients and members of the medical team, appreciating the efforts of the Indian Army towards extending a helping hand to civilians on a large scale.

Speaking on the occasion, DGAFMS Air Marshal Sandeep Thareja commended the medical team for its outstanding contribution and setting a new benchmark in professional excellence, dedicated service and compassionate patient care. AFMS is focusing not only on veterans and the dependents of serving personnel; but also the civilian population who do not have access to such facilities, he said.

412 surgeries are the highest-ever in any previous eye camp, setting a new benchmark in delivering quality healthcare and compassionate service. The surgeries were performed by an expert team of doctors from Army Hospital (Research & Referral), led by Head of Department (Ophthalmology) Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, who is spearheading Operation Drishti, the series of mega surgical eye camps that carries advanced eye care to remote and underserved regions of the country. The camp was organised under the aegis of HQ Surya Command.

***

The 164-minute Telugu-language feature is among the five films selected for the Mainstream Cinema section of Indian…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Making Audiences Laugh Is a Serious Creative Exercise: Anil Ravipudi at IFFI 2026
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:47PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 25 November 2026

 

“Making audiences laugh is a demanding creative exercise”, said National Film Award-winning filmmaker Shri Anil Ravipudi at a press conference on his film Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu during the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. The 164-minute Telugu-language feature is among the five films selected for the Mainstream Cinema section of Indian Panorama at IFFI 2026. The director was joined by producers Shri Sahu Garapati and Ms. K. Sushmita and actor Ms. Catherine Tresa.

“Comedy is always a serious business,” remarked Shri Ravipudi, explaining the challenges of writing humour while balancing family emotions and the expectations associated with a superstar like Chiranjeevi. He observed that it is difficult to predict which jokes will resonate with audiences. Crediting his writing team for its support, the director said his endeavour has been to craft stories that appeal to audiences across age groups.

Written and directed by Shri Ravipudi, Mana Shankara Vara Prasad Garu follows a national security officer whose devotion to his profession leaves him estranged from his wife and children. Six years later, he seeks to reconnect with them by taking up a position at their school. Blending humour and action with family emotions, the film explores the tension between professional duty and personal relationships, and the possibility of reconciliation.

Reflecting on his experience of directing Chiranjeevi, Shri Ravipudi recalled growing up watching the veteran actor’s films. His familiarity with the actor’s diverse roles over the years helped him develop a simple family narrative that showcased Chiranjeevi’s distinctive strengths.

Speaking about his association with the films being released around Sankranti, the director said the festive season naturally lends itself to family entertainers, as families come together and visit theatres. He observed that cinema offers audiences much-needed relief from the stresses of everyday life, adding that the joy of bringing smiles to their faces was a major motivation for him to continue making such films.

Ms. Catherine Tresa, who plays an important character in the film, described working alongside the veteran actor as a valuable learning experience. Speaking about her transition from serious roles to lighter ones, she emphasised the importance of versatility and understanding the director’s vision. She also expressed happiness at the film’s selection for IFFI, having wanted to connect with a wider audience through a commercial entertainer.

Welcoming the recognition of mainstream cinema at film festivals, Shri Ravipudi appreciated the jury’s efforts to accommodate different kinds of films. He observed that festivals could celebrate artistic and technical excellence while also recognising commercially successful films that connect with large audiences.

The film’s presentation at IFFI highlights the place of popular cinema alongside diverse cinematic traditions, celebrating stories that bring families together through humour, emotion and shared experiences.

The session was moderated by Swati Aggarwal.

The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs. 1,491 crore
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Department of Posts for the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme, the Estates Management Scheme, during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year period.

Strategic Objective:

The scheme aims to comprehensively transform and modernize the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts. It focuses heavily on the construction, re-construction, renovation, uniform branding of post offices and residential colonies, along with the preservation of India’s heritage postal buildings. This modernization strategy directly supports first-mile delivery, fosters financial inclusion and enhances citizen centric service delivery nationwide, aligning with the broader visions of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

As one of the world's largest postal networks with 1.65 lakh post offices (including 1,49,385 in rural areas), India Post remains a critical vehicle for mails, banking (POSB/IPPB), insurance (PLI), Aadhaar services, Post Office Passport Seva Kendras and rural artisan support via Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs).

Implementation Timeline:

The scheme is scheduled for phased implementation over a five-year horizon, starting from FY 2026-27 through FY 2030-31.

Key Components of the Approved Scheme:

  • New Construction (Rs. 280 Crore): Building 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant departmental plots to replace currently rented spaces and eliminate rental liabilities.
  • Re-construction (Rs. 108 Crore): Demolishing and rebuilding 50 dilapidated departmental postal structures to ensure long-term structural safety.
  • Renovation & Branding (Rs. 318 Crore): Upgrading and establishing uniform branding across 2,550 departmental SubPost Offices as per SPA guidelines.
  • Rented Post Office Upgrades (Rs. 37.50 Crore): Upgrading and uniformly branding 2,500 post offices operating out of rented premises.
  • Heritage Preservation (Rs. 180 Crore): Restoring and preserving 20 landmark heritage postal buildings to safeguard the historical legacy of the department.
  • Colony Renovation (Rs. 357.50 Crore): Revamping 150 high demand postal residential colonies to elevate employee welfare and satisfaction.
  • Allied & Inclusive Activities (Rs. 100 Crore): Implementing sustainable features (Solar power, Rainwater Harvesting) and universal accessibility infrastructure (ramps, Braille signage) under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, alongwith gender-focused additions like ladies toilets and feeding rooms.
  • Integrated Technology Center (Rs. 100 Crore): Setting up a permanent physical infrastructure for the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) in Bengaluru to drive Advanced Postal Technology (APT) services and support the indigenous Opensource Tech Stack.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
Cabinet approves continuation of Postal Operations Scheme with an outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore for 16th Finance Commission Cycle (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31)
The scheme aims to modernize postal network, strengthen parcel and mail operations, enhance rural connectivity and improve citizen-centric services
Focus on e-commerce logistics, financial inclusion, international mail operations and digital transformation of India Post services
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:41PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme “Postal Operations” during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with a proposed outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore. The scheme seeks to strengthen postal infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and support the growing requirements of logistics, e-commerce and digital service delivery across the country. 

With one of the world’s largest postal networks comprising 1.65 lakh post offices, including 1,49,655 post offices in rural areas, India Post continues to serve as an important platform for delivery of mail, parcels, banking, insurance and other citizen-centric services, particularly in remote and underserved regions. 

Apart from its core postal operations, India Post provides a wide range of public services through initiatives such as Post Office Savings Bank (POSB), India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), Postal Life Insurance (PLI), Aadhaar enrolment and updation, Passport Services through Post Office Passport Seva Kendras, KYC verification services and support to rural artisans through Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). 

The scheme would support modernization of postal infrastructure, strengthen last-mile delivery, improve logistics efficiency, promote financial inclusion and enhance customer-centric service delivery across the country. The proposal also aligns with the broader objectives of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. 

The scheme is intended to be implemented over a period of five years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. 

The Postal Operations Scheme comprises the following six sub-schemes: 

  1. Rural Business and Access to Postal Network – Rs. 120 crore – Focused on infrastructure upgrades, standardized branding and better resource utilization to transform post offices, particularly in rural areas, into efficient and citizen-centric service hubs. The component aims to strengthen financial inclusion, digital connectivity and local economic development while improving last-mile delivery and enhancing access to postal and citizen-centric services in underserved regions. 
  2. Mail Network Optimization – Rs. 575 crore – Envisages modernization of mail operations through centralized delivery systems, mechanization, advanced IT solutions under Advanced Postal Technology (APT 2.0), GIS-based services and upgraded infrastructure. The initiative also includes strengthening delivery post offices, mail handling systems, Mail Motor Service (MMS) workshops, Road Transport Network and modern smart 24x7 letter boxes to improve operational efficiency, transparency, service quality and logistical reliability across the network. 
  3. Parcel Network Optimization – Rs. 278 crore – Includes construction of Parcel Hubs and expansion of Parcel Packaging Units (PPUs) aligned with the redesigned sorting framework to streamline parcel movement, reduce handling points, ease capacity constraints and improve transit times. The component also aims to support growing parcel volumes from e-commerce and rural markets through purpose-built facilities, standardized secure packaging and enhanced operational flexibility while improving customer trust and strengthening India Post’s competitiveness in the logistics sector.  
  4. Infrastructure Upgrade and Augmentation of Infrastructure for International Mails – Rs. 8 crore – Aims to strengthen international mail services by upgrading Foreign Post Offices (FPOs) and Sub Foreign Post Offices (SFPOs) to improve infrastructure and expedite processing of international consignments. The initiative also includes marketing and Advertisement through Postal / RMS Division and position India Post as a reliable international logistics provider while improving compliance, technology integration and export logistics support.  
  5. Marketing Functions including Quality of Service – Rs. 100 crore – Focused on promotion, branding, outreach and customer engagement through multi-channel campaigns across television, digital, radio, print and outdoor platforms. The component also includes participation in events and exhibitions, social media campaigns, direct marketing and expansion of Dak Chaupal activities to deepen grassroots engagement, especially in rural and underserved areas. In addition, it envisages infrastructure upgrades, studio facilities, ICT enhancements, market research, influencer engagement and third-party evaluation mechanisms to improve quality of service and strengthen a customer-centric approach.  
  6. Philately Operations – Rs. 60 crore – Proposes initiatives to promote philately through exhibitions, seminars, quizzes, school philatelic clubs and innovative stamp designs including scented, holographic and 3D stamps. The component also includes digital outreach activities, programmes such as the Dhai Akhar letter-writing competition and SPARSH scholarship, modernization of production and fulfillment centres, market research and international collaboration with the objective of revitalizing philately as an engaging educational and cultural activity while also improving operational efficiency and revenue potential.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Civil Aviation
Cabinet approves development of Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam at an estimated cost of 2,014 crore
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi

To overcome the severe operational and spatial constraints of the existing defense landlocked civil enclave at Silchar Airport and to accommodate sustained passenger growth, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the  development of a New Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at an estimated cost of Rs.2,014 crore.

Doloo, situated in the Cachar District of Assam, serves as the strategic heart of the Barak Valley—a region renowned for its extensive tea gardens, agro-based industries, and immense potential for eco and cultural tourism.

The proposed Terminal Building will span a total area of 12,351 sqm with a capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hour, designed with modern passenger amenities, sustainable green building principles, and modular expansion capability. In addition, the project encompasses the development of a 2,705m x 45m, Code-4C compliant runway suitable for A-320 aircraft operations, along with the construction of a new Apron capable of parking 6 nos. A-320 aircraft and a dedicated isolation bay.

As a project of immense strategic significance, the Doloo Greenfield Airport will meet the rapidly growing demands of air traffic in South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring States. It will significantly decongest existing infrastructure, unlock regional economic potential by boosting trade and tourism, and offer a world-class gateway integrating Northeast India with broader national and international growth corridors.
