item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
Cabinet approves development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) Basis
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposed project for development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL) under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis, at an estimated project cost of Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST. The project envisages the development of a 900-metre-long container terminal with a design draft of 18 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs), to be implemented in two phases.

Expenditure involved:

The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The investment is to be arranged by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. The project proposal separately indicates an estimated dredging cost of Rs.450 crore to be borne by KPL.

Details:

(i)    The project envisages development of a 900-metre-long Second Container Terminal with a berth width of 30 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million TEUs. The terminal will be developed in two phases: Phase I with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs and Phase II with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs.

(ii)   The terminal is designed to handle large container vessels, including vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length overall, with a design draft of 18 metres. This will strengthen KPL’s ability to handle larger mainline vessels and improve connectivity with international shipping routes.

(iii)  The project is intended to meet the growing demand for containerised export-import (EXIM) cargo from the Chennai–Ennore industrial and economic region and the wider southern hinterland. Key cargo-generating sectors include automobiles and auto components, engineering goods, electronics, chemicals and other manufactured products.

(iv)  KPL handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26, including more than 7 lakh TEUs of container traffic. The existing container terminal has an installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs per annum and handled approximately 0.7 million TEUs in FY 2025–26, representing utilisation of about 88%.

(v)   Container traffic in India has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 7% over the last five years, while KPL’s container traffic has grown at approximately 9.9% during the same period. The feasibility study projects continued growth in container traffic in the south-eastern region, supporting the need to augment capacity at KPL.

(vi)  The project will be implemented on a DBFOT basis for a concession period of 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months. Phase I is scheduled for completion within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, with commercial operations commencing in the 25th month. Construction of Phase II will be undertaken from the 25th to the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month.

(vii) The estimated project cost is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The cost is to be financed by the selected concessionaire through the DBFOT framework. In addition, KPL is to incur an estimated Rs.450 crore towards dredging, as indicated in the project proposal.

(viii) The project is proposed to be implemented through a transparent, open global bidding process. The concessionaire will arrange the required financing and recover its investment through user charges in accordance with the provisions of the Concession Agreement and applicable tariff framework.

(ix)  The project is aligned with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. It is expected to strengthen KPL’s position as a container gateway on India’s East Coast, improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics chain and support the growth of EXIM trade.

Implementation Strategy and Targets:

The project will be implemented by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. Phase I, with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs, is to be completed within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, and commercial operations are to commence in the 25th month. Phase II, with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs, is to be completed by the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month. The project proposal also provides for obtaining environmental and other necessary clearances in a time-bound manner before the bid due date.

Major Impact:

(i)  The additional capacity of 2.0 million TEUs per annum will strengthen KPL’s ability to accommodate growing container traffic and provide an additional gateway for EXIM cargo from the industrial clusters of Tamil Nadu and the adjoining hinterland.

(ii) The terminal’s design draft of 18 metres and capability to handle large container vessels are expected to improve international connectivity, facilitate direct calls by mainline vessels and reduce dependence on foreign deep-water hub ports and associated feedering costs.

(iii) The project is expected to improve maritime logistics efficiency, support trade and manufacturing, strengthen the port’s revenue potential and contribute to India’s maritime competitiveness.

(iv)     The project is expected to generate employment for approximately 750 persons directly and indirectly during construction and to increase about 800 persons during the operational phase.

(v) The project supports the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by augmenting domestic port capacity and improving logistics support for industries and original equipment manufacturers in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and the adjoining hinterland.

(vi)     There will be no financial implication for the Government of India, as the investment in the PPP component will be arranged by the selected concessionaire.

Background:

(i)  Kamarajar Port Limited, formerly known as Ennore Port Limited, one of the 12 Major Ports of India and is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Located on the east coast of Tamil Nadu near the Chennai industrial and economic region, the port handles a range of cargo, including coal, petroleum, oil and lubricants, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo.

(ii) During FY 2025–26, KPL recorded revenue of approximately Rs.1,280 crore and Profit Before Tax of Rs.924 crore. The port has recorded cargo growth at a CAGR of 13.64% over the last five years, reflecting the expansion of economic activity and trade in its hinterland.

(iii) The Chennai–Ennore region is a major industrial and manufacturing cluster of India. As trade and containerisation expand, additional container-handling capacity and efficient facilities for larger vessels are required to support the movement of EXIM cargo from Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra Pradesh and the wider southern hinterland.

item.content:encoded:
Vice President's Secretariat
Vice-President Inaugurates Swayamsiddha National Conference 2026 on Women’s Empowerment in Nagpur
Respect for Women and Their Leadership Is Deeply Rooted in Indian Civilisation: Vice-President 
Women’s Empowerment Is a Shared Responsibility of Government, Universities and Society: Vice-President
Women’s Empowerment Must Move from Education to Leadership: Vice-President
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the Swayamsiddha National Conference 2026 on Women’s Empowerment, themed “VIJAYA – A Journey of Empowerment through Education”, organised by the Swayamsiddha Centre of Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University in Nagpur, Maharashtra.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today graced the inaugural session of the first National Conference under Swayamsiddha – “VIJAYA: A Journey of Empowerment through Education” at Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University, Nagpur, Maharashtra. Highlighting the transformative role of education in women’s empowerment, he emphasised the need to equip women with skills, confidence and opportunities to achieve economic independence and leadership.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 25, 2026


Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President recalled initiating the Swayamsiddha programme during his tenure as Governor of Maharashtra and appreciated its continued expansion under the leadership of the present Governor, Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, with universities across Maharashtra participating in its activities. He emphasised that universities must go beyond imparting academic qualifications and actively contribute to women’s empowerment by promoting skills, economic independence, confidence and leadership.

Highlighting the growing participation of women in higher education, the Vice-President observed that, at convocations across the country, women students increasingly outnumber men among gold medallists. Referring to the All India Survey on Higher Education, he noted that the female Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education had increased significantly over the last decade. He said this progress reflected the expanding opportunities for women and the country’s transition from women’s development to women-led development.

Referring to the forthcoming Constitution Day, the Vice-President recalled the contributions of 15 women members of the Constituent Assembly to the framing of the Constitution of India. He also highlighted the significance of the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam in advancing women’s representation in democratic institutions.

Emphasising India’s cultural ethos, the Vice-President said that respect for women and their leadership is deeply rooted in Indian civilisation. He called upon educational institutions to prepare young women for leadership roles across all spheres of life. He stressed that education must open pathways for women to participate in research, entrepreneurship, administration, public life and institutional decision-making, with particular attention to those from rural, remote and economically disadvantaged backgrounds.

The Vice-President emphasised that women’s empowerment was a shared responsibility of governments, universities, industry, civil society and families. He expressed hope that the proposed Maharashtra–VIJAYA Framework for Women in Higher Education would provide a basis for sustained institutional action.

Congratulating the University for bringing Swayamsiddha to the national platform, the Vice-President expressed hope that the VIJAYA conference would facilitate meaningful discussions, innovative solutions and practical recommendations. He said that the success of Swayamsiddha would ultimately be reflected in the confidence, independence and leadership of the women it reaches.

On the occasion, the Vice-President unveiled the Swayamsiddha logo and released two compendiums—Hundred Voices of Young Women and Best Practices in Higher Education. He also felicitated Swayamsiddha leaders in recognition of their contributions to the initiative and joined the participants in taking the ‘No to Drugs’ pledge.

Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today felicitated Swayamsiddha leaders at the inaugural session of the first National Conference under Swayamsiddha – ‘VIJAYA: A Journey of Empowerment through Education’ in Nagpur. The recognition celebrates their contributions and commitment to advancing women’s empowerment.

— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) November 25, 2026



The event was attended by Shri Jishnu Dev Varma, Governor of Maharashtra; Dr. Manali Kshirsagar, Vice-Chancellor, Rashtrasant Tukadoji Maharaj Nagpur University; Dr. Prashant Narnaware, IAS, Secretary to the Governor of Maharashtra; Dr. Akhilesh Peshwe, Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University; representatives of the National Commission for Women and Maharashtra State Commission for Women; academicians, faculty members, officers and students.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Heavy Industries
Cabinet approves Rs.11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem
The scheme aims to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment ecosystem in India, supporting the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:35PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the "Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem" with a financial outlay of Rs.11,000 crore. The Scheme, to be implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), aims to incentivize domestic manufacturing of CIE and its components and to establish a dedicated CIE testing facility in the country, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the Global CIE market.

India's CIE industry is currently the world's third largest, after China and the United States, with a market size of around Rs.97,500 crore in FY2024-25. Driven by accelerated growth in infrastructure (roads and ports) and housing, the industry is projected to increase more than double, reaching a market size of around Rs.2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30.

Driven by rapid growth in the construction and infrastructure sector, the scheme aims to incentivize manufacturing of technologically advanced equipment such as Ship-to-Shore Cranes, Tunnel Boring Machines, Hydraulic Excavators, Off-Highway Trucks, etc. The scheme has also provision of establishment of state of art dedicated CIE testing facility in the country.

The scheme with duration of eight years from FY2026-27, comprise of a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) for setting up manufacturing facilities, followed by a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33), and a final year (FY2033-34) for settlement of incentives on incremental sales of FY2032-33.

The scheme has two components:

  1. Sales-linked Incentive – Incentives will be provided on the Incremental Sales Value of eligible CIE equipment and components to approved applicants across two categories – eligible OEMs and Component Manufacturers. Graded Incentive rates range from 13% to 8% of incremental sales value over a five-year period.
  2. Grant for CIE Testing Facility – A grant of up to Rs.375 crore, in the nature of Viability Gap Funding, for setting up a dedicated CIE testing facility,

This initiative by the Government of India is a landmark step towards strengthening the domestic Construction and Infrastructure Equipment manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in the global markets. By fostering indigenous capabilities in manufacturing of CIE, the scheme will ensure supply chain security, increase opportunities for employment and promote Atmanirbhar Bharat. It embodies the Government’s unwavering commitment to build a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive and sustainable industrial base, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

item.content:encoded:
Cabinet
Cabinet approves continuation of Estates Management Scheme for Department of Posts with an outlay of Rs. 1,491 crore
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:32PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposal of the Department of Posts for the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme, the Estates Management Scheme, during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. The scheme carries a total financial outlay of Rs.1,491 crores over a five-year period.

Strategic Objective:

The scheme aims to comprehensively transform and modernize the estates infrastructure of the Department of Posts. It focuses heavily on the construction, re-construction, renovation, uniform branding of post offices and residential colonies, along with the preservation of India’s heritage postal buildings. This modernization strategy directly supports first-mile delivery, fosters financial inclusion and enhances citizen centric service delivery nationwide, aligning with the broader visions of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat.

As one of the world's largest postal networks with 1.65 lakh post offices (including 1,49,385 in rural areas), India Post remains a critical vehicle for mails, banking (POSB/IPPB), insurance (PLI), Aadhaar services, Post Office Passport Seva Kendras and rural artisan support via Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs).

Implementation Timeline:

The scheme is scheduled for phased implementation over a five-year horizon, starting from FY 2026-27 through FY 2030-31.

Key Components of the Approved Scheme:

  • New Construction (Rs. 280 Crore): Building 190 departmental postal buildings on vacant departmental plots to replace currently rented spaces and eliminate rental liabilities.
  • Re-construction (Rs. 108 Crore): Demolishing and rebuilding 50 dilapidated departmental postal structures to ensure long-term structural safety.
  • Renovation & Branding (Rs. 318 Crore): Upgrading and establishing uniform branding across 2,550 departmental SubPost Offices as per SPA guidelines.
  • Rented Post Office Upgrades (Rs. 37.50 Crore): Upgrading and uniformly branding 2,500 post offices operating out of rented premises.
  • Heritage Preservation (Rs. 180 Crore): Restoring and preserving 20 landmark heritage postal buildings to safeguard the historical legacy of the department.
  • Colony Renovation (Rs. 357.50 Crore): Revamping 150 high demand postal residential colonies to elevate employee welfare and satisfaction.
  • Allied & Inclusive Activities (Rs. 100 Crore): Implementing sustainable features (Solar power, Rainwater Harvesting) and universal accessibility infrastructure (ramps, Braille signage) under the Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan, alongwith gender-focused additions like ladies toilets and feeding rooms.
  • Integrated Technology Center (Rs. 100 Crore): Setting up a permanent physical infrastructure for the Centre for Excellence in Postal Technology (CEPT) in Bengaluru to drive Advanced Postal Technology (APT) services and support the indigenous Opensource Tech Stack.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Communications
TRAI releases findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Noida, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and nearby areas route under Delhi LSA, for the month of Sep 2026
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:31PM by PIB Delhi

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Noida, Ghaziabad, Greater Noida and nearby areas route under Delhi LSA, during the month of Sep 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.

These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analyzed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.

TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 813.4 Km, Hotspot locations - 08, Walk Test – 3.8 Km, Inter Operator Calling at 01 location during 01st Sep 2026 to 05th Sep 2026 in Delhi LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Delhi. The observations presented in drive test reports represent the performance of the TSPs on the area / route under test on the day / time of conducting the drive test.

Drive Test Route Map: The following map provides overview of drive test routes indicating City drive, Inter-operator calling, Hotspots & walk test as per the legends shown on the map: - 

Figure-1: Drive test routes

Key Parameters Assessed

a) Coverage Gap: Percentage of samples, for which signal strength observed less than the minimum prescribed signal strength for respective technology (2G/ 3G/ 4G/ 5G).

b) Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).

    c) Call Silence Instance: Number of call silence instances occurred during the calls.

    d) Data Services: Download / Upload Throughput, Latency, Jitter, Packet Drop Rate.

The overall mobile network performance across Ghaziabad, Noida and Greater Noida (Delhi LSA) for the key Parameters has been summarized below:

a)  Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1053/127346 for Airtel, 79985/121733 for BSNL/MTNL, 2146/127212 for RJIL & 1246/132094 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

b)  Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 9/1139 for Airtel, 173/1071 for BSNL/MTNL, 14/1146 for RJIL & 2/1158 for VIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 8/1086 for Airtel, 10/878 for BSNL/MTNL, 54/1086 for RJIL & 4/1107 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

  1. Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i) Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 114.38 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 5.49 Mbps for BSNL/MTNL (4G) ,  248.50 Mbps for RJIL (5G) & 94.30 Mbps for VIL(5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 25.11 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 1.72 Mbps for BSNL/MTNL (4G) ,  18.71 Mbps for RJIL (5G) & 18.92 Mbps for VIL(5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-I.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-I.

The overall mobile network performance on Noida Sector 121 to World Trade Centre (Delhi LSA) for the key Parameters has been summarized below:

a) Coverage Gap - The signal strength observed during voice testing on the drive test route in auto-selection mode (5G/4G/3G/2G), measured as the number of samples having poor signal strength out of the total samples collected, was 1/2793 for Airtel, 1646/2743 for BSNL/MTNL , 12/2849 for RJIL & 4/2973 for VIL. Details of the coverage gaps have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

b) Dropped Calls - Dropped calls in auto-selection mode (5G/ 4G/ 3G/ 2G), measured as the number of dropped calls out of the number of successfully established calls, were 0/25 for Airtel, 06/23 for BSNL/MTNL, 0/26 & 0/24 for VIL for RJIL. Details of the dropped call locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

c) Call Silence Instance - Call silence instances in Auto-selection mode (5G/4G), measured as the total number of silence instances observed for > 3 seconds out of the total calls established, were 0/24 for Airtel, NA for BSNL/MTNL, 0/21 for RJIL & 0/24 for VIL. Details of the call silence instance locations have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

d) Data Download and Upload Throughput:

i) Data Download performance (Overall): Average download speed was observed as 175.41Mbps for Airtel (5G), 3.39 Mbps for BSNL/MTNL (4G), 346.84 Mbps for RJIL (5G) & 129.86 Mbps for VIL (5G). Detail of Download throughput has been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

ii) Data Upload performance (Overall): Average upload speed was observed as 19.29 Mbps for Airtel (5G), 1.02 Mbps for BSNL/MTNL (4G) ,  27.94 Mbps for RJIL (5G) & 29.08 Mbps for VIL(5G). Details of Upload throughput have been provided in the map of Annexure-II.

Locations of Dropped Calls and Call Silence instances can be seen by clicking red dot on the map of Annexure-II.

Details of drive test route and area covered during the IDT are as below: -

a) City - The areas covered in the city drive are Mandoli, Sahibabad, Govindpuram, Vasundhara, Indirapuram, Pratap Vihar, Lal Kuan, Dhoom Manikpur, Madhuban Bapudham, Chipyana Khurd urf Tigri, Ghaziabad, Raj Nagar Extension, Chhapraula, Noida, Noida Sector 62, Noida Sector 63, Amity University Noida, Bisrakh Jalalpur, Kulesara, Surajpur, Greater Noida, Badalpur, Tilpata Karanwas, Sector XU-2, Dadha and Kasna and nearby areas.

b) Hotspot - The hotspot locations, capturing stationary user experience are Alpha 1 Market, Fortis Hospital Sec-62 Noida, Ghaziabad Junction Railway Station, MMG District Hospital, Noida City Centre Bus Stand, Noida Sector 52 Metro Station, Pari Chowk Station and The Grand Venice Mall.

c) Walk Test - The walk test conducted on 05th Sep 2026, covered Gandhi Nagar Market Ghaziabad, Ghaziabad Ghantaghar Market Including Turav Nagar Market and   Noida Sec-52 Metro to Noida Sec-51 Skywalk and Surrounding Areas capturing mobile network behaviors in crowded pedestrian environments.

item.content:encoded:
Cabinet
Cabinet approves continuation of Postal Operations Scheme with an outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore for 16th Finance Commission Cycle (FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31)
The scheme aims to modernize postal network, strengthen parcel and mail operations, enhance rural connectivity and improve citizen-centric services
Focus on e-commerce logistics, financial inclusion, international mail operations and digital transformation of India Post services
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the continuation of the Central Sector Scheme “Postal Operations” during the 16th Finance Commission Cycle from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with a proposed outlay of Rs. 1,141 Crore. The scheme seeks to strengthen postal infrastructure, improve operational efficiency and support the growing requirements of logistics, e-commerce and digital service delivery across the country. 

With one of the world’s largest postal networks comprising 1.65 lakh post offices, including 1,49,655 post offices in rural areas, India Post continues to serve as an important platform for delivery of mail, parcels, banking, insurance and other citizen-centric services, particularly in remote and underserved regions. 

Apart from its core postal operations, India Post provides a wide range of public services through initiatives such as Post Office Savings Bank (POSB), India Post Payments Bank (IPPB), Postal Life Insurance (PLI), Aadhaar enrolment and updation, Passport Services through Post Office Passport Seva Kendras, KYC verification services and support to rural artisans through Dakghar Niryat Kendras (DNKs). 

The scheme would support modernization of postal infrastructure, strengthen last-mile delivery, improve logistics efficiency, promote financial inclusion and enhance customer-centric service delivery across the country. The proposal also aligns with the broader objectives of Digital India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat. 

The scheme is intended to be implemented over a period of five years from FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31. 

The Postal Operations Scheme comprises the following six sub-schemes: 

  1. Rural Business and Access to Postal Network – Rs. 120 crore – Focused on infrastructure upgrades, standardized branding and better resource utilization to transform post offices, particularly in rural areas, into efficient and citizen-centric service hubs. The component aims to strengthen financial inclusion, digital connectivity and local economic development while improving last-mile delivery and enhancing access to postal and citizen-centric services in underserved regions. 
  2. Mail Network Optimization – Rs. 575 crore – Envisages modernization of mail operations through centralized delivery systems, mechanization, advanced IT solutions under Advanced Postal Technology (APT 2.0), GIS-based services and upgraded infrastructure. The initiative also includes strengthening delivery post offices, mail handling systems, Mail Motor Service (MMS) workshops, Road Transport Network and modern smart 24x7 letter boxes to improve operational efficiency, transparency, service quality and logistical reliability across the network. 
  3. Parcel Network Optimization – Rs. 278 crore – Includes construction of Parcel Hubs and expansion of Parcel Packaging Units (PPUs) aligned with the redesigned sorting framework to streamline parcel movement, reduce handling points, ease capacity constraints and improve transit times. The component also aims to support growing parcel volumes from e-commerce and rural markets through purpose-built facilities, standardized secure packaging and enhanced operational flexibility while improving customer trust and strengthening India Post’s competitiveness in the logistics sector.  
  4. Infrastructure Upgrade and Augmentation of Infrastructure for International Mails – Rs. 8 crore – Aims to strengthen international mail services by upgrading Foreign Post Offices (FPOs) and Sub Foreign Post Offices (SFPOs) to improve infrastructure and expedite processing of international consignments. The initiative also includes marketing and Advertisement through Postal / RMS Division and position India Post as a reliable international logistics provider while improving compliance, technology integration and export logistics support.  
  5. Marketing Functions including Quality of Service – Rs. 100 crore – Focused on promotion, branding, outreach and customer engagement through multi-channel campaigns across television, digital, radio, print and outdoor platforms. The component also includes participation in events and exhibitions, social media campaigns, direct marketing and expansion of Dak Chaupal activities to deepen grassroots engagement, especially in rural and underserved areas. In addition, it envisages infrastructure upgrades, studio facilities, ICT enhancements, market research, influencer engagement and third-party evaluation mechanisms to improve quality of service and strengthen a customer-centric approach.  
  6. Philately Operations – Rs. 60 crore – Proposes initiatives to promote philately through exhibitions, seminars, quizzes, school philatelic clubs and innovative stamp designs including scented, holographic and 3D stamps. The component also includes digital outreach activities, programmes such as the Dhai Akhar letter-writing competition and SPARSH scholarship, modernization of production and fulfillment centres, market research and international collaboration with the objective of revitalizing philately as an engaging educational and cultural activity while also improving operational efficiency and revenue potential.

item.title: India’s Bio-Economy Set to Reach 300 million Dollars by 2030; Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Industry to Seize Opportunities in Next Biotechnology Revolution
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Science & Technology
item.description: Ministry of Science & Technology India’s Bio-Economy Set to Reach 300 million Dollars by 2030; Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Industry to Seize Opportunities in Next Biotechnology Revolution Biotechnology Startups Grow from 50-60 in 2014 to Nearly 11,000; Bio-Economy Expands from 10 billion Dollars to 195 billion Dollars: Dr. Jitendra Singh Genomics and Multi-Omics Emerging as Strategic Technologies for Healthcare, Agriculture and Economic Growth: Dr. Jitendra Singh at CII Global Genomics Summit 2026 India’s Genetic Diversity Offers a Unique Global Advantage for Research and Innovation, says Dr.…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
India’s Bio-Economy Set to Reach 300 million Dollars by 2030; Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Industry to Seize Opportunities in Next Biotechnology Revolution
Biotechnology Startups Grow from 50-60 in 2014 to Nearly 11,000; Bio-Economy Expands from 10 billion Dollars to 195 billion Dollars: Dr. Jitendra Singh
Genomics and Multi-Omics Emerging as Strategic Technologies for Healthcare, Agriculture and Economic Growth: Dr. Jitendra Singh at CII Global Genomics Summit 2026
India’s Genetic Diversity Offers a Unique Global Advantage for Research and Innovation, says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Industry Participation, Private Investment and R&D Partnerships Crucial to Translating Scientific Discoveries into Economic Opportunities, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi

India’s bio-economy is set to reach 300 billion Dollars by 2030, with biotechnology set to drive the next Industrial Revolution, while Biotech Startups in India had already grown from just 50-60 in 2014 to over 11,000 today, Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh said today, urging industry leaders, Startups and investors to seize emerging opportunities through greater investment and participation in genomics, multi-omics and advanced biotechnology.

Drawing a parallel with the transformative role of Information Technology in the previous industrial revolution, the Minister said that biotechnology is now emerging as a strategic technology platform that will shape the future of healthcare, agriculture and global economic competitiveness. He cautioned that businesses must adapt to the rapidly changing technological landscape, as those failing to embrace emerging technologies risk becoming irrelevant.

Addressing the CII Global Genomics Summit 2026, themed ‘Powering the Next Bioeconomy Through Genomics and Multi-omics’, at New Delhi, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the summit provided an important platform to bring together the frontiers of science and technology with industry participation, translating scientific discoveries into healthcare solutions, economic opportunities and overall national development. He appreciated CII for bringing together industry representatives, startups and other stakeholders to advance India's biotechnology ecosystem.

Dr. Jitendra Singh said that the convergence of DNA sequencing, computational biology, Artificial Intelligence and different omics technologies, including metabolomics, transcriptomics and proteomics, would transform the understanding of complex diseases and enable more personalised healthcare. The same disease could require different treatment approaches for different individuals, making genomics an increasingly essential component of future medical practice. He said these technologies were no longer confined to research laboratories but were becoming indispensable for healthcare systems, businesses and nations seeking to remain competitive.

Emphasising India's unique advantage in genomic research, the Minister said the country's extraordinary genetic diversity could become a major global asset for research and development. India's diverse population groups and wide spectrum of diseases provide an extensive knowledge base for generating genomic data and developing solutions relevant to populations across the world. He said greater investment in genomic research would not only strengthen India's scientific capabilities but also create significant industrial and commercial opportunities.

Referring to the Genome India Project, he said whole-genome sequencing of 10,000 individuals representing 80 different population groups had already been undertaken, creating a valuable foundation for future research. He encouraged industry stakeholders to partner with government initiatives and translate this scientific resource into practical applications.

The Minister also drew attention to the extensive opportunities biotechnology offers in agriculture and livestock, beyond healthcare. Genomics and advanced biotechnology can help improve crop productivity, nutritional quality and resistance to pests and diseases, while supporting climate-resilient agriculture. In livestock, genomic applications can improve breeding practices and strengthen disease surveillance. He said the breadth of these applications offered businesses opportunities to specialise in different sectors and build sustainable, innovation-driven enterprises.

Speaking about India's rapidly expanding biotechnology ecosystem, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the government had introduced the BioE3 Policy- Biotechnology for Economy, Environment and Employment, to accelerate biotechnology-led growth. The establishment of bio-foundries and other enabling infrastructure is aimed at supporting research, startups and industry in translating scientific discoveries into commercially viable products.

He said India's biotechnology startup ecosystem had grown from just 50-60 startups in 2014 to over 11,000 today, while the country's bio-economy had expanded from approximately 10 billion Dollars to nearly 195 billion Dollars. With the target of reaching 300 billion Dollars by 2030, India is entering a significant phase of biotechnology-led economic growth.

Citing India's growing global credibility in biotechnology, the Minister referred to the country's DNA vaccine for COVID-19, which was supplied to 30 countries, and said Indian biotechnology products were increasingly gaining international acceptance. He also referred to developments in HPV vaccines, research on haemophilia treatment and cost-effective CAR-T cell therapy for cancer at Tata Memorial Centre as examples of India's growing capabilities in advanced healthcare research. He said these achievements demonstrated that India had reached a stage where its biotechnology innovations could find wider global markets and attract greater industry participation.

Dr. Jitendra Singh called upon the private sector to increase investment in research and development and build stronger partnerships with government institutions, research organisations and startups. He referred to the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme as an important initiative to accelerate private-sector participation in high-impact technologies. He also urged business leaders to support scientific research through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funding, particularly in areas such as cancer, diabetes and other major healthcare challenges. Describing research funding as a contribution to the well-being of society, he said investment in scientific research could create benefits extending far beyond individual businesses.

During his interaction with industry representatives, the Minister said that the biggest bottleneck in India's journey towards becoming a genomic powerhouse was the mindset, calling for greater openness towards emerging technologies and new business opportunities. Responding to concerns regarding regulatory processes for biotechnology products and advanced therapies, he said the government was working in consultation with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to simplify procedures and address overlapping regulatory requirements. He invited industry representatives to share specific challenges and practical suggestions so that these could be examined through better institutional coordination.

Concluding his address, Dr. Jitendra Singh called upon CII to act as an important bridge between the government and industry, facilitating greater investment, research partnerships and wider participation in India's biotechnology ecosystem. He said the success of India's scientific and technological progress would ultimately be measured not merely by the number of genomes sequenced or research papers published, but by the lives improved, products developed and economic opportunities created. He called for collective efforts to harness India's scientific potential towards Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat 2047.

item.content:encoded:
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)
Cabinet approves development of Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam at an estimated cost of 2,014 crore
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi

To overcome the severe operational and spatial constraints of the existing defense landlocked civil enclave at Silchar Airport and to accommodate sustained passenger growth, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the  development of a New Greenfield Airport at Doloo, Silchar, Assam by the Airports Authority of India (AAI) at an estimated cost of Rs.2,014 crore.

Doloo, situated in the Cachar District of Assam, serves as the strategic heart of the Barak Valley—a region renowned for its extensive tea gardens, agro-based industries, and immense potential for eco and cultural tourism.

The proposed Terminal Building will span a total area of 12,351 sqm with a capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hour, designed with modern passenger amenities, sustainable green building principles, and modular expansion capability. In addition, the project encompasses the development of a 2,705m x 45m, Code-4C compliant runway suitable for A-320 aircraft operations, along with the construction of a new Apron capable of parking 6 nos. A-320 aircraft and a dedicated isolation bay.

As a project of immense strategic significance, the Doloo Greenfield Airport will meet the rapidly growing demands of air traffic in South Assam and adjoining areas of neighbouring States. It will significantly decongest existing infrastructure, unlock regional economic potential by boosting trade and tourism, and offer a world-class gateway integrating Northeast India with broader national and international growth corridors.

item.dc:creator: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)
item.description: Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) Cabinet approves development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) Basis Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposed project for development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL) under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode on a Design, Build,…
item.content:encoded:
Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA)
Cabinet approves development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited under Public Private Partnership (PPP) Mode on Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) Basis
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the proposed project for development of the Second Container Terminal at Kamarajar Port Limited (KPL) under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) mode on a Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer (DBFOT) basis, at an estimated project cost of Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST. The project envisages the development of a 900-metre-long container terminal with a design draft of 18 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million Twenty-foot Equivalent Units (TEUs), to be implemented in two phases.

Expenditure involved:

The estimated project cost of the PPP component is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The investment is to be arranged by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. The project proposal separately indicates an estimated dredging cost of Rs.450 crore to be borne by KPL.

Details:

(i)    The project envisages development of a 900-metre-long Second Container Terminal with a berth width of 30 metres and an annual container-handling capacity of 2.0 million TEUs. The terminal will be developed in two phases: Phase I with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs and Phase II with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs.

(ii)   The terminal is designed to handle large container vessels, including vessels of up to 24,346 TEUs and 400 metres in length overall, with a design draft of 18 metres. This will strengthen KPL’s ability to handle larger mainline vessels and improve connectivity with international shipping routes.

(iii)  The project is intended to meet the growing demand for containerised export-import (EXIM) cargo from the Chennai–Ennore industrial and economic region and the wider southern hinterland. Key cargo-generating sectors include automobiles and auto components, engineering goods, electronics, chemicals and other manufactured products.

(iv)  KPL handled 49.08 million tonnes of cargo and 1,008 vessels during FY 2025–26, including more than 7 lakh TEUs of container traffic. The existing container terminal has an installed capacity of 0.8 million TEUs per annum and handled approximately 0.7 million TEUs in FY 2025–26, representing utilisation of about 88%.

(v)   Container traffic in India has grown at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of about 7% over the last five years, while KPL’s container traffic has grown at approximately 9.9% during the same period. The feasibility study projects continued growth in container traffic in the south-eastern region, supporting the need to augment capacity at KPL.

(vi)  The project will be implemented on a DBFOT basis for a concession period of 40 years, including a construction period of 48 months. Phase I is scheduled for completion within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, with commercial operations commencing in the 25th month. Construction of Phase II will be undertaken from the 25th to the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month.

(vii) The estimated project cost is Rs.4,288.26 crore, including GST, comprising Rs.2,429.32 crore for Phase I and Rs.1,858.94 crore for Phase II. The cost is to be financed by the selected concessionaire through the DBFOT framework. In addition, KPL is to incur an estimated Rs.450 crore towards dredging, as indicated in the project proposal.

(viii) The project is proposed to be implemented through a transparent, open global bidding process. The concessionaire will arrange the required financing and recover its investment through user charges in accordance with the provisions of the Concession Agreement and applicable tariff framework.

(ix)  The project is aligned with Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. It is expected to strengthen KPL’s position as a container gateway on India’s East Coast, improve the efficiency of the maritime logistics chain and support the growth of EXIM trade.

Implementation Strategy and Targets:

The project will be implemented by the selected concessionaire under the DBFOT model. Phase I, with a capacity of 1.1 million TEUs, is to be completed within 24 months from the Date of Award of Concession, and commercial operations are to commence in the 25th month. Phase II, with a capacity of 0.9 million TEUs, is to be completed by the 48th month, with full commercial operations commencing in the 49th month. The project proposal also provides for obtaining environmental and other necessary clearances in a time-bound manner before the bid due date.

Major Impact:

(i)  The additional capacity of 2.0 million TEUs per annum will strengthen KPL’s ability to accommodate growing container traffic and provide an additional gateway for EXIM cargo from the industrial clusters of Tamil Nadu and the adjoining hinterland.

(ii) The terminal’s design draft of 18 metres and capability to handle large container vessels are expected to improve international connectivity, facilitate direct calls by mainline vessels and reduce dependence on foreign deep-water hub ports and associated feedering costs.

(iii) The project is expected to improve maritime logistics efficiency, support trade and manufacturing, strengthen the port’s revenue potential and contribute to India’s maritime competitiveness.

(iv)     The project is expected to generate employment for approximately 750 persons directly and indirectly during construction and to increase about 800 persons during the operational phase.

(v) The project supports the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by augmenting domestic port capacity and improving logistics support for industries and original equipment manufacturers in Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and the adjoining hinterland.

(vi)     There will be no financial implication for the Government of India, as the investment in the PPP component will be arranged by the selected concessionaire.

Background:

(i)  Kamarajar Port Limited, formerly known as Ennore Port Limited, one of the 12 Major Ports of India and is wholly owned by Chennai Port Authority under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Located on the east coast of Tamil Nadu near the Chennai industrial and economic region, the port handles a range of cargo, including coal, petroleum, oil and lubricants, LNG, LPG, containers, automobiles and general cargo.

(ii) During FY 2025–26, KPL recorded revenue of approximately Rs.1,280 crore and Profit Before Tax of Rs.924 crore. The port has recorded cargo growth at a CAGR of 13.64% over the last five years, reflecting the expansion of economic activity and trade in its hinterland.

(iii) The Chennai–Ennore region is a major industrial and manufacturing cluster of India. As trade and containerisation expand, additional container-handling capacity and efficient facilities for larger vessels are required to support the movement of EXIM cargo from Tamil Nadu, southern Andhra Pradesh and the wider southern hinterland.

item.title: Cabinet approves Rs.11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem
item.dc:creator: Cabinet
item.description: Cabinet Cabinet approves Rs.11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem The scheme aims to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment ecosystem in India, supporting the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the "Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem" with a financial outlay of…
item.content:encoded:
Cabinet
Cabinet approves Rs.11,000 crore Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem
The scheme aims to promote domestic manufacturing of construction and infrastructure equipment ecosystem in India, supporting the Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan
Posted On: 25 NOV 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi

The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved the "Scheme for Enhancement of Construction and Infrastructure Equipment (CIE) Manufacturing Ecosystem" with a financial outlay of Rs.11,000 crore. The Scheme, to be implemented by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI), aims to incentivize domestic manufacturing of CIE and its components and to establish a dedicated CIE testing facility in the country, thereby enhancing self-reliance and positioning India as a key player in the Global CIE market.

India's CIE industry is currently the world's third largest, after China and the United States, with a market size of around Rs.97,500 crore in FY2024-25. Driven by accelerated growth in infrastructure (roads and ports) and housing, the industry is projected to increase more than double, reaching a market size of around Rs.2,28,100 crore by FY2029-30.

Driven by rapid growth in the construction and infrastructure sector, the scheme aims to incentivize manufacturing of technologically advanced equipment such as Ship-to-Shore Cranes, Tunnel Boring Machines, Hydraulic Excavators, Off-Highway Trucks, etc. The scheme has also provision of establishment of state of art dedicated CIE testing facility in the country.

The scheme with duration of eight years from FY2026-27, comprise of a two-year gestation period (FY2026-27 to FY2027-28) for setting up manufacturing facilities, followed by a five-year incentive disbursement period (FY2028-29 to FY2032-33), and a final year (FY2033-34) for settlement of incentives on incremental sales of FY2032-33.

The scheme has two components:

  1. Sales-linked Incentive – Incentives will be provided on the Incremental Sales Value of eligible CIE equipment and components to approved applicants across two categories – eligible OEMs and Component Manufacturers. Graded Incentive rates range from 13% to 8% of incremental sales value over a five-year period.
  2. Grant for CIE Testing Facility – A grant of up to Rs.375 crore, in the nature of Viability Gap Funding, for setting up a dedicated CIE testing facility,

This initiative by the Government of India is a landmark step towards strengthening the domestic Construction and Infrastructure Equipment manufacturing ecosystem and enhancing competitiveness in the global markets. By fostering indigenous capabilities in manufacturing of CIE, the scheme will ensure supply chain security, increase opportunities for employment and promote Atmanirbhar Bharat. It embodies the Government’s unwavering commitment to build a technologically self-reliant, globally competitive and sustainable industrial base, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Celebrate Cinema by Bringing People Together”: Gujarati Film, Laalo – Krishna Sada Sahaayate wins hearts at IFFI 2026
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 8:42PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 24 November 2026

 

Laalo – Krishna Sada Sahaayate, a 2025 Gujarati spiritual drama directed by Ankit Bhupatbhai Sakhiya featured in the Indian Panorama section at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) 2026 in Goa today. The film follows a struggling rickshaw driver with a troubled past and a life of poverty, who is trapped in a remote farmhouse, where he confronts his guilt and seeks redemption through visions of Lord Krishna. Addressing the press at IFFI today, director Sakhiya spoke about the film's making, its spiritual themes and its unexpected journey to box-office success.

At its heart, the film celebrates faith and resilience. Lord Krishna serves as a silent companion to the protagonist, guiding his journey of self-reflection and healing. The director said his intention was to create an emotional connection with audiences through the universal themes of love, faith and inner transformation.

Explaining the title, Sakhiya said ‘Laalo’ is an affectionate name for Lord Krishna, also used for little boys. Marking Sakhiya’s debut as a feature-film director, the film was made on a modest budget, with financial support from friends who also became part of the cast. 

Sakhiya recalled that the film gradually gained popularity through word of mouth and went on to register a reported box-office collection of around Rs. 130 crores. He credited social media for expanding its reach through videos capturing audience reactions. He also recalled the special experience of screening the film in his own village and receiving the affection and blessings of its people.

Speaking about its creative approach, Sakhiya highlighted the influence of Garba on the film's music and the use of close-up shots to convey emotions. The music director contributed remotely from Australia. The film relies on natural performances, dialogue and emotional depth rather than visual grandeur. The film is simple and mostly shot in a linear form, yet Sakhiya wanted it to engage the audience. The story also evolved organically.

On the future of Gujarati cinema, Sakhiya said the state's rich cultural heritage offers many stories waiting to be told. He expressed optimism about the growing presence of regional cinema and emphasised the need to prioritise meaningful storytelling alongside commercial success.

The session was moderated by Shri Kuldeep Meena.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Elephants in the Fog Explores the Paradox of Social Acceptance and Exclusion: Director Abinash Bikram Shah
Director Uses Elephant Metaphor to Examine Social Prejudice in Elephants in the Fog
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 8:28PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 24 November 2026

 

A society that welcomes transgender women during auspicious occasions but often denies them dignity and acceptance in everyday life forms the central paradox explored in Nepali feature film Elephants in the Fog. Director and screenwriter Abinash Bikram Shah and lead actor Pushpa Thing Lama discussed the film and its themes during a press interaction organized on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

The film, which received the Jury Prize in the Un Certain Regard section and the Best Sound Creation Award at the 79th Cannes Film Festival, now marks another significant milestone for Nepali cinema on the international stage.

Set in Nepal, Elephants in the Fog follows Pirati, a transgender woman and mother of three daughters, who dreams of building a new life with the man she loves. Her aspirations are disrupted when her youngest daughter, Apsara, goes missing during a night patrol organised to protect the village from wild elephants. As the search unfolds, the film examines the intersections of motherhood, identity, personal freedom and social exclusion.

Sharing the film’s journey to Cannes, Shah described the international recognition as surreal and expressed satisfaction at representing Nepali cinema on a global platform. He said receiving two awards was particularly gratifying, noting that the Best Sound Creation Award held special significance for a film seeking to amplify voices and experiences that often remain unheard.

Explaining the title, Shah said elephants were not part of the original screenplay but gradually emerged as a metaphor for the film’s central theme. He drew a parallel between elephants, revered when within accepted boundaries but feared when they cross them, and transgender people, welcomed during auspicious occasions but often denied dignity and acceptance in everyday life. Through this contrast, the film questions society’s conditional acceptance of marginalized communities.

For Pushpa Thing Lama, portraying Pirati was both a challenging and deeply personal experience. Speaking from her own perspective as a transgender woman, she highlighted the difficulties transgender people continue to face in securing social acceptance and recognition. She described the film as an opportunity to bring their experiences to a wider audience and enable their stories to be seen, heard and understood.

Reflecting on her preparation for the role, Lama said it required her to draw upon real-life experiences and emotions and understand the character’s journey from within. She also spoke about the influence of her mother’s upbringing and teachings in shaping her outlook towards life, resilience and the challenges of confronting society.

The filmmaker said the film took nearly three years to develop. Through Pirati’s journey and the metaphor of elephants, Elephants in the Fog examines social boundaries around identity and belonging, highlighting the gap between symbolic acceptance and the everyday denial of dignity.

The press interaction was moderated by Lekshmi Priya.

item.title: Mid-fest film ‘I Matter’ Explores Identity, Belonging and the Many Layers of Humanity: Director Alina Șerban at IFFI 2026
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting Mid-fest film ‘I Matter’ Explores Identity, Belonging and the Many Layers of Humanity: Director Alina Șerban at IFFI 2026 Working on the lead character helped me embrace my Roma roots with pride: Lead Actress Denisa Farcaș Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 8:18PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 24 November 2026 There are many untold stories from the Roma community waiting to be discovered, said Romanian-Roma filmmaker Alina Șerban, director of I Matter ( Eu Contez ), the Mid-Fest film at the 57th International Film Festival of India…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Mid-fest film ‘I Matter’ Explores Identity, Belonging and the Many Layers of Humanity: Director Alina Șerban at IFFI 2026
Working on the lead character helped me embrace my Roma roots with pride: Lead Actress Denisa Farcaș
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 8:18PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 24 November 2026

 

There are many untold stories from the Roma community waiting to be discovered, said Romanian-Roma filmmaker Alina Șerban, director of I Matter (Eu Contez), the Mid-Fest film at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa.

Interacting with the media at a press conference organised by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) on the sidelines of IFFI today, Șerban spoke about the inspiration behind the film, its portrayal of the Roma community and the importance of challenging stereotypes through cinema. Lead actresses Denisa Farcaș and Vanessa Dancea also participated in the interaction.

A multilingual drama featuring dialogues in Romanian and Romani, I Matter had its Indian premiere at IFFI today. A co-production of Romania, Germany and Belgium, the film explores identity, family, belonging and the pursuit of a future beyond one's past. It follows Rebeca, a young Roma woman preparing to leave the orphanage she has called home. As she hopes to reunite with her father, who is about to be released from prison, and build the family she has always longed for, her admission to university to study acting offers the possibility of a new beginning.

Responding to a question on challenging stereotypes through cinema, she said the film seeks to explore different dimensions of humanity. “The film asks questions about who deserves to be a human. I want to portray different layers of humanity,” she said. She also expressed happiness at being part of IFFI, describing her visit to India as a homecoming.

Highlighting the challenges of representing the Roma community on screen, Șerban observed that despite its significant cultural influence, the community continues to remain on the margins of society. “Our culture, like flamenco, has impacted universal culture. But we are still at the margins of society. We live so close to other people, but they still don't know us,” she said.

Emphasising the film's message of empowerment, Șerban said she wanted to reach out particularly to young people from disadvantaged backgrounds. “I wanted to tell a story that would empower, first and foremost, young people from disadvantaged groups. I wanted to tell them what I also needed to hear: that I will manage, that there is maybe a small place for each of us in the world,” she said.

Lead actress Denisa Farcaș, who portrays Rebeca, described the film as a deeply personal experience that transformed her relationship with her own identity. Recalling her initial hesitation about acknowledging her Roma ethnicity, she said, “For the first time, I saw Roma people in a positive light.” She added that portraying the character helped her overcome the shame associated with her identity and embrace her roots with pride. “I am proud to be Roma,” she said, expressing happiness that the stories of the community and its children were finally being heard.

The session was moderated by Pranjal Rai.

item.content:encoded:
President's Secretariat
PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES BALI JATRA FESTIVAL 2026 AT KATAKA
DRAW INSPIRATION FROM THE PAST TO SHAPE THE PRESENT AND BRIGHTEN THE FUTURE: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 8:16PM by PIB Delhi

The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the Bali Jatra Festival 2026 at Kataka, Odisha today (November 24, 2026).

Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Bali Jatra is a unique festival which celebrates the glorious history of Odisha. The history of maritime trade has evolved into a tradition and the tradition has become a festival. This reflects both the creativity and the historical perspective of the people of Odisha.

The President said that the merchants from Odisha used to travel to distant lands to engage in trade and commerce. Through trade, they accomplished many significant things for the country. They discovered new maritime routes and strengthened international relations. They were also a medium of cultural exchange.

The President said that the historic connection between Odisha and Bali could be transformed into modern commercial and cultural cooperation. She was happy to note that cultural troupes from Indonesia are participating in this Bali Jatra. The Odisha Festival is being celebrated in Bali over two days, featuring Odisha’s dance and music, handlooms, handicrafts, and traditional cuisine. She expressed confidence that such cultural exchanges will strengthen the historic ties between India and Indonesia.

The President said that it is good to be proud of glories of the past and celebrate our festivals. But we should draw inspiration from the past to shape the present and brighten the future. Our younger generation, in particular, has much to learn from the courage and competence of our merchants.

The President said that building Viksit Bharat is our national goal. India’s stature on the international stage has grown. While there is unrest in many parts of the world and instability in the global economy, India’s economy continues to remain strong. This is a promising indicator of our journey toward becoming Viksit Bharat.

The President was happy to note that Odisha is emerging as an industrial hub and is attracting an increasing number of investors. Entrepreneurs, artisans, weavers and the younger generation in Odisha are strengthening the state's economy through their skills and spirit of enterprise. Their growing contributions are an encouraging sign of progress towards realizing the vision of Viksit Odisha.

item.title: “Not Only Filmmakers, Every Human Being Breathes Stories”: Bogdan Mureșanu at IFFI Masterclass
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting “Not Only Filmmakers, Every Human Being Breathes Stories”: Bogdan Mureșanu at IFFI Masterclass “When a Monologue in your Mind Becomes a Dialogue, the Film Is No Longer Yours Alone”: Mureșanu Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 7:42PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 24 November 2026 Every story carries a fragment of reality, just as every memory holds the possibility of fiction. Exploring this intricate space between lived experience and cinematic imagination, acclaimed Romanian writer-director and producer Bogdan Mureșanu conducted an…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
“Not Only Filmmakers, Every Human Being Breathes Stories”: Bogdan Mureșanu at IFFI Masterclass
“When a Monologue in your Mind Becomes a Dialogue, the Film Is No Longer Yours Alone”: Mureșanu
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 7:42PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 24 November 2026

 

Every story carries a fragment of reality, just as every memory holds the possibility of fiction. Exploring this intricate space between lived experience and cinematic imagination, acclaimed Romanian writer-director and producer Bogdan Mureșanu conducted an engaging masterclass titled ‘The Thin Borders Between the Reality and Fiction’ at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa today.

Addressing an enthusiastic gathering of cinephiles, students and film professionals, Mureșanu shared insightful reflections on why storytelling is intrinsic to human existence and how narratives help us comprehend the world. Emphasising that storytelling is not the exclusive domain of artists, he observed that from everyday anecdotes shared among friends to stories told through cinema, narratives allow us to explore possible realities and recharge our spirit.

He described filmmaking as a deeply personal process that ultimately transforms into a collective experience. “When a monologue in your mind becomes a dialogue, the film is no longer yours alone,” he remarked, highlighting how a filmmaker's private vision finds new meaning through the audience's interpretation. Discussing the craft of cinema, Mureșanu emphasised the importance of a clear central idea. “Unlike a novel, which can accommodate several narrative diversions, a two-hour film must remain focused, with its context, premise and themes aligned with a strong central vision”, he asserted.

He also highlighted the power of the ‘unspoken’ in cinematic storytelling. Recalling a sequence in one of his films, he explained how he deliberately chose not to show a character lighting a firecracker, leaving the moment to the audience's imagination. Such creative restraint, he noted, allows viewers to emotionally participate in the story.

Challenging the perception of archival footage as an entirely objective representation of history, Mureșanu pointed out that every camera captures only one perspective. Drawing on his films The Christmas Gift and The New Year That Never Came, he discussed how archival material and fictional narratives can complement one another. Sharing a fascinating anecdote, he observed, “When fiction works as a simplified model to understand reality, it becomes one with reality. They feed each other.”

Mureșanu further explored how visual language shapes storytelling, explaining his use of the 4:3 aspect ratio in films set during Romania's communist era to complement archival footage and create a sense of intimacy and confinement. In contrast, his animated short The Magician, employed a sweeping widescreen format that gave the harbour an active narrative presence.

Reflecting on contemporary cinema, he stressed that true cinematic power lies not merely in pace or spectacle, but in the expressive possibilities of the human face and the emotions conveyed through a gaze. The interactive Q&A explored historical biopics, mythology and the ethical responsibilities of portraying real-life personalities. Referring to a recent offer to direct a biopic on legendary personality, Mureșanu observed that focusing on a defining chapter of a person's life can often reveal deeper truths than attempting an exhaustive biography.

Concluding on a philosophical note, he encouraged storytellers to move beyond inherited perspectives, engage with the wider world and return to their roots with courage and clarity.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
Gala Premiere at IFFI showcases ambitious Malayalam film Half blending supernatural elements with human emotions
Half Explores a Distinctive Vampire Universe with Action, Emotion and an Unconventional Narrative
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 7:27PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 24 November 2026

 

Malayalam film Half, which brings together supernatural elements, high-octane action and deeply rooted human emotions, held its gala premiere at the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), offering audiences a glimpse into an unconventional cinematic universe.

Speaking at a Press Conference organised by Press Information Bureau today, actress Amala Paul said that roles involving vampires and supernatural characters are rarely offered to actors, making Half a particularly exciting project for her. She described it as an opportunity to step into a character she had never imagined portraying, something she had always wanted to explore as an actor.

Actor Abbas described his role in the film as something distinctly different from his previous projects. Recalling the challenges of filming in the intense heat of Jaisalmer, he said the experience pushed him beyond familiar territory. Describing the film as a surprise package, he praised the entire team for their efforts in creating an entertaining cinematic experience for audiences.

For actor Ranjith Sajeev, his passion for acting made the project particularly exciting. Describing Half as an action thriller with a distinctive approach, he revealed that both lead actors, himself and Aiswarya Raj, underwent an intensive workshop to prepare for the demanding action sequences. Explaining his character, he pointed out that despite being an action-driven film, Half does not feature a single slow-motion shot, reflecting the team's intention to create a distinctive theatrical experience.

Actress Aiswarya Raj highlighted the sibling relationship as one of the aspects of the film that resonated most strongly with her. She acknowledged that learning and performing the action sequences was challenging and quite different from what she had anticipated.  Describing Half as one of the most striking portrayals of vampires, she said the film presents them as friendly, relatable, almost next-door characters rather than conventional supernatural beings.

Producer Anne Sanjeev spoke about the film's bold concept and distinctive theme, emphasising the team's ambition to take Malayalam cinema beyond geographical boundaries. The team, she added, was keen to introduce its distinctive story to international audiences. She also expressed her hope of bringing more unique and engaging content to viewers in the future.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Union Minister Dr Virendra Kumar Visits Siddharth Nasha Mukti Kendra in Lucknow
Minister Interacts with Beneficiaries, Reviews Treatment and Rehabilitation Facilities; Directs Centre Management to Strengthen Infrastructure, Hygiene and Counselling Services
De-Addiction centres function not merely as treatment facilities but as comprehensive rehabilitation spaces supporting physical, psychological, emotional and social reintegration of beneficiaries: Dr Virendra Kumar
Posted On: 24 NOV 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment, Dr. Virendra Kumar, today visited Siddharth Nasha Mukti Kendra, at Thakurganj, in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, to review the functioning of the de-addiction and rehabilitation facility and assess the quality of services being provided to persons undergoing treatment for substance dependence.

The Centre, is run by the voluntary organisation Bhartiya Samaj Seva Sansthan, Lucknow.

During the visit, the Minister was informed about the ongoing activities, services provided, treatment and rehabilitation of the victims of substance abuse, at the Centre.

As part of the inspection, Dr. Virendra Kumar undertook a detailed review of the available facilities and interacted directly with the beneficiaries to understand their well-being, treatment experience and the support being provided to them. He enquired about the quality of medical care, counselling sessions and recreational facilities available at the centre.

Emphasising the importance of a comprehensive and compassionate approach to de-addiction, the Minister directed the management to further strengthen the quality, effectiveness and regularity of treatment, counselling and rehabilitation services.

Observing that the centre had been functioning from the same building for several years, the Minister directed the management to undertake necessary improvements in its infrastructure and overall appearance. He specifically instructed the authorities to ensure fresh painting of the premises and upgradation of furniture so that beneficiaries could be provided with a clean, comfortable and conducive environment during their treatment and recovery.

 

The Minister also inspected the cleanliness arrangements and kitchen facilities at the centre. While expressing satisfaction with the overall maintenance and kitchen arrangements, he emphasised that hygiene and sanitation must be maintained consistently. He directed the staff to sustain the existing standards and undertake further improvements wherever necessary, particularly in areas related to food preparation, cleanliness and the daily living environment of beneficiaries.

Highlighting the importance of emotional, mental and spiritual well-being in the process of recovery from substance dependence, Dr. Virendra Kumar directed the centre management to earmark a dedicated and peaceful space within the premises for daily prayers and worship.

He further advised the management to periodically invite representatives of reputed spiritual and humanitarian organisations, including The Art of Living, Brahma Kumaris and other such institutions, to conduct positive counselling and motivational sessions for the beneficiaries. Such engagements, he emphasised, could complement medical treatment and psychological counselling by fostering positivity, self-confidence, inner strength and a sense of purpose among individuals undergoing rehabilitation.

The Minister underscored the need to ensure that de-addiction centres function not merely as treatment facilities but as comprehensive rehabilitation spaces that support the physical, psychological, emotional and social reintegration of beneficiaries.

The Union Minister’s visit reflects the emphasis of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment on strengthening the monitoring of de-addiction and rehabilitation facilities, ensuring quality service delivery and promoting a beneficiary-centric approach to drug demand reduction. The directions issued by the Minister are intended to further improve the standards of care, infrastructure and rehabilitation support at the centre, with an emphasis on their time-bound implementation.

Officials from the Prohibition Department and the State Social Welfare Department, the Centre Director, Shri Jitendra Verma, along with other staff members, were present on the occasion.
