item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj
Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh Calls for Mission-Mode Implementation of SVAMITVA to Achieve Saturation by March 31, 2027
States Urged to Prepare Time-Bound Action Plans; Drone surveys completed in 3.28 Lakh villages; 3.47 Crore Property Cards Generated
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 7:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Review Meeting on the SVAMITVA Scheme was held today in New Delhi, with the Centre and the States committing themselves to complete the implementation of rural property ownership under the Scheme within the stipulated timeframe. The meeting was addressed by Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (FAHD), Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh and Union Minister of State for Panchayati Raj and FAHD, Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel. Participants included Ministers from nine States, Dr. Vineet Joshi, Secretary, Ministry of Panchayati Raj and other senior officers of the Ministry, senior officials from the States/Union Territories and Survey of India.

Addressing the meeting, Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh said that SVAMITVA, launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 24th April 2020, aims to strengthen rural India by promoting peace, social harmony and financial progress through clear land ownership records. He said that the Scheme embodies Prime Minister’s vision of revitalising the rural economy, enabling the monetisation of rural properties and resolving property disputes in rural areas, and described it as a transformative step for Grameen Bharat. Drone technology and GIS mapping are employed under the Scheme to determine property boundaries with precision and to provide legal records of ownership to rural households. The Union Minister pointed out that banks now accept SVAMITVA Property Cards as collateral, enabling rural citizens to access loans against their properties, start enterprises, pursue livelihood opportunities and lessen their reliance on informal sources of high-cost credit. Clear land ownership records, he said, are also reducing land-related disputes and advancing economic empowerment of women. Shri Singh apprised the participants that till now, drone surveys have been completed in 3.28 lakh villages and under this scheme, 3.47 crore Property Cards have been generated for 2.20 lakh villages. He appreciated the collaborative efforts made in partnership with the Survey of India, the Revenue Departments of the States and the Ministry, while commending the States that have achieved saturation. The union minister called upon the States to make full use of the high-resolution spatial data generated under the Scheme for the estimation of solar potential, planning of drainage networks and spatial planning in Gram Panchayats, thereby strengthening Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) and need-based village development planning. Urging all States to prepare time-bound action plans to achieve saturation under the Scheme by 31st March 2027, he underlined its significance in realising the vision of Gram Swaraj through empowered villages.

Union Minister of State Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel spoke of the far-reaching impact of the Scheme in providing a Record of Rights to households in rural inhabited (Abadi) areas. He said that the distribution of Property Cards has established clear land ownership records and enabled rural citizens to leverage their property for institutional credit, thereby promoting financial inclusion and contributing to poverty alleviation. He added that the Scheme has also helped reduce land-related disputes and strengthen the social fabric of rural areas. Prof. Baghel urged the States to carry the remaining drone surveys, and the preparation and distribution of Property Cards, to ensure completion in mission mode, so that rural citizens may reap the full benefits of the Scheme.

A presentation providing an overview of the Scheme, including its progress, State-wise achievements and the way forward, was made during the meeting. The deliberations focused on expediting ground verification and Property Card distribution, sharing best practices adopted by States and leveraging high-resolution geospatial maps for improved rural planning. Emphasis was also laid on strengthening Centre-State coordination to realize the Scheme’s vision of empowered rural communities through transparent property ownership and effective governance. The growing use of SVAMITVA Property Cards to access institutional credit was also highlighted, with 16,614 loans amounting to ₹1,769.56 crore availed across Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Gujarat, Mizoram, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The overall progress with regard to implementation of the Scheme is as follows:

 

Activity

Progress

Target Villages

3.33 lakh villages

Drone Survey Completed

3.28 lakh villages (98%)

Village Maps Generated and Handed Over to States

3.17 lakh villages (95%)

Ground Verification by States

2.69 lakh villages (81%)

Maps Placed for Objections/Claims

2.46 lakh villages (74%)

Property Cards Generated

3.47 crore Property Cards for 2.20 lakh villages (66%)

 

State representatives shared how SVAMITVA is promoting financial stability, improving property tax assessment and strengthening village-level planning through GIS-based maps for infrastructure such as drainage networks, street lighting and solar installations. They also apprised the chair, of the progress made in drone surveys and ground verification in their respective States/UTs, assuring that the remaining work would be expedited to meet the Scheme’s targets within the stipulated timeline. The meeting concluded with the Centre and States reaffirming their commitment to work in close coordination such that the benefits of clear property ownership reach every eligible rural household.

***

AA

item.title: From Ancestral Roots to Human Bonds, 12 Goan Films Bring Local Stories to the Global Stage at 57th IFFI
item.description: Ministry of Information & Broadcasting From Ancestral Roots to Human Bonds, 12 Goan Films Bring Local Stories to the Global Stage at 57th IFFI Films in Konkani and Marathi explore identity, family, social realities and the complexities of everyday life Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 7:54PM by PIB Mumbai Goa, 20 November 2026 Long celebrated across the world for its coastal charm, vibrant heritage, and unmatched hospitality, Goa has another side that deserves equal attention — its stories and the people behind them. At the 57th International Film Festival of…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Information & Broadcasting
From Ancestral Roots to Human Bonds, 12 Goan Films Bring Local Stories to the Global Stage at 57th IFFI
Films in Konkani and Marathi explore identity, family, social realities and the complexities of everyday life
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 7:54PM by PIB Mumbai

Goa, 20 November 2026

 

Long celebrated across the world for its coastal charm, vibrant heritage, and unmatched hospitality, Goa has another side that deserves equal attention — its stories and the people behind them. At the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI), a specially curated package brings this side of Goa to the screen, exploring lives, relationships, memories and experiences that are both deeply local and universally relatable.

Scheduled for screening from November 21 to 28 at INOX Panjim, this collection of films traverses a rich emotional landscape. Stories of an elderly woman confronting her conscience, a forgotten local hero whose past resurfaces, a daughter seeking reconciliation with her family, and an elderly villager defending his ancestral home reflect the range of human experiences explored through these films.

Spanning Konkani and Marathi, the selection comprises feature and short films that explore a wide spectrum of themes, including family relationships, social realities, personal struggles, identity, childhood, loneliness and personal discovery. From deeply personal narratives to quirky comedies and thought-provoking dramas, the films offer audiences an engaging glimpse into the evolving landscape of filmmaking in Goa.

A glimpse into the Goan film selection:

ANCESSAO

Director: Manguirish J. Bandodkar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 30 minutes

Set in a quiet Goan village, Ancessao follows an elderly woman living alone, filling the silence of her life with conversations about others. Unable to confront her own grief, she eventually recognises her gossip as a distraction from an unhealed wound. When her conscience prompts her to change, she makes a resolve to mend her ways, but the transformation proves short-lived.

UMESH

Director: Vardhan Vijaykumar Kamat | Language: Konkani | Duration: 1 hour 39 minutes

Once a celebrated local hero, Umesh now leads a reclusive life in a rural Goan village, surviving on odd jobs and haunted by an unresolved past. His life takes an unexpected turn when aspiring filmmakers Anton and Rohan arrive to document him. As they navigate local rumours and half-truths, they uncover a forgotten talent and the painful circumstances behind his isolation. As trust gradually develops, Umesh grows increasingly wary of the camera. Umesh explores identity, trust and the cost of a forgotten legacy.

SHAKUNTALA

Director: Prasad M. Naik | Language: Konkani | Duration: 11 minutes

An emotional family drama about love, identity and tradition, Shakuntala follows a woman estranged from her conservative family after marrying a Christian man from her neighbourhood. Years later, following her father's death, she is denied the opportunity to attend his funeral. As the twelfth-day death ritual approaches, Shakuntala gathers the courage to return to her childhood home, confronting buried conflicts and societal judgment. Her journey is not merely to fulfil a ritual but to reclaim her place as a daughter and question whether love can transcend tradition.

PURNATA

Director: Shravan Kankonkar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 25 minutes

Through the journey of Zayo, a garland of jasmine flowers, Purnata captures the many lives it touches, bringing comfort, hope and joy through moments of happiness and sadness. Even as the flowers gradually wither, they continue to make lives beautiful. The film reflects on the continuity of life and purpose, suggesting that even when one life ends, another carries the journey forward.

NOISE

Director: Suvidha Torgal Bakhle | Language: Konkani | Duration: 16 minutes

An intimate exploration of human behaviour and relationships, Noise follows Tara as she struggles to break free from a troubled relationship and recurring patterns that cause her distress. Despite her efforts to heal and move forward, she repeatedly finds herself drawn towards the familiar. The recurring presence of an old fan becomes a metaphor for these cycles of behaviour, echoing the film's central reflection on the difficulty of changing even when one recognises the need to do so.

DARYAA

Director: Kishor Arjun | Language: Marathi | Duration: 25 minutes

Daryaa tells the story of Aakash, a visually impaired boy with cerebral palsy who has never seen the sea and knows it only through stories, sounds and imagination. When his grandfather takes him on an unexpected journey to the coast, Aakash encounters the world he has long dreamed of. The film explores the profound experience of discovering the sea and reminds us that seeing may have little to do with sight.

PERFECT SHOT

Director: Sankalp Sainath Parab | Language: Konkani | Duration: 14 minutes

For Vasudha, a young film school student, the quest for the perfect cinematic frame becomes an obsession shaped by the Golden Ratio, symmetry and the rule of thirds. At the same time, she struggles with unresolved emotions towards her late father, believing he left her with nothing of value. As memories resurface, her pursuit of visual perfection turns into a personal journey of discovery. The film explores how relationships shape our vision and creativity, revealing that meaningful storytelling goes beyond the technical rules of cinema.

BAPO KALE

Director: Krisha Raul | Language: Konkani | Duration: 24 minutes

Set in the village of Mauxi, Bapo Kale follows an elderly man who refuses to leave his ancestral mud house when an emergency evacuation drill reaches his doorstep. What begins as a routine exercise brings back memories of displacement, lost homes and a changing village. As Bapo and his wife Bhagi confront the authorities through a tense night, their home emerges as a powerful symbol of identity, dignity, memory and an enduring connection to the land.

WOODWORM (ROTO)

Director: Akhil Lotlikar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 22 minutes

Woodworm (Roto) follows a determined clinic receptionist navigating a chaotic family situation as she tries to help her sister win a school competition. But as she struggles to balance family responsibilities and her sister's aspirations, an unforeseen danger begins to close in on her.

CHEERS!

Director: Anurag Verdekar | Language: Konkani | Duration: 19 minutes

Bored with their routine, two young boys board a random bus and embark on an aimless journey into the unfamiliar world of adults. Their adventure takes them to an old fort, across a river ferry and eventually to a secluded waterfall, where they impulsively decide to buy their first alcoholic drink. Their unsuccessful attempt to conceal their age exposes their vulnerability and brings home the realisation that the adult world is far more complicated than they imagined. Cheers! captures the curiosity, innocence and uncertainties of growing up, as the boys return home with a subtly changed perspective on the world.

MEDIUM PIECE

Director: Jay Amonkar | Language: Marathi | Duration: 23 minutes

A chicken escaping from a butcher's shop sets off an unusual chain of events in this bittersweet comedy-drama set in a rural village. Blamed for repeatedly losing chickens, the butcher comes up with an unconventional solution: installing a television to keep the birds entertained. However, he soon becomes addicted to the television himself, affecting his behaviour, responsibilities and relationship with his wife. When the television malfunctions and all the chickens escape, the butcher faces punishment from his employer and rejection at home. Through this quirky tale of a man caught between captivity and the desire for escape, Medium Piece explores loneliness, modern distractions and the unintended consequences of seeking an escape from everyday life.

HEALTH CENTRE

Director: Anup Sardesai | Language: Konkani | Duration: 2 hours 7 minutes

Set in a chaotic government health centre, Health Centre follows Dr. Sridhar Kamat, its Chief Medical Officer, as he confronts a moral crisis involving a young rape victim, Surbhi, who is pressured by corrupt politicians and police to withdraw her complaint against an influential accused, Ajay. Amid a workers' strike, he also struggles to provide care for a comatose patient whose daughter, Manisha, depends on the hospital's limited resources. When Surbhi finally succumbs to intimidation, Dr. Kamat takes justice into his own hands by secretly administering a fatal injection to Ajay before resigning in protest, while ensuring the comatose patient remains on life support. Ten years later, his legacy resurfaces when his son Raj joins a new facility and encounters a senior doctor who is revealed to be Surbhi.

Goa has been the permanent home of the International Film Festival of India since 2004, welcoming filmmakers, cinema enthusiasts and creative voices from across the world every November. The 57th edition, being held from November 20 to 28, 2026, under the theme ‘Stories Without Borders’, celebrates cinema's ability to transcend geographical, linguistic and cultural boundaries, connecting audiences through shared human experiences.

The Goan film selection is a fitting reflection of this spirit. Rooted in the everyday lives, cultural traditions and social realities of Goa, these twelve films demonstrate how stories that emerge from a particular place can speak to audiences far beyond it.

Whether exploring family relationships, questions of identity, childhood, loneliness or the complexities of social life, they offer perspectives shaped by local experiences but connected by universal emotions.

By bringing Konkani and Marathi cinema to an international platform, the 57th edition of IFFI creates an opportunity for these voices to travel beyond their immediate cultural and linguistic contexts, allowing audiences from across the world to discover Goa not just as a destination, but through the lives, memories and stories of its people. In the spirit of the theme of this year’s festival ‘Stories Without Borders’, the selection reminds us that while stories may begin locally, their ability to move, connect and resonate knows no boundaries.

Read IFFILOID here: https://www.pib.gov.in/iffi/57/iffiLoid.aspx?yr=2026&lang=1&reg=48

 

* * *

PIB IFFI Team | Rajith Chandran/ Rabee Hashmi/ Lekshmi Priya S S/ Bibin S Nath/ Darshana Rane | IFFI 57 - 041

item.title: NISD Successfully Concludes First Batch of Three-Month Certificate Course on Drug De-addiction, Counselling Skills, Treatment and Rehabilitation (2026–27)
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment NISD Successfully Concludes First Batch of Three-Month Certificate Course on Drug De-addiction, Counselling Skills, Treatment and Rehabilitation (2026–27) 51 Participants Successfully Complete Training Programme Combining Classroom Learning and Practical Field Exposure Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi The National Centre for Drug Abuse Prevention (NCDAP), under the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, successfully concluded the…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
NISD Successfully Concludes First Batch of Three-Month Certificate Course on Drug De-addiction, Counselling Skills, Treatment and Rehabilitation (2026–27)
51 Participants Successfully Complete Training Programme Combining Classroom Learning and Practical Field Exposure
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 7:20PM by PIB Delhi

The National Centre for Drug Abuse Prevention (NCDAP), under the National Institute of Social Defence (NISD), Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, successfully concluded the first batch of the Three-Month Certificate Course on Drug De-addiction, Counselling Skills, Treatment and Rehabilitation for the academic year 2026–27.

A total of 51 participants successfully completed the training programme combining classroom learning and practical field exposure.

A Senior Official in the Ministry said the Course commenced in the first week of August 2026, is designed to equip participants with essential knowledge, practical skills and professional competencies in the areas of drug de-addiction, treatment, counselling and rehabilitation, strengthening their capacity to contribute to the prevention and treatment of substance use disorders.

He said the programme included two months of intensive theoretical classroom sessions at NISD, delivered by eminent subject experts from the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), Delhi University and other reputed institutions.

The classroom-based academic component was complemented by five weeks of practical field exposure at the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, and de-addiction centres functioning under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, the Official said.

 

The Official said the final examination for the course was conducted on November 17, 2026, followed by the valedictory session and certificate distribution ceremony on November 20, 2026, at NISD, in the National Capital here.

Through this initiative, NISD aims to develop a pool of trained and skilled professionals equipped to contribute effectively to the national response to substance use disorders, he said.

The Official noted the programme seeks to strengthen the availability and delivery of quality de-addiction, counselling, treatment and rehabilitation services across the country, in support of the Government’s efforts towards building a drug-free society.

Director, NISD, Shri Gaurav Singh Rajawat awarded the certificates to the successful participants.

PR-238-TAR/KV/GA/RK

item.content:encoded:
AYUSH
9th Naturopathy Day Celebrated with Eco-Friendly and Plastic-Free Arrangements at Nagamangala
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:50PM by PIB Delhi

The 9th Naturopathy Day national-level celebration at the Central Research Institute of Yoga and Naturopathy (CRIYN), Nagamangala, Karnataka, on 18 November 2026, was organised with a strong emphasis on environmental sustainability and eco-friendly practices, in keeping with the theme ‘Prakritik Chikitsa, Swasth Bharat’.

The programme adopted a plastic-free approach, with minimal use of banners and no plastic materials in decorations, event mementos or participant kits. Food was served in reusable steel plates and on banana leaves, avoiding disposable plastic and promoting traditional, environmentally responsible practices.

The arrangements were designed to minimise waste and encourage the use of reusable and natural alternatives. By reducing unnecessary event materials and avoiding single-use plastic, the celebration demonstrated how large-scale public outreach programmes can be conducted while remaining mindful of their environmental footprint.

Through these measures, the Ministry of Ayush reaffirmed the importance of incorporating sustainable practices into public programmes and celebrations, demonstrating that environmental responsibility can be an integral part of promoting a healthier and more sustainable India.

***

SR/AK/SG

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Tourism
item.description: Ministry of Tourism Ministry of Tourism holds Stakeholder Consultation on MICE and Wedding Tourism Consultation focuses on strengthening the MICE and Wedding Tourism ecosystem through closer Government–industry collaboration India improves its global ranking in international association meetings from 37th in 2022 to 26th in 2025 Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Tourism organised a Stakeholder Consultation on MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions) and Wedding Tourism in New Delhi on 19 November 2026, under…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Tourism
Ministry of Tourism holds Stakeholder Consultation on MICE and Wedding Tourism
Consultation focuses on strengthening the MICE and Wedding Tourism ecosystem through closer Government–industry collaboration
India improves its global ranking in international association meetings from 37th in 2022 to 26th in 2025
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Tourism organised a Stakeholder Consultation on MICE (Meetings, Incentives, Conferences and Exhibitions) and Wedding Tourism in New Delhi on 19 November 2026, under the chairmanship of Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Tourism. The consultation brought together representatives of leading industry associations, convention and exhibition venues and industry bodies to review progress in the two sectors and seek industry inputs to position India as a leading global destination for business events and weddings.

The consultation witnessed participation from the Indian Exhibition Industry Association (IEIA), Event and Entertainment Management Association (EEMA), Indian Weddings Industry Association (IWIA), Jio World Convention Centre (JWCC), India Trade Promotion Organisation (ITPO), India Convention Promotion Bureau (ICPB), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI) and Confederation of Indian Industry (CII).

Addressing the participants, Shri Bhuvnesh Kumar, highlighted the potential of the MICE sector and emphasised the need for a structured approach, closer coordination and regular engagement between the Government and industry.

Shri Suman Billa, Additional Secretary and Director General (Tourism), underscored the important role of sectoral bodies in strengthening the MICE and Wedding Tourism ecosystem.

The deliberations focused on strengthening the overall MICE and Wedding Tourism ecosystem, recognising professional service providers, improving sectoral data and promoting Indian destinations in collaboration with States and Union Territories.

Under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Government is working to position India as a leading global MICE destination. India’s MICE market, valued at USD 49.4 billion in 2024, is projected to reach USD 103.7 billion by 2030. The Ministry of Tourism promotes India as a MICE destination through the ‘Meet in India’ sub-brand under the ‘Incredible India’ campaign.

India has also recorded progress in the international association meetings segment. According to the International Congress and Convention Association (ICCA), India’s global ranking improved from 37th in 2022 to 26th in 2025, while the country ranked 6th in the Asia-Pacific region. In 2025, New Delhi was the highest-ranked Indian city, followed jointly by Bengaluru and Mumbai.

***

RK

By enabling small business owners to expand their operations, improve infrastructure and enhance production capacity,…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Empowering Women Entrepreneurship Through Financial Assistance under NSFDC
Journey Of Lakshmi Devi’s Small Paper Bag Manufacturing Unit To A Growing Enterprise In Salem, Tamil Nadu
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:31PM by PIB Delhi

Access to timely financial assistance and institutional support plays a significant role in strengthening entrepreneurship among women from Scheduled Caste communities. By enabling small business owners to expand their operations, improve infrastructure and enhance production capacity, financial assistance contributes to sustainable livelihoods, economic independence and inclusive growth.

A Journey of Enterprise and Determination

Smt. Lakshmi Devi (name changed), a 55-year-old woman entrepreneur belonging to the Scheduled Caste community from Salem district in Tamil Nadu, has demonstrated remarkable determination in building and sustaining her paper bag manufacturing enterprise.

Coming from an agricultural background, she ventured into paper bag manufacturing and has been successfully operating her unit for more than ten years. Through consistent efforts, she established a presence in the local market, supplying paper bags to customers and businesses in and around Salem.

Despite her experience and commitment, limited financial resources constrained the expansion of her enterprise. Inadequate manufacturing infrastructure and restricted production capacity affected her ability to meet growing market demand and increase her earnings. Her monthly income remained approximately ₹15,000, highlighting the need for additional financial support to strengthen her business.

Financial Assistance for Business Expansion

Recognising the opportunity to expand her enterprise, Smt. Lakshmi Devi approached a bank for financial assistance to improve her manufacturing infrastructure and increase production capacity.

On 11 October 2023, she was sanctioned a loan of ₹4 lakh under the MSME Loan Scheme, with support linked to the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC).

She effectively utilised the financial assistance to strengthen her paper bag manufacturing unit, improve its operational capacity and increase the availability of finished products.

The intervention enabled her to expand both wholesale and retail sales of paper bags in Salem and surrounding areas. The beneficiary also received support under the VISVAS scheme implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, as reported in the beneficiary information.

Strengthening Income and Economic Independence

The financial assistance brought a measurable improvement in the beneficiary's economic circumstances. With enhanced production capacity and improved market access, her monthly income increased from approximately ₹15,000 to ₹20,000, representing an additional earning of ₹5,000 per month.

This 33.3% increase in monthly income reflects the positive impact of need-based credit assistance in supporting small-scale women entrepreneurs.

Beyond the improvement in earnings, the intervention strengthened her confidence in managing and expanding her enterprise. Increased production and greater market participation have helped establish a stronger foundation for sustained business operations and financial self-reliance.

Promoting Inclusive and Sustainable Entrepreneurship

The journey of Smt. Lakshmi Devi illustrates how accessible institutional credit can help experienced women entrepreneurs overcome financial constraints and realise the growth potential of their enterprises.

Her experience highlights the importance of financial assistance facilitated through NSFDC in promoting entrepreneurship, strengthening livelihoods and enhancing economic opportunities among Scheduled Caste communities.

By supporting the expansion of micro and small enterprises, such initiatives contribute to women's economic empowerment, self-reliance and inclusive economic development.

The success story follows the narrative structure of the attached reference document, with a changed beneficiary name and no personal contact details.

The horizontal infographic includes the manufacturing-unit photograph with the beneficiary shown from behind to protect her identity, along with the key loan and income figures.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
Announcement of National Gopal Ratna Award 2026 winners -reg.
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:30PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, is promoting conservation and development of indigenous bovine breeds in a scientific manner. To fulfil this objective, “Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM)” was launched by the Department in December 2014.

2. As part of this initiative, the Department has instituted the National Gopal Ratna Award (NGRA) to recognize and encourage the contributions of stakeholders such as Milk producing farmers, dairy cooperative societies/MPC/FPOs and Artificial Insemination Technicians (AITs), engaged in the conservation, development and promotion of indigenous bovine breeds. This year also National Gopal Ratna Award is given for the following categories:

  1. Best Dairy farmer rearing indigenous cattle/buffalo breeds.
  2. Best Dairy Cooperative Society (DCS)/ Milk producer Company (MPC)/ Dairy Farmer Producer Organization (FPO).
  3. Best Artificial Insemination Technician (AIT).

3. There is special award for North Eastern Region (NER) and Himalayan States so as to encourage and boost the dairy development activities in these States/UTs.

4. NGRA 2026 will be conferred to winners for 1st, 2nd & 3rd ranks and a Special Award for North Eastern Region(NER)/Himalayan States in each category as mentioned above. NGRA 2026 consists of a Certificate of merit, a memento and monetary prize in first two categories i.e Best Dairy Farmer and Best DCS/FPO/MPCs as under:

    • Rs. 5,00,000/-(Rupee five lakh only) -1st rank
    • Rs. 3,00,000/- (Rupee three lakh only) -2nd rank
    • Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupee two lakh only) -3rd rank
    • Rs. 2,00,000/- (Rupee two lakh only) -Special Award for North Eastern Region (NER)/Himalayan States.

5. A Certificate of merit and a memento will be provided for Best Artificial Insemination Technician (AIT) category.

 

6. The applications were invited through the online application portal i.e. https://awards.gov.in developed by Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) during 10.08.2026 to 30.09.2026. A total of 1583 applications were received.

7. After following due procedure, the Department of Animal Husbandry is hereby declaring the winners of National Gopal Ratna Award 2026 in each category as under:

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Minority Affairs
Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s Message of Peace, Equality and Service Continues to Guide Humanity: Shri Kiren Rijiju
National Commission for Minorities (NCM) celebrates Guru Purab paying tribute to the teachings and legacy of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:13PM by PIB Delhi


National Commission for Minorities (NCM) celebrated Guru Purab with devotion and reverence, commemorating the Prakash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji and paying tribute to his timeless teachings of peace, harmony, equality and selfless service.

Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Minority Affairs, Shri Kiren Rijiju, paid homage to Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji and said his teaching’s remain profoundly relevant in contemporary society. Shri Rijiju said Guru Nanak Dev Ji gave humanity the eternal message of Ik Onkar — One God, and all human beings as His children. Through the three guiding principles of Naam Japo, Kirat Karo and Vand Chhakko, the Guru taught remembrance of God, honest labour, and sharing with others.

Referring to the tradition of  Shabad Kirtan, the Union Minister said Guru Nanak Dev Ji established it as a powerful medium for peace, spiritual awakening and harmony among people. Highlighting the institution of Langar, he underscored the Guru’s vision that no person should go hungry. Langar, he said, embodies equality, sharing and service to humanity — where all sit together in one pangat, without distinction of caste, status or creed.

The Union Minister also referred to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s visit to Gurdwara Khalsa Diwan in Manila, Philippines, highlighting the Government’s commitment to strengthening India’s spiritual and cultural connections across the world. He reiterated that the Government’s guiding philosophy of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas’ reflects the spirit of inclusivity and equal opportunities for all.

Speaking about the spirit of sacrifice deeply embedded in Sikh history and tradition, the Union Minister said he was deeply moved by the extraordinary courage and sacrifices of the Sahibzadas. He noted that their lives continue to inspire generations with lessons of courage, faith and unwavering commitment to principles.


The programme was attended by Chairman, National Commission for Minorities, Shri Harjit Singh Grewal; Vice-Chairperson Smt. S. Munawari Begum; Members Shri Berjis Desai, Shri Glenn D. Ticlo and Dr. Yangchan Dolma.

Shri Suchindra Mishra, Secretary, NCM; Dr. Atya Nand, Joint Secretary, NCM; and Joint Secretaries from the Ministry of Minority Affairs were also present. Senior officers and staff members of the National Commission for Minorities and the Ministry of Minority Affairs also attended the programme. The celebration concluded with Langar, reaffirming the timeless Sikh tradition of equality, community service and sharing, as envisioned by Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji.

*****

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation
Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP) to be held in Mumbai on 23rd November 2026
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:07PM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) is organising a “Data Users Conference on the New Series of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Index of Industrial Production (IIP)” on 23rd November 2026 in Mumbai. The conference follows the launch of the new series of all three indicators during the year 2026 and aims to familiarise data users with the methodological changes, data sources used and key improvements.

  • The new series of National Accounts with base year 2022-23 was released on 27th February 2026, followed by updation in August 2026 on incorporation of updated series of IIP and Producer Price Index (PPI). The new series has improved measurement of the private corporate and unincorporated sectors through greater use of MCA data, Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE), and the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) data etc. Adoption of double deflation in manufacturing sector in addition to agriculture sector, integration of Supply and Use Tables in annual estimates and use of Proportional Denton method for benchmarking and that of GST data for quarterly estimates are the other key features.
  • The new CPI series with base year 2024 was released on 12th February 2026. It is based on the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2023-24 and adopts the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018. The basket has been expanded to 358 items, including 50 services, with prices collected from 1,465 rural and 1,395 urban markets across 434 towns, besides 12 online markets. Rural house rent has been included for the first time, and administrative and e-commerce data are used for items such as fuel, air fares, telecom charges and OTT services.
  • The new IIP series with base year 2022-23, aligned with the base year of GDP, WPI and PPI, was released on 1st June 2026. Its coverage has been expanded to include minor and rare earth minerals, gas supply, and a new sector of water supply, sewerage and waste management. The series has an updated item basket and factory panel, a provision for factory substitution, and greater use of the Output Producer Price Index (OPPI) for deflating production reported in value terms.

The conference will bring together representatives of RBI, SEBI, economists, researchers, experts from financial institutions and the banking sector, academia, subject-matter specialists, users of official statistics and senior officials from the Central Government.

The inaugural session will feature addresses by Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, MoSPI; Dr. Poonam Gupta, Deputy Governor, RBI; Shri Deepak Parekh, Former Chairman, HDFC and Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics). It will be followed by three technical sessions on the new series of GDP, CPI and IIP, with presentations by MoSPI and RBI and open house discussions. A booklet containing the brief concept notes on the revised series of these indices will also be shared with the participants.

The conference will provide valuable opportunity to both users and official data compilers to directly discuss the changes, its interpretation and implications.

The conference aims to promote better understanding and effective use of official statistics and to strengthen engagement between MoSPI and the user community.

The Ministry welcomes active participation and insights of all stakeholders in this important consultative exercise.

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Defence
DELIVERY OF DSC A21 (YARD 326) OF DIVING SUPPORT CRAFT (DSC) PROJECT TO THE INDIAN NAVY
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi

‘DSC A21’ of the Diving Support Craft (DSC) project, was delivered to the Indian Navy on 20 Nov 2026 at Naval Dockyard, Mumbai. The vessel has been indigenously designed and constructed by M/s Titagarh Rail Systems Limited (TRSL), Kolkata.

Featuring a catamaran-hull form, DSC A21 is equipped with state-of-the-art diving equipment. The ship’s superior design offers enhanced stability, enlarged deck area and improved sea-keeping characteristics, which makes it suitable for its specialist role.

The ship is indigenously designed and built under relevant Naval Rules and Regulations of Indian Register of Shipping (IRS), whose hydrodynamic analysis/ model testing during design stage was undertaken by Naval Science and Technological Laboratory (NSTL), Visakhapatnam. With induction of these ships, the Indian Navy’s capabilities in diving support, underwater inspection, salvage assistance and coastal operational deployment will be augmented.

DSC A21 is a proud flag bearer of Make in India initiative of Government of India (GoI)/ Ministry of Defence (MoD).

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Finance

item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Finance
NLMC revises payment structure for e-auction of HIL land at Zakhira, New Delhi
Corrigendum no. 3 introduces five-instalment payment schedule extending up to 240 days
Agreement to Sell to be executed upon payment of 10% of total sale consideration, excluding EMD
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 6:00PM by PIB Delhi

The National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC), under the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, has issued Corrigendum No. 3 to the Request for Proposal (RFP) for the e-auction of a prime 5.119-acre freehold land parcel belonging to HIL (India) Limited, located at Najafgarh Industrial Area, Rohtak Road, Shivaji Marg, Zakhira, New Delhi.

The property, measuring approximately 20,722.93 square metres, carries a reserve price of ₹829.69 crore and is being offered through a transparent and competitive e-tender-cum-e-auction process.

The latest Corrigendum introduces a revised payment structure and provisions relating to the execution of the Agreement to Sell, providing a structured payment framework for the successful bidder.

 

Revised payment structure

Under the revised provisions, the successful bidder will be required to pay the total sale consideration in five instalments over a period extending up to 240 days from the date of issuance of the Letter of Acceptance (LoA) by HIL.

Instalment

Payment timeline

Amount payable

First

T + 10 days

10%

Second

T + 60 days

30%

Third

T + 120 days

20%

Fourth

T + 180 days

20%

Fifth

T + 240 days

20% (after eligible EMD adjustment)

 

T represents the date of issuance of the Letter of Acceptance, including the date of issuance.

The revised schedule provides a phased payment mechanism with clearly defined timelines for completion of the transaction.

 

Execution of Agreement to Sell

Under the revised terms, the Agreement to Sell between HIL and the successful bidder shall be executed upon receipt of 10% of the total sale consideration, excluding the Earnest Money Deposit (EMD), subject to fulfilment of the applicable requirements under the RFP.

Execution of the Agreement to Sell shall not confer ownership, title, interest or possession rights over the property. The successful bidder shall remain obligated to complete the balance payments within the stipulated timelines.

 

Payment default and grace period

The Corrigendum also clarifies provisions governing payment defaults.

In the event of failure by the successful bidder to make payment of the first and second instalments within their respective stipulated timelines, the LoA shall be liable to cancellation and the amount paid by the successful bidder up to that date, including EMD, shall be liable to forfeiture in accordance with the RFP.

For the third, fourth and fifth instalments, a grace period of 30 days may be considered, subject to payment of simple interest at 12% per annum for the period of delay and other applicable conditions.

The Corrigendum also specifies the applicable payment obligations for H2 and H3 bidders in the event of default by a higher-ranked bidder, without extending the original payment schedule.

 

Revised key dates for HIL e-auction

As per Corrigendum No. 2, the revised schedule is as follows:

 

Particulars

Revised date and time

Last date for registration, technical bid submission and EMD/Bank Guarantee

30 November 2026, 4:00 PM

Opening of technical bids

1 December 2026, 4:00 PM

Declaration of technically qualified bidders

7 December 2026, 4:00 PM

Mock e-auction

10 December 2026, 11:00 AM – 2:00 PM

E-auction

14 December 2026, 11:00 AM – 2:00 PM

 

Registration and participation

Interested investors and eligible bidders may access the RFP, Corrigendum Nos. 1, 2 and 3, property details, eligibility criteria and other relevant documents through the designated e-auction portal:

E-auction Portal: https://nlmc.enivida.com

NLMC Website: https://nlmc.dpe.gov.in

Prospective bidders are advised to carefully review the revised terms and conditions and complete registration, technical bid submission and EMD/Bank Guarantee formalities by 30 November 2026, 4:00 PM.

 

Advancing transparent asset monetisation

The revised provisions reflect NLMC's continued efforts to facilitate structured, transparent and competitive monetisation of surplus public-sector assets.

The HIL land e-auction represents an important initiative in unlocking the economic potential of strategically located public-sector land and encouraging wider investor participation through a technology-driven auction process.

All other terms and conditions of the original RFP dated 8 October 2026 and earlier Corrigenda, unless specifically modified, shall remain unchanged.

 

About NLMC

National Land Monetization Corporation (NLMC) is a wholly owned Government of India company under the administrative control of the Department of Public Enterprises, Ministry of Finance. NLMC facilitates the monetisation of surplus land and building assets of Central Public Sector Enterprises (CPSEs) and other Government entities through transparent, competitive and market-driven processes.

item.title: India Takes a Historic Leap Towards Self-Reliance: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Dedicates Country’s First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine to the Nation in Bhopal
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
item.description: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare India Takes a Historic Leap Towards Self-Reliance: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Dedicates Country’s First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine to the Nation in Bhopal A befitting response to those who malign India abroad: Shri Chouhan says the world must see the new, self-reliant and developed India Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Announces ₹300-Crore State-of-the-Art Animal Disease Research Laboratory in Bhopal Indigenous Bird Flu Vaccine to Protect Poultry Farmers from Disease Outbreaks at Just ₹1-2 per Dose: Shri Chouhan Shri Chouhan Salutes…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare
India Takes a Historic Leap Towards Self-Reliance: Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Dedicates Country’s First Indigenous H5N1 Bird Flu Vaccine to the Nation in Bhopal
A befitting response to those who malign India abroad: Shri Chouhan says the world must see the new, self-reliant and developed India
Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Announces ₹300-Crore State-of-the-Art Animal Disease Research Laboratory in Bhopal
Indigenous Bird Flu Vaccine to Protect Poultry Farmers from Disease Outbreaks at Just ₹1-2 per Dose: Shri Chouhan
Shri Chouhan Salutes Scientists for Months of Research and Unprecedented Commitment in Developing Indigenous Bird Flu Vaccine
Shri Chouhan Highlights India's Progress in Animal Disease Control, Credits National Vaccination Drive for Major Gains
Shri Chouhan Hits Back at Critics Questioning India's Institutions and Scientific Achievements, Says Country's Progress Speaks for Itself
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

In a major milestone for India's scientific capabilities and the country's drive towards self-reliance, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today dedicated India's first indigenous chicken vaccine against Avian Influenza (H5N1), commonly known as bird flu, to the nation at a program in Bhopal. On the occasion, the Union Minister announced the establishment of a new state-of-the-art laboratory in Bhopal at an estimated cost of ₹300 crore. He also took a dig at opposition leaders for questioning India's constitutional institutions and the capabilities of its scientists while speaking abroad. Priced at an affordable ₹1-2 per dose, the vaccine is the world's first vaccine against this particular variant of bird flu. It is expected to strengthen disease prevention in the poultry sector, protect the livelihoods of millions of poultry farmers and help reduce the enormous economic losses caused by animal diseases.

 

 

Those who malign India abroad must see the new, self-reliant India

 

Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan took aim at opposition leaders who, he said, seek to discredit the country on international platforms. He said that those who go abroad and malign their own country must take note of India's achievements and its growing scientific capabilities. He said that people who hold constitutional positions but question the Constitution abroad, undermine constitutional institutions and cast doubts on the contribution of India's armed forces, scientists and hardworking citizens must look at the changing India of today. Shri Chouhan recalled that Indian scientists had earlier surprised the world by developing two indigenous COVID-19 vaccines in just nine months through a task force constituted under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. The development of the country's first indigenous bird flu vaccine is another demonstration of India's scientific strength and self-reliance, he added.

 

₹300-crore state-of-the-art laboratory to come up in Bhopal

 

Highlighting the achievements of the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal, Shri Chouhan announced a new state-of-the-art laboratory worth ₹300 crore for the city. He said that the Bhopal-based institute had emerged as a symbol of India's scientific excellence. The Minister also explained why the vaccine was dedicated to the nation in Bhopal rather than Delhi. Although there had initially been a proposal to launch the vaccine from Delhi, he decided that the occasion should take place in Bhopal, among the scientists who had worked day and night to develop it and in the presence of the people of the city. The achievement belonged to these scientists, and it was important to recognise their contribution at the very place where the vaccine had been developed, he said.

 

Livestock are 'moving ATMs' for farmers; indigenous vaccines to help prevent annual losses of ₹56,000 crore

 

Describing animal husbandry and poultry as vital pillars of the rural economy, Shri Chouhan said that livestock are 'moving ATMs' for farmers, providing a regular source of monthly income alongside agriculture. He highlighted that animal husbandry contributes 14 per cent to India's GDP, while the poultry sector accounts for another 1 per cent. He also underlined the substantial economic burden caused by major animal diseases. According to the figures shared by the Minister, Foot and Mouth Disease causes average annual losses of ₹22,000 crore, Lumpy Skin Disease results in losses of ₹20,000 crore, Brucellosis accounts for ₹9,212 crore and Peste des Petits Ruminants, a disease affecting sheep and goats, causes losses of ₹4,683 crore. Together, these diseases have caused losses of approximately ₹56,000 crore to the country and its farmers. Indigenous vaccines are playing a crucial role in protecting livestock, safeguarding farmers' incomes and reducing this economic burden, he said.

 

 

Vaccine priced at just ₹1-2 per dose; India has witnessed over 500 bird flu outbreaks since 2006

 

Shri Chouhan recalled that India's first bird flu outbreak was reported in 2006 in Navapur, Maharashtra, resulting in the death of 10 lakh chickens. To contain the infection, lakhs of additional birds had to be culled and buried. Subsequently, around 9 lakh chickens died in 2021, while another 2 lakh died this year. Since 2006, India has witnessed more than 500 bird flu outbreaks, causing significant damage to the poultry industry. The disease also poses a risk of transmission to mammals and humans, making effective prevention and control measures particularly important. The new indigenous vaccine has been priced at just ₹1-2 per dose to ensure that even small poultry farmers can afford it. Its low cost will make preventive vaccination more accessible and help protect the livelihoods of poultry farmers across the country, the Minister said.

 

National vaccination drive delivering decisive results against animal diseases

 

Shri Chouhan highlighted the government's sustained efforts to control major animal diseases through vaccination. He said Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi launched the National Animal Disease Control Program from Mathura, the land of Lord Krishna, to strengthen disease prevention and protect livestock. Under the program, 147 crore 16 lakh free vaccine doses have so far been administered against Foot and Mouth Disease. Brucellosis has also been brought under control, he said. Recalling the outbreak of Lumpy Skin Disease in 2022, Shri Chouhan said that 32 lakh 80 thousand animals were infected and 1 lakh 86 thousand animals lost their lives. Scientists at Hisar and Izatnagar subsequently developed the 'Lumpi-ProVacInd' vaccine to combat the disease. He also commended the achievements of ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, which has previously developed indigenous vaccines for Gumboro disease, Brucella abortus S-19 Delta, Classical Swine Fever and African Swine Fever. The latest H5N1 vaccine adds another significant achievement to the institute's contribution to India's animal health research.

 

Scientists worked through holidays and followed stringent biosafety protocols to develop the vaccine

 

Paying tribute to the scientists behind the vaccine, Shri Chouhan described them as the real heroes of this achievement and praised their extraordinary commitment and dedication. The research team comprised Dr. S. Nagarajan, Dr. Manoj Kumar, Dr. C. Tosh, Dr. H. V. Murugkar, Dr. Aniket Sanyal, Dr. Senthil Kumar D., Dr. Naveen Kumar and Dr. Yogisharadhya R. The Minister shared that the scientists worked continuously for months, foregoing their Saturday and Sunday holidays to complete the research. Their work also required strict adherence to demanding biosafety protocols. As part of these protocols, they had to undergo sanitisation procedures before and after leaving the laboratory, use 120 litres of water daily for bathing and refrain from keeping any pets at home throughout the research period. Shri Chouhan saluted their commitment, describing their dedication as being akin to the discipline and sacrifice of soldiers serving the nation. He said that the achievement reflected the extraordinary perseverance of India's scientific community.

The program was attended by Madhya Pradesh Minister for Youth Welfare, Sports and Cooperation Shri Vishwas Sarang; Bhopal MP Shri Alok Sharma; Khategaon MLA Shri Ashish Sharma; Bhopal Mayor Smt. Malti Rai; senior public representatives Shri Rakesh Sharma, Shri Naresh Mewada, Shri Rakesh Jadon, Shri Rajesh Chouksey and Ms. Chhaya, along with councillors. ICAR Director General Dr. M. L. Jat, NIHSAD Director Dr. Aniket Sanyal, scientists and a large number of distinguished guests were also present.

Mande, President of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), has been appointed by the United Nations Secretary-General to the United Nations Group of Ten High-level Representatives of Civil Society, Private Sector and Scientific Community to Promote Science, Technology and Innovation for the Sustainable…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Science & Technology
INSA President Professor Shekhar C. Mande Appointed to UN’s 10-Member Group on Science, Technology and Innovation for Sustainable Development Goals
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:42PM by PIB Delhi

Professor Shekhar C. Mande, President of the Indian National Science Academy (INSA), has been appointed by the United Nations Secretary-General to the United Nations Group of Ten High-level Representatives of Civil Society, Private Sector and Scientific Community to Promote Science, Technology and Innovation for the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for the 2026–2028 term.

Professor Mande joins nine other eminent experts from across the world in the High-Level Expert Group, which includes Ms. Marian Dorcas Quain (Ghana) and Mr. Giorgio Rossi (Italy) as Co-Chairs, along with Mr. Magnus Andersson (Sweden), Ms. Mônica Tejo Cavalcanti (Brazil), Ms. Evgeniya Dmitrieva (Russian Federation), Ms. Motoko Kotani (Japan), Mr. Jin Li (China), Mr. Madin Maseeh (Maldives), and Ms. Rita Orji (Nigeria). The members represent diverse scientific disciplines and sectors and will bring their collective expertise to advancing global efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals under the UN's 2030 Agenda.

The 10-Member Group is an integral part of the United Nations Technology Facilitation Mechanism (TFM), which promotes collaboration and partnerships to harness science, technology and innovation for sustainable development. The Group works closely with the UN Inter-agency Task Team on Science, Technology and Innovation for the SDGs (IATT), providing guidance and recommendations on emerging scientific and technological developments and their implications for sustainable development.

The Group's mandate includes contributing to the UN Science, Technology and Innovation Forum, providing recommendations on technology solutions and partnerships, and advising on areas such as emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, digitalisation, biotechnology, quantum technologies, capacity building, social inclusion and STI roadmaps for the SDGs.

Professor Mande is a distinguished structural and computational biologist and scientific administrator. He is currently President of INSA and a Distinguished Professor at the Bioinformatics Centre, Savitribai Phule Pune University, as well as a JC Bose Fellow at the National Centre for Cell Science (NCCS), Pune. Professor Mande also serves as the National President of Vijnana Bharati, a national science movement dedicated to promoting scientific awareness in India. He has previously served as Director General of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and Secretary, Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR), Government of India.

His appointment reflects the growing recognition of Indian scientific expertise and its contribution to international dialogue on science, technology and innovation for addressing global development challenges.

The Indian National Science Academy congratulates Professor Shekhar C. Mande on this significant international appointment and looks forward to his contributions towards strengthening the role of science, technology and innovation in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals.

item.dc:creator: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
item.description: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal confers SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh among the leading States recognised for their performance in implementing the Scheme Assam, Sikkim , Mizoram , Tripura awarded among North-Eastern and Hilly States Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:37PM by PIB…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs
Union Minister Shri Manohar Lal confers SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026
Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh among the leading States recognised for their performance in implementing the Scheme
Assam, Sikkim , Mizoram , Tripura awarded among North-Eastern and Hilly States
Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:37PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, organised the SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 on 20 November 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The awards were conferred by Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, as Guest of Honour, to recognise the outstanding contributions of States/UTs, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Lending Institutions and partner organisations in strengthening street vendors’ livelihoods and advancing financial inclusion, digital adoption and social security under the PM SVANidhi Scheme.

Featuring 52 awards and 5 special recognitions, the awards celebrated excellence across States, cities, banks and other stakeholders. Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh were among the leading States recognised for their performance in implementing the Scheme and expanding its outreach. Cities and ULBs were also recognised for their contribution to effective grassroots implementation, improved outreach and digital adoption.

 

Among the Lending Institutions, State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, Punjab National Bank and Union Bank were recognised for their lending performance and contribution towards extending accessible formal credit to street vendors.

Since its launch in June 2020, PM SVANidhi has enabled around 81 lakh street vendors to access over 1.21 crore loans amounting to approximately ₹20,000 crore. Following the restructuring of the Scheme in August 2025, around 22 lakh loans worth ₹6,294 crore were disbursed to 10.6 lakh new beneficiaries in the first year. The Scheme has also expanded access to formal credit through an UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card, offering eligible beneficiaries who have repaid their second loan tranche a credit limit of up to ₹30,000.

Under SVANidhi se Samriddhi, socio-economic profiling of over 52 lakh beneficiary families has been completed, resulting in more than 1.62 crore sanctions under eight Central Government welfare schemes. The Scheme is also strengthening the street vending ecosystem through initiatives such as the development of 50 Street Food Hubs and capacity-building programmes, including food safety and hygiene training.

The awards covered the Scheme's implementation ecosystem across 35 States/UTs, over 4,900 ULBs and more than 120 Lending Institutions. The assessment was based on category-specific Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), using data primarily from the PM SVANidhi and SVANidhi se Samriddhi portals. Performance following the Scheme's restructuring was assessed for the period from 1 September 2025 to 31 August 2026, while overall performance was evaluated from the Scheme's inception up to 31 August 2026.

The SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 recognise the collective contributions of stakeholders towards strengthening the street vending ecosystem and improving the livelihoods of street vendors. These efforts will further promote inclusive urban development and contribute towards realising the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

 

Key Highlights from Addresses

Shri Manohar Lal emphasised that the vision of Antyodaya, leading towards Viksit Bharat @2047, can be realised by ensuring that the benefits of PM SVANidhi reach every eligible street vendor. He highlighted that the Scheme enables street vendors to progress from small loans to higher bank credit and expand their businesses, thereby promoting livelihood opportunities, financial inclusion and social security.

The Minister underscored that the success of PM SVANidhi is driven by the collective efforts of the Central and State Governments, banks and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs). He noted that the SVANidhi Samman Awards recognise the contributions of States, cities, institutions and officials in translating the objectives of the Scheme into tangible outcomes at the grassroots level.

Describing street vendors as ‘Street Wonders’, Shri Manohar Lal acknowledged their entrepreneurial spirit, resilience and ability to transform small livelihood activities into successful enterprises.

Referring to the Scheme's song, “Har mehnatkash ka saath diya, PM SVANidhi ne samman diya”, the Minister highlighted how PM SVANidhi has extended support to hardworking street vendors while strengthening their dignity, recognition and respect in society.

 

MOS Shri Tokhan Sahu  Speech Highlights

Addressing the gathering, Minister of State Shri Tokhan Sahu emphasised that the transformation in the lives of the poor should be viewed through the collective impact of various Government welfare initiatives rather than through any single scheme. Referring to the World Bank’s October 2026 report, he highlighted that approximately 50 crore people in India have moved out of poverty, reflecting the impact of sustained and coordinated efforts towards inclusive development.

The Minister also highlighted Chhattisgarh’s achievement of receiving four awards, particularly appreciating the recognition of Dantewada and Bade Bacheli, erstwhile Naxal-affected areas. He noted that this achievement reflects the reach of the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi and the positive transformation taking place in regions progressing towards becoming Naxal-free.

item.title: Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’
item.dc:creator: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
item.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’ Calls For Whole-Of-Government Approach To Build An Inclusive, Accessible And Drug-Free India Centre And States Identify Time-Bound Action Points On Drug Demand Reduction, Scholarships, Early Intervention And Accessibility; Summit Reinforces Collective Commitment Towards Viksit Bharat @2047 Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi applauded the Ministry of Social Justice…
item.content:encoded:
Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment
Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Chairs Plenary Session of ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’
Calls For Whole-Of-Government Approach To Build An Inclusive, Accessible And Drug-Free India
Centre And States Identify Time-Bound Action Points On Drug Demand Reduction, Scholarships, Early Intervention And Accessibility; Summit Reinforces Collective Commitment Towards Viksit Bharat @2047
Posted On: 20 NOV 2026 5:31PM by PIB Delhi

Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi applauded the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for organizing the Departmental Summit and facilitating meaningful deliberations. The Prime Minister emphasized the importance of collective action and a ‘Whole of Government’ approach in achieving the objectives of social justice, social empowerment and a Nasha Mukt Bharat.

Addressing the plenary session of the two-day Departmental Summit titled ‘Samaveshi Niti Sankalp’, at the Sushma Swaraj Bhawan, in the National Capital here on Thursday, Shri Modi highlighted the transformative impact of the Government’s welfare initiatives, he observed that nearly 50 crore people lifted out of poverty have experienced genuine social empowerment.

Calling for the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan to be transformed into a nationwide Jan Andolan, the Prime Minister stressed that every citizen, family, educational institution and community must contribute to building a drug-free India.

Shri Modi encouraged schools to organize essay competitions and undertake awareness initiatives, while sensitizing parents to recognize early signs of substance abuse and addiction.

Emphasizing the importance of rehabilitation and social reintegration, the Prime Minister observed that the journeys of individuals who have successfully overcome substance dependence carry a powerful message of hope.

“These journeys carry the strongest message of hope. They show that recovery is possible and that a life free from drugs is a life of dignity,” he said.

The Prime Minister also urged farmers to shun illicit crop cultivation and called for coordinated efforts involving all Ministries, State Governments, district administrations and spiritual organizations to strengthen the national campaign against drug abuse.

Recognising the influence of spiritual leaders, the Prime Minister said that spiritual gurus and organisations have a vital role to play in the mission. Their guidance, he noted, can inspire millions to choose a life free from drugs.

On the empowerment of persons with disabilities, the Prime Minister highlighted the significance of the term ‘Divyang’, noting its contribution towards enhancing the dignity, respect and self-esteem of persons with disabilities.

Shri Modi encouraged its wider use and popularization to foster a positive outlook towards Divyangjan across society. He also emphasized the need to identify, nurture and recognize their inherent talents and abilities by providing appropriate opportunities and platforms for their participation and contribution.

The Prime Minister’s address reinforced the need for sustained cooperation between the Centre and States, institutional convergence and effective implementation of welfare programmes to ensure that the benefits of development reach every section of society.

The Summit was attended by Union Ministers for Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministers from 27 States and Union Territories, Secretaries of both Departments, Secretaries from 35 States and Union Territories, and senior officers of the Ministry and participating State/UT administrations, to deliberate on key priorities and strengthen collaborative efforts towards inclusive social development and empowerment.

Four thematic priorities deliberated at the Summit

The two-day Departmental Summit commenced on November 18, 2026, with the inaugural session addressed by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar. Context-setting remarks were delivered by the Secretaries of the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE) and the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD), outlining the policy priorities and implementation challenges relating to drug demand reduction, scholarships, early intervention and accessibility.

The first day featured four thematic deliberations focusing on Re-imagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction for Nasha Mukt Bharat; Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students; Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden; and Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat.

Four parallel breakout sessions provided a platform for Ministers and senior officials from States and Union Territories to exchange best practices, discuss implementation challenges and identify actionable measures with clearly defined timelines.

1. Re-imagining Prevention and Drug Demand Reduction for Nasha Mukt Bharat

The session, chaired by Dr. (Col.) Dhani Ram Shandil, Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Himachal Pradesh, and co-chaired by Shri Avinash Gehlot, Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment, Rajasthan, focused on transforming drug prevention and awareness efforts into a sustained Jan Andolan.

The key action points included observing the 10th of every month as Nasha Mukti Sankalp Diwas, beginning December 2026; making drug prevention a standing agenda item in every Gram Sabha and Municipal Ward; and establishing at least one de-addiction centre in every district by March 2029.

States shared several innovative initiatives, including Chandigarh’s VADA Clubs, Punjab’s SOORMA Ambassadors, Meghalaya’s DREAM Solace Home, Jammu and Kashmir’s 100 Days Campaign and Haryana’s STARS Rating for rehabilitation centres.

Dr. Shandil underscored the importance of structured and continuous interventions through families, schools and communities, observing that prevention is both sound public health policy and sound economics.

Shri Gehlot emphasised the need to move beyond government-led programmes towards community-driven participation.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma affirmed that the outcomes of the deliberations would inform the national action plan.

2. Accessible Scholarships, Empowered Students

Chaired by Shri Asim Arun, Minister in the Government of Uttar Pradesh, and co-chaired by Shri Kishan Kumar Bedi, Minister in the Government of Haryana, the session focused on developing an integrated, accessible and student-centric scholarship delivery ecosystem.

The deliberations emphasized simplification of application procedures, secure digital integration between the Centre and States, assisted application facilities, timely disbursement of scholarships and strengthened grievance redressal mechanisms. Suggestions relating to revision of income eligibility criteria and scholarship amounts were also discussed.

States highlighted successful initiatives, including common scholarship platforms in Odisha, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh; Andhra Pradesh’s One Stop Scholarship Portal; prior scrutiny of applications in Madhya Pradesh; and auto-approval mechanisms adopted by Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

The discussions underscored the importance of technology-enabled service delivery, intergovernmental coordination and transparent processes to ensure that eligible students receive scholarship assistance in a timely and hassle-free manner.

3. Early Intervention and Reduction of Disability Burden

The session, chaired by Dr. Shweta Gupta, Minister in the Government of Bihar, and co-chaired by Ms. Pi Lalrinpuii, Minister in the Government of Mizoram, focused on strengthening early identification, timely assessment and intervention for children with developmental delays and disabilities.

The key priorities included strengthening convergence among health, nutrition, education and disability-related services; expanding tele-rehabilitation and mobile outreach facilities; developing integrated digital tracking systems; and enhancing the availability of trained human resources.

West Bengal presented its SANSPARSH model, which facilitates community-level screening for Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) through a 20-point questionnaire.

Dr. Gupta highlighted that early identification and convergence of existing services are critical to reducing the burden of disability and ensuring that support reaches beneficiaries at the grassroots level.

Ms. Lalrinpuii emphasised the importance of parental awareness, continuous follow-up and shared responsibility among families, institutions and service providers.

4. Sugamya Bharat for Viksit Bharat

The fourth thematic session focused on mainstreaming universal accessibility and inclusive design in public infrastructure, transport systems and digital services from the planning stage itself. The discussions highlighted the need for regular accessibility audits, effective monitoring mechanisms and active participation of persons with disabilities in the design and evaluation of public facilities.

States showcased several good practices, including Kochi Metro and Water Metro in Kerala, with Indian Sign Language-trained staff and accessible amenities; accessibility upgrades at Chennai Egmore and suburban railway stations in Tamil Nadu, including Braille-enabled lifts, tactile pathways and induction loops; accessible tourist spaces in Goa; level-boarding Ahmedabad Janmarg buses in Gujarat; and mandatory barrier-free infrastructure in schools in Assam.

Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B. L. Verma emphasised that accessibility is not an additional facility but the foundation of equal opportunities and a life of dignity, particularly in the context of the national vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.

Goa Minister Shri Subhash Faldessai advocated incorporating accessibility at the design and planning stage rather than relying on retrofitting.

Assam highlighted proposals for a dedicated National Mission, district-level monitoring and appropriate penalties for non-compliance with accessibility requirements.

Knowledge-sharing and exhibition of best practices

During the full-house sessions, experts Dr. Varsha Gathoo (formerly AYJNISHD) and Prof. J. S. Thakur (PGIMER) presented global best practices from the US, Australia, Switzerland, Iceland, Thailand, and the African Union alongside national policies.

An exhibition at Sushma Swaraj Bhawan showcased schemes, initiatives, success stories, digital applications and portals of both Departments, providing participants with an opportunity to understand innovative interventions and effective models of service delivery.

Renewed commitment to inclusive and empowered India

The deliberations culminated in a renewed commitment to strengthen Centre-State cooperation, institutional convergence and time-bound implementation of the agreed action points.

The Summit provided an important platform for translating policy priorities into coordinated action, leveraging successful State-level practices and addressing implementation gaps through collective responsibility.

With a shared focus on drug demand reduction, equitable access to educational opportunities, early intervention for persons with disabilities and universal accessibility, ‘SAMAVESHI NITI SANKALP 2026’ reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to building an inclusive, empowered, accessible and drug-free India in keeping with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047.
